Today is a birthday unlike any other in my life. This birthday I’m a mum. Of TWO. I’m a mum of twins. It’s still pretty surreal to say. I feel like me still, there are just two new tenants in this house that are incredibly demanding 😅

It’s been a tough two weeks. The adjustment was a huge slap to the face, any parent knows one child is demanding - two has been insanely hard. My first few days in hospital weren’t great, even though I was flagged as Bipolar (hence an at risk patient) with staffing issues and an overfull labour ward, I didn’t get any help to breastfeed or any sleep for 3 days. I slipped through the cracks in there system and my mental health took a very dangerous dive. I’m on the mend and thankfully had an uptick when the good midwives got me back on track, and I’ve had extra help at home from my mum (thank you mummy 💖) and my mother-in-law. 

I will say the birth was amazing. A twin birth vaginally is rare, so rare I didn’t realise til I was at the hospital. Every midwife had a look of shock on her face or gave me a ‘fuck yeah go you!!!’ - even the physio was confused when she checked for my scar and saw it had ‘healed miraculously’ 🤣 I was like ‘I didn’t have a c-section’ and she responded with excited expletives ☺️
I cried my eyes out when the student midwife at my delivery came to visit me days later and shared that she had told my story in class - about how it reminded her why she wants to be a midwife. 

I feel so proud I stuck to my guns with my choice to not get bullied into a Caesar. 

(Second) Last but not least, my husband, @bradequate  there is a whole post I could write about you. Your strength and support and love is unparalleled. 🚫 Dying Right Here Is Strictly Prohibited 🚫

Remember what we grew up with? 
‘Cocaine thin’ models and Retouched & Airbrushed Cosmo and Dolly magazines? 

We didn’t even have technology to be in our face 24/7, and we STILL grew up with huge body image problems, eating disorders and ridiculous body standards. 

How do young people stand a chance with celebrities that can’t admit they’ve had work done? When there’s AI image filtering, FaceTune, face augmenting filters, clear skin filters, etc. distorting our interpretation of what we should look like? 

Social Media (primarily its ‘influencers’ - amongst other things) has contributed towards a toxic culture of being preoccupied with perceived defects and flaws contributing to an increase in cosmetic procedures to ‘fix’ these perceived flaws. 
These constant messages day-in day-out have a profound effect upon our youth. 

After battling some pretty heavy body image issues (what 00’s teen girl didn’t) I’m determined to have a positive effect on those who look up to me, and I hope you do too. 
 
Start by having easy conversations with your younger siblings, charges, or children.
Start by talking about yourself with a loving mindset. 
Start by following positive movements against beauty standards. 

I’ll start with this untouched photo of me, my fine lines, my zits and sunspots enjoying a Moana Icecream at Disneyworld. 

I will love you more for being you than you trying to be anyone else, I promise x

What I love about Bipolar ⬆️ ⬇️ 

Not all of Bipolar is bad, whilst both the mood cycles (Hypomania and Depression) can be hard to manage there are some positives to my condition. 

💖 When the hypomanic days work for me. I can channel my power into being insanely productive, I get all my overdue tasks done, I clean the house, I finish that ‘thing that needs doing’. It makes up for the days of depression when I can barely make a meal for myself. 

💖 How happy I can feel. The euphoria of almost feeling love-drunk without the actual drunk part. 🤪 How the sun feels on my skin, how beautiful the world is, how bright colours are, books become a magic adventure, movies are a thrilling escape, generally feeling a child-like wonder towards the world - I’ve been told the symptoms are similar to MDMA 😅

💖 Tied in with this is how deeply I can feel. It goes both ways, the depression can be so destructive but the love and empathy is so deeply connecting. I feel a deep love and connection to my family and friends, I feel another’s feelings as if they are my own, I cry for them, I laugh with them, but I can also deeply support another person with my level of emotional understanding. 💓

💖 The creativity I have. My mind goes wild with ideas. I want to cross-stitch, build a miniature model, do pottery, paint, draw, make something with my hands. I just itch to do something else that isn’t passive like watching TV, lately it’s been Rhine-stoning my Burly Costumes! 💎 

💖 I can help other babes with Bipolar. I have a passion and a drive to educate and help others deal with their own or a loved ones Bipolar.

See, It’s been a tough week as I’ve been in the midst of a Mixed Episode. 

A mixed episode in Bipolar is when you experience both Depression and Hypomania (or mania for BP1) at the same time. 

Symptoms can include:

-feeling a mixture of elevated and low moods
-doing pleasurable activities but still having depressive symptoms
-experiencing low mood with rapid speech
-experiencing elevated mood with suicidal ideation
-experiencing severely disturbed sleep
-having a severe disruption of appetite

Amongst my peers we call this time ‘tired but wired’. 

In my own experience I’ve felt my heart racing, but I’m tired AF. 
I have trouble falling to sleep but then I sleep 9+ hrs. 
I experience Anhedonia. An inability to experience pleasure from activities I usually find enjoyable. 
Additionally my social battery is incredibly low. 
I have severe generalised anxiety and intrusive and/or ruminating thoughts. 
I have trouble articulating myself, but also stumble through a giant overshare. 
I get easily distracted and confused. 
I get very easily overwhelmed and cry a lot over the (depressed) pain I’m in. 

The best I can do in this situation is to be aware of my mood and do my best to avoid triggering or stimulating activities. I primarily distract myself with low effort activities and tasks. 

I limit my social media interactions and try to organise a few fulfilling but low effort social activities. 

Mainly I’ve been crawled up with a book and chocolate ✨ 

It will pass and I’ll return to my normal mood cycles, so I’ve just got to ride it out.

But in the meantime, I’m practicing my gratefulness. I found a profound moment of peace in this moment and I’m revisiting it as often as possible to soothe my nervous system. 

Peace ✌🏻 Tahlia

It feels like a new chapter. 
A year ago, my mental health/bipolar was at its absolute worst. 
I felt untethered, and overwhelmed and purposeless. I felt unloved and worthless.
I felt like a burden. 

I had a very severe mental breakdown. I lost a lot of people who I thought were close to me. I found some people who took me seriously and supported my mental health and recovery. 
It took the last 6 months of getting me onto the right meds and for the side effects to wear off. 
It took 9 months to get into a hospital program to learn the skills to support myself. (And 3 months for the waiting period!)
It took a year to believe I’m worth it and I deserve happiness. 
Finding my new therapist feels like the final piece of the puzzle.
Finding a human who wants to be apart of my support team, who wants to see
me succeed, and in her words ‘cultivate a full and meaningful life’ 

Bipolar will always be with me but it won’t get to always take the best of me.

इस बार गिनती की प्रक्रिया को पूरी तरह पारदर्शी और सुरक्षित बनाने के लिए आधुनिक तकनीक का सहारा लिया जा रहा है। 3D मैपिंग, वीडियोग्राफी और फोटोग्राफी के जरिए हर एक आभूषण का रिकॉर्ड तैयार किया जा रहा है। पहले चरण में चलित और बाहरी खजाने की गणना पूरी हो चुकी है, और अब सबसे अहम माने जाने वाले भीतरी रत्न भंडार की गिनती जारी है।

यह रत्न भंडार बेहद संवेदनशील माना जाता है, जहां केवल अधिकृत समिति के सदस्य ही प्रवेश कर सकते हैं। सदियों से राजा-महाराजाओं और भक्तों द्वारा अर्पित यह खजाना रहस्यों से भरा हुआ है, जिसे लेकर लोगों में जबरदस्त उत्सुकता बनी हुई है। माना जाता है कि मंदिर परिसर में आज भी कई ऐसे गुप्त कक्ष और सुरंगें हैं, जिनमें अनमोल धरोहर छिपी हो सकती है।

इतिहास के पन्नों में दर्ज है कि कई बार इस मंदिर को लूटने की कोशिशें हुईं, लेकिन हर बार सेवकों ने भगवान की प्रतिमाओं और खजाने की रक्षा की। आज, 48 साल बाद जब यह रत्न भंडार खुला है, तो देश ही नहीं, पूरी दुनिया की नजर इस पर टिकी हुई है कि आखिर इसके अंदर क्या-क्या अनमोल खजाने सामने आएंगे।

I participated in my last triathlon in 2015, Devonport, Tasmania. I left the sport after experiencing multiple stress fractures, chronic fatigue, and undergoing two surgeries for external iliac artery endofibrosis. 

On reflection, I can now say I was trying to compensate for something. Someone once asked me what was I running from? Honestly, at the time this puzzled me. I now appreciate their honesty. 

I had not yet learnt how to fuel my body to train, perform and recover. @danatk08 you did always say energy in vs energy out. I now understand this. 

Over the years I have maintained some level of fitness in rec running. But never had the drive to “Race” again. I had not yet found the “Why”. 

On a recent trip to Girona, Spain where @sallypilbeam and @steve_gleeson were based for the Paris Paralympic prep - safe to say was inspired. I had the opportunity to join for some run sessions with @sallypilbeam @charlottehall_hk & @steve_gleeson . I was reminded of how strong the mind and body is, most importantly how strong the human heart is.

Working as a Clinical Nurse Manager in Aged Care, I see on a daily basis what it’s like to live without your health and mobility. This is a strong motivator for me. 

With the help of my husband @steve_gleeson I have found the “Why”.

The mentors, coaches, and support network over the years who have played such a valuable role in not only developing athletes, but developing good people. 
For me, your advice has deeply impacted all aspects of my life. 

The art of showing up, staying disciplined & resilient, it’s priceless 🏃‍♀️✌️

BLOODY TIRED. But we got there. ✌️

The fact that we don’t even recognise the change women go through whilst having a baby just blows my mind. No wonder women are confused, lost, feeling like they don’t know who they are anymore, and struggle to figure out their new life with their baby. 

They’re missing half the picture - and it’s not their fault. 

If only mothers were more empowered through recognising this transition, then maybe we would see mothers thriving and not feeling like everything they’re doing is just invisible to the rest of society. 🩷

GENTLE REMINDER. The hormonal drop is something I have never felt in my life before. Of course I was exhausted, I had just had my baby, I was up all through the night with a clingy newborn who hated her bassinet, and my milk was coming in. But the hormone drop on top of it? That was the weird head-spinning feeling I couldn’t quite put my finger on. 

It made me feel so bizarre, like I was in a dream-like state. I even experienced some weird light sensitivity in my eye sight. And I swear even if I had slept, I still would have felt it. 

Did you experience any symptoms around 3 days post partum? 🤍

Girl, all I have to say to you is - just “do the basics”. But… it’s not that simple anymore, right? Basic sleeping, basic eating, basic hygiene - when you’re attached to your newborn 24/7, it can actually be highly challenging to do those things. 

And then… it can become the new normal, months or even years into motherhood. 

Once I realised these small people aren’t going anywhere, that’s when I understood that I need to take the initiative to look after my own wellbeing. Not by adding more to my list, but by putting myself back on the list of priorities. Because my children are my number 1, but it doesn’t just end there. I can put myself number 2, or a close tie. 🤍

Every old successful person who gets interviewed on TikTok always says “I wish I didn’t worry so much about work, and I spent more time with my family”. So when I feel like I’m stuck at home, with the kids, I think about that. And it helps me. 

I shift the mood. I put on some music I love (my girls are used to that now). I switch off the tv. I sit in the beach chair out the back, while they play. And I remember what life is about. 

There’s nothing like motherhood to shift your perspective on time, and the meaning of life. 🩷

I loved becoming a mum - it surprised me in the best way possible. But somewhere along the way, I forgot who I was. And honestly? I was miserable - and I didn’t even realise it. I saw a video my sister took of me, she thought it was lighthearted and funny, but I saw a sad human. 

I kept thinking - when does it get easier? And most people responded with, when they go to school. So… we’re meant to wait until our children aren’t in our company, to start enjoying our life again?? So I decided to take matters into my own hands, and not take that as my final answer. 

Social media is great because it exposes so many truths of motherhood. But it can also sometimes leave us hanging, feeling guilty, when we’re not the mum we “should” be 24/7. In reality? Motherhood is supposed to show us our shadow side, and help us grow, with the right support. 

So follow along for more conversations where we talk about what to actually do as a mother, as a parent, in our new life with our little ones. 🤍

I found myself a few months into motherhood, which turned into years, of survival mode. Not knowing how to enjoy this time that everyone talks about “blink and you’ll miss it”. Because will I miss it? Well maybe I will, but I’ll have to live in regret. And I don’t want that. Not when it comes to my children, who matter more to me than the world. 

Doing that has become a daily challenge, and a daily mission for me.

Of course, there are still hard days, where I feel like my confidence is shaky. 

But overall, I stand taller, I speak clearer, and with more certainty. And I know who I am. I know what I am about. I know what I value and what is important in my life. 

Motherhood gets to be your best era yet ❤️‍🔥

Hey 👋 I’M ALANA! 

Lately… I’ve been thinking about what I’m passionate about. And honestly? It’s been a bit of a journey to work out exactly what that is, but I think a really good way to figure it out is to ask yourself what you could literally talk underwater about. What you could chew someone’s ear off about. And for me, I was always in Tom‘s (my partner) ear about motherhood, and the challenges that modern mums have to face. From everything like being a working mum, and having to show up as a professional having a career, while being a mum, through to managing money stress, to feeling isolated geographically and emotionally from family. And so for a long time I was posting on my Instagram, but not really knowing what I was doing. Because I loved sharing about the reality of mum life, but I didn’t quite know how to actually help mums. I thought that just by being authentic, it was helping. Which I do think is one important part of it, but I also felt like social media used to leave me hanging with those relatable moments, but not actually giving me any tools to help.

This is why I created this Instagram account. I have such a passion for mums, and I just want mums to be able to enjoy those early years as much as they humanly can. Every child deserves a mum that is happy. 

I truly believe the world would be a better place if we all had happy mums. 

So here’s to empowering mums, or maybe better put, helping mothers reignite that power that they forgot they had along the way ❤️‍🔥

What a year 2025 was ! 
We started off pretty fresh going on holidays than it got shorty with our first miscarriage of the year that completely changed our life and our thoughts on extending our little family . 

We literally chased many many highs this year , going to more local outings ,
Chasing sunsets , enjoying each others company and trying to blend well as a family of 4 ! 

Riley had an extremely rough first semester then we started his ADHD management an started Ritalin . 

We started to see some personal wins and success in his learning over semester 2 and we couldn’t be prouder . 

We found out we were expecting another little bundle in may that turned our whole world back down side up ! 
Our little rainbow princess added hope and love to our family that we never thought we’d knew we needed and has allowed us to move onto our next chapter as a family of 5 ! 

We can’t wait to meet her in a few short weeks in February 🩷

Oliver Turned 2 ! 
He is such a ray of sunshine , full of fire and the biggest sweet heart ever ! 
He still however shy’a away around people and raids the boss aunty’s loll draw every time we leave school . 

He pushes the boundaries and tests limits , seeks curiosity, friendships and connections amongst others and is always full of surprises and new tricks . 

Let’s bring on 2026 , new adventures , thrill seeking and begin a new chapter as moving completely forward as a family of 5 ! 
We close the chapter of lots of last moments but will fill our lives with lots of firsts . 

Happy new year everyone 🥳 🥂 🎆 

.

The pause on the injunction will remain in place until April 17, giving the administration time to potentially seek emergency intervention from the U.S. Supreme Court.

President Trump first announced plans for the approximately 90,000-square-foot ballroom last year, saying the project would be privately funded and designed to host major state and diplomatic events at the White House.

The legal dispute is expected to continue as courts review whether the project complies with federal law and presidential authority over White House construction decisions.

That means that I dislocated my knee, because the patellar ligament holds it in place, so sometimes it likes to just pop out lol.  He had suggested that since it’s my first injury, to do physical therapy for a month and then see.  It’s been a month, and I’ve hit a plateau with my PT, so I’m getting surgery. 

And I’m getting it this Wednesday!  The day before Halloween.  It was either do it now or have to wait until the new year.  This is my first real surgery and I’ll be in physical therapy for months following.  Prayers and show recommendations would be really appreciated for all those seeing this.  Thanks for reading :)

I think most photographers will agree that there are times in our lives when we will meet people who challenge our views of life and living. Dean Potter was one of those special humans. He embraced his own view of the world, living life on his own terms, doing something that most people are fearful of doing. That’s a brave man living in a world of facades. Dean was no different than us….he was ALL of us, “beautifully flawed” Thank you Dean for enriching my life. #hbofilms #hbo #senderfilms #deanpotter #thedarkwizard

Photo taken at Camp 4 Yosemite Valley 2003

Very excited to see this new film about Dean Potter called “The Dark Wizard”. Directed by Nick Rosen (the Alpinst) and Peter Mortimer. 

It was an incredible opportunity to spend a few days with Dean following him around with my 8x10 Deardorff and my long time assistant and now photographer Todd Meier in Yosemite Valley many years ago thanks to @outsidemagazine making photos. I found Dean to be a deeply kind and insightful human being, and because of his spirit we formed a friendship. 

Kudos to the directors of this beautiful film and bringing his story to life. It’s just brilliant! 
#deanpotter #thedarkwizard #outsidemagazine #hbo

So this is Mr. Orange, my first 3D Sculpture created in #nomadsculpt iPad app. A view from a few different angles. I have always been in awe of people who created 3D art and animators, but I have a renewed respect for people who do this for a living. This is a lot of work. Some great 3D artists I enjoy following are @smallrobotstudio and @drugfreedave3d and @quantillion

Here is my first attempt using a 3D sculpting app on my iPad called #NomadSculpt and let me tell you, this stuff is much harder than it looks when you are a complete newbie to using 3D Sculpting applications. But the tutorials that I watched said it’s a fantastic app for people who already know how to do this kind of artwork and they assured me it was a great one to use for people like me. Well, it was tougher than the tutorials made it look, but I fumbled through and managed to finish this little guy. The hardest thing for me was figuring out all the new terminology used in the interface and learning how to use the tools. That gizmo is so difficult to get used to using. LOL! And I wish that the app came with more texture files, environment, and background options. I’m not convinced 3D Art is my thing, but I will do a little more exploring and see if I can turn out something better than this first attempt.

It’s here! The 2026-27 Local Food Guide is out now! Look for free copies making their way to farmers markets, groceries, restaurants, and other community locations around the region in the next few weeks.

In addition to hundreds of listings for farms, markets, restaurants, artisan producers, and groceries, this year’s guide includes stories on agritourism as a means for farms to welcome back visitors after Helene, the momentum behind local food in schools, and heritage foods of Appalachia. Plus, get recipes from @finestavl, @reidscafe_nc, @vernerasheville, and Enola Group Head Start!

If you’re too eager to get your hands on a copy, check out the online version in the meantime at asapconnections.org.

Many farmers are making their long-awaited return as farmers tailgate markets are preparing to open for a new season with a few shifts in operating hours over the next few weeks. Here is a list of all Buncombe County markets, but you can also find opening dates for markets across the region at appalachiangrown.org. 

At these early spring markets, you’ll begin to find some new and exciting seasonal produce over the next few weeks, including strawberries, asparagus, rhubarb, alliums, ramps, and more! You’ll also be able to source much of the produce we’ve seen through the winter, like cold-hardy greens, salad mixes, turnips, and radishes. As always, you can also get mushrooms, eggs, meat, cheese, bread, and prepared foods. Look out for a wide variety of plant starts for your gardens in the coming weeks as well! 

See a full list of Buncombe markets in this week's roundup of What' Fresh at asapconnections.org.

A new report from ASAP's Local Food Research Center is out now! This data brief compares prices at farmers markets and retail outlets revealing that seasonal produce and local eggs often cost the same at farmers markets as in grocery stores. 

In ASAP's “Why Buy Local?” consumer research report (2025), Local Food Research Center found that 87 percent of consumers in Western North Carolina purchased local food products at least monthly. The primary driver was connection and support of local farmers. However, 35 percent of these local food shoppers reported that price was a barrier to buying more local food. Among typical shoppers, this figure rose to 57 percent.

Therefore, ASAP conducted an environmental audit of 10 farmers markets and 13 nearby retail stores in autumn of 2025. The purpose of the audit was to assess food prices on seasonal food items and to assess product labeling including name/variety, price, and growing practices.

Read the full report at asapconnections.org/local-food-research-center.

What a joy to invite children to taste local ingredients, learn more about where their food comes from, and even meet a real life farmer!

We also want to extend a thank you and special shout out to Chef Emily of @boneandbrothavl, who helped make local root veggie chips for the kids to try–we'd say it was a hit! And to @terramonga Farm for setting up a table so kids could experience "purchasing" produce right from the farmer.

Thank you Danielle, Debbi, and Suzi for fostering these experiences.

Want to gain visibility for your business and connect with the region's passion for local food? Be a Farm Tour sponsor! ASAP's annual Farm Tour (Sept. 19-20 this year) has approximately 2,000 participants who are eager to engage with their community and find fun experiences. Contact ASAP's Development Director, Nora Scheff (nscheff@asapconnections.org), to learn more about how to showcase your support of local food and farms.

It’s no secret that Asheville and the surrounding Blue Ridge Mountain region draws visitors from all over. Travelers flock for the sweeping mountain views, vibrant food culture, and the opportunity to slow down and experience the landscape in a deeper way. Visiting farms, whether from out of town or in one’s own backyard, has become one of the most meaningful ways to take in that scenery while experiencing a true taste of place.

Across Southern Appalachia, farms welcome visitors to wander through apple orchards, pick strawberries straight from the field, taste the grape harvest in handcrafted wines, or gather bouquets in colorful flower patches. Children feed goats through wooden fences, families take tractor rides through orchards, and visitors leave with bags of farm goods raised just yards away. For many farmers, these moments are more than an average day on the farm—they are part of a vital economic lifeline known as agritourism.

In this year’s Local Food Guide, we look at agritourism as a means for farms to welcome back visitors after Helene with stories from @broomsblooms, @thetenacregarden, @steppshillcrestorchard, and @theorchardataltapass.

Read more of these stories at asapconnections.org/guide, or look for the print edition, available for free at farmers markets, local businesses, and other community locations over the coming weeks.

Beets might not be a favorite for everyone, but they sure taste like something ancient rising from the earth. The first beets were actually sea beets growing along the coastal regions of the Mediterranean. Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans first cultivated the sea beet for its leafy greens–think something like swiss chard.

In hot climates where the beet originated, chilled dishes are a welcomed and cooling delight, making them a perfect addition to any mezze platter. And after the week of heat we have had, a mezze spread might be right up your alley!

Try out these Moroccan beet salad and beet yogurt dip recipes in this week's roundup of What's Fresh at Buncombe County farmers tailgate markets at asapconnections.org.

Not in Buncombe? Search for markets across the region at appalachiangrown.org.

For this month’s Faces of Local interview, we spoke with Ellie Goldstein who is a farmer and co-owner of @smallholdingfarm in Morganton and @mainseasonmarket in Marion.

When COVID-19 disrupted Ellie’s and her partner, Dan’s, life plans, they pivoted their small farm operation in Alexander and moved to a larger growing space in Morganton, birthing Smallholding Farm. A few years later, working with their friend Walter Kaelin, Ellie and Dan opened Main Season Market and Brewery in downtown Marion. Main Season is open Thursday to Saturday, 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday to Monday, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Read more from Ellie at asapconnections.org.

This year, students across North Carolina will eat locally grown products in school meals, engage in educational activities about agriculture and nutrition, and take part in school gardening experiences. 

According to the 2023 USDA Farm to School Census, 59 percent of school nutrition departments in North Carolina served local foods in their schools, ranking 34th out of 50 states, and 10 percent of total food costs came from local products, ranking 41st out of 50 states.

School nutrition directors often want to purchase more local products, and farmers often want to sell to local school districts, but challenges to purchasing local food remain.

In this year’s Local Food Guide, we feature the momentum and challenges behind local food in schools. This story is excerpted from the original by Analisa Sorrells Archer with @educationnc. Find the full text at ednc.org/schools-want-to-serve-more-local-food-in-cafeterias-but-challenges-remain.

Read more of these stories at asapconnections.org/guide, or look for the print edition, available for free at farmers markets, local businesses, and other community locations over the coming weeks.

ASAP's Local Food Research Center annually surveys farmers in the Appalachian Grown region to assess changes and opportunities in the local food system. A report based on the 2025 Appalachian Grown Producer Survey is available now at asapconnections.org/research-reports.

Analysis of the annual survey data, which includes questions about land access, production costs, market opportunities, marketing strategies, and product sales, helps inform ASAP’s farmer programs. The 2025 survey was completed approximately 14 months after Hurricane Helene struck the region and in addition to standard questions farmers were asked about the impact the year after the storm.

Despite hardships brought about by Helene and economic instability due to national and global factors, Appalachian Grown farmers remained hopeful with many citing the power of community support. Read more in the report.

Food informs our identities—it holds our history, our present time, and our future. It’s no secret that the Southern Appalachian region has a long and rich history of traditional foods with strong ties to the land. Appalachian people are known for using what they have. Characterized by food preservation, game meat, and foraging, Appalachian food traditions were born out of geographic isolation, resourcefulness through poverty, farming ingenuity among mountain landscapes, and strong ties to community.

In this year’s Local Food Guide, we share stories from farmers about their ties to Southern Appalachian foodways. Read about how tobacco shaped our region, how farmers like @burnettefamilyfarm are keeping sorghum alive, why @blackthornfarmandkitchen is growing out a productive pawpaw orchard, and the reasons @melvinhillmeats is raising the heritage American Guinea hog.

Read more of these stories at asapconnections.org/guide, or look for the print edition, available for free at farmers markets, local businesses, and other community locations over the coming weeks.

Did you know you can Double SNAP for Fruits and Vegetables at farm stands in WNC, too?

While ASAP's Double SNAP for Fruits and Vegetables Program predominantly operates at farmers markets across WNC, ASAP staff have been working with interested farms that are key local food access points to begin accepting SNAP payments on the farm level. Currently, SNAP participants can visit @3barnfarms and @dealfarmsfreshproduce in Franklin, NC to double their SNAP. 3 Barn Farm is kicking off accepting SNAP with a plant sale this weekend!

Becoming approved to accept SNAP is no easy lift, but our aim is to continue to work alongside farms to facilitate this process, and to offer Double SNAP support to more communities in WNC. Stay tuned for new Double SNAP partner additions in the future.

Our Growing Mind's team sure has been busy in schools this spring! 

The week before last alone, the team hosted seven cafeteria taste tests throughout Buncombe and Haywood County. Taste tests provide students the opportunity to try a variety of foods, introducing them to foods that are locally grown and in season. It also facilitates a change in food choices, creates positive food environments, and is a fun and memorable experience.

Students at Haw Creek Elementary and WD Williams tasted a salad with local lettuce from @terramonga and radishes from @wwcfarm with a strawberry poppyseed vinaigrette. @buncombeschools

At Haywood County Schools, students tasted local greens grown by Two Trees Farm (baby bok choy), Tuscola High School (Buttercrunch lettuce), and Pisgah High School (turnips & mustard greens) CTE horticulture program.  At these taste tests, younger students experienced the taste test from their older student peers, which of course made it easier to try something new when offered from a cool high school student!

What better way to kick off Earth Day than by uplifting farmers markets and the people that make them happen. For this month’s Faces of Local interview, we spoke with Dakota Parker (pictured left), the Downtown Event Coordinator for the City of Hendersonville, as well as the Market Manager for @hendersonvillefarmersmarket.

Born and raised in Western North Carolina, Dakota didn’t come into this role with much experience or knowledge of farmers markets or local agriculture four years ago, but he has gained many skills and fallen in love with the community he has built at the market. Hendersonville Farmers Market is set to reopen for the season on Saturday, May 2, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.

“With the addition of [ASAP’s Farm Fresh] Prescription Program, even more members of our community have access to fresh, locally grown food that they might not otherwise be able to afford,” shared Dakota. “It also provides a meaningful economic boost for our vendors. This support has made a real impact.”

Read more from Dakota at asapconnections.org.

As more markets open over the coming weeks, make your trip to market more exciting and easeful with some simple tips to help you make the most of your market visits—and feel good knowing your choices are helping our communities grow and thrive.

Shopping at a farmers market is as much about the experience as it is about the fresh food and a little preparation goes a long way as markets can be busy places with different traffic flows, parking situations, payment methods, pet policies, and more.

Meet and welcome one of the new members of ASAP's Board of Directors! 

Karen Blaedow is a Horticultural Agent at NC Cooperative Extension we are excited for her to bring her expertise and connections to our mission. We asked her a little about herself and this is what she had to say!

Q: What are you up to when you’re not at our board meetings? 
A:  When I am not at ASAP board meetings, I’m working full-time assisting vegetable and small fruit farms in Henderson County. I also currently serve on a few additional boards which include the NC Tomato Growers Association, North American Raspberry and Blackberry Association, NC Caneberry Association and as the chair of the WNC AgOptions Steering Committee. When I’m not working, I’m gardening, immersing myself in nature and spending lots of time with my husband and son.

Q: Why is ASAP important to you?
A: ASAP has played a critical role in the work that I do with local foods and in particular farmers markets. I can’t think of a more impactful partner organization working in this space. ASAP provides community support for helping producers market their local products, they empower markets to provide a place for local farms to sell their products and more importantly their programs help increase local food access to more customers regardless of their economic situation. ASAP builds farms, markets & community!

Q: What’s your favorite local food dish? 
A: I’m a mushroom maniac so basically any dish that has oysters, maitake, or lion’s mane with it.

Meet and welcome one of the new members of ASAP's Board of Directors! 

Amy Yaroch is the Chief Executive Officer of Center for Nutrition & Health Impact and we are excited for her to bring her expertise and insight to our mission. We asked her a little about herself and this is what she had to say!

Q: What are you up to when you’re not at our board meetings? 
A:  Hiking and getting outdoors to enjoy all that Western North Carolina has to offer, including visiting our amazing farmers markets. I am so happy that the East Asheville Tailgate Market started back up. I try to swing by every Friday afternoon (when I am not traveling) to pick up local goodies.

It’s Spring! 🌱 That means it’s time to get those seeds started. This DIY newspaper plant pot is a fun idea to do with the kids in your life. Plus, it’s cheap and easy to make! All you need is newspaper, a cup, seeds, soil, and water. 

🌱Step 1: Rip your newspaper in half and use a few sheets for each pot. 
🌱Step 2: Roll your cup on the newspaper but leave a little space at the top. 
🌱Step 3: Fold the newspaper into the open part of the cup. 
🌱Step 4: Remove the cup, reach your hand inside, and push the newspaper down to create a bottom. 
🌱Step 5: Fill your pot with potting soil.
🌱Step 6: Pick out some spring seeds and plant a few in the pot.
🌱Step 7: Water your seeds and place them in a sunny place in your house to watch them sprout and grow! Water regularly. Once the threat of frost has passed, you can plant them directly into the soil and they will biodegrade.

If you’ve been online lately, you may have seen 2026 declared as the year of the cabbage, but foodies and farmers market goers know that cabbage never really needed to be trending. Long before social media anointed the humble, layered globe as the vegetable of the moment, communities across the world relied on cabbage as a winter staple and a nourishing crop that has carried families through the coldest months of the year.

Cabbage belongs to the Brassica family—the same plant lineage that includes broccoli, kale, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and many Asian greens. So whether you're making Polish-inspired cabbage and kielbasa, Korean kimchi, or a simple stir-fry with bok choy, you're cooking with a long history of brassicas.

The CSA season typically begins in April or May, around the same time that seasonal farmers markets reopen, and lasts for 20-26 weeks. Some farms offer a fall extension, often as an add-on to the regular season. There are even a few farms that have winter or year-round produce CSAs! Look at the fall/winter column in ASAP’s CSA charts.

Now is the time to sign up for a regular season CSA share! If your first choice farm has already sold out, look for a newer farm that is still building a customer base.

Paying before the season starts is fundamental to the CSA model, but some farms do offer installment or pay-as-you-go plans. A few farms have a work-trade option to assist with on-farm tasks in exchange for a reduced price or free share.

Some farms set aside shares to donate to feeding sites or community members in need, and you may choose to pay toward those. Ask if the farm has the means to donate missed shares, such as when you’re on vacation.
Hold the vision, trust the process.

I am courageous, I am creative, I am beautiful…
I am strong, I am independent, I am vivacious…

I am this, this, this, and this…
and that, that, that and that…

what a woman is in their perspective. That person's

I had to figure it out, work it out, balance it out.
I prayed, I sought, I cried, I endured… I am Woman!

My image of a woman is defined through God's transformation of me, not through the image of what the world says a woman should be.

Do not let this flower Jell-O intimidate you. It is easy to make. You just need a flower silicon mold. To make the flowers you need one cup or 200 mL milk, 50 mL heavy whipping cream, 50 g sugar, 2 tablespoon unflavored gelatin powder, half a teaspoon vanilla, a few drops of red color. Mix all the above and dissolved gelatin using  bain_marie method. I put the bowl on top a boiling kettle. Lightly brush your flower mold with oil. Fill up the mold with the above liquid. Placed in the freezer for 15 minutes, then carefully take the flower out of the mold. It takes about two hours to make nine flowers. Once you have all your flower start making  the first layer. Mix one pack of aloe vera Jell-O or unflavored gelatin with 1 1/2 cup hot water, steer to dissolve the Jell-O completely. Pour 10 tablespoon of the clear gelatin mix at the bottom of your mold.  Put the mold in the fridge for 10 minutes. Then place all flowers face down on the clear Jell-O. If you like sprinkle a few slivered pistachio or mint leaves on the side of the flowers.. carefully pour the rest of the clear Jell-O on top and around the flowers and place in the fridge for 15 minutes. For the last layer. Dissolve one pack of strawberry Jell-O with 2 tablespoon unflavored gelatin, in one and a half cup of hot water. In a food processor place the dissolved gelatin, 120 g of tea biscuits 1 teaspoon vanilla, 200 mL heavy cream and one cup milk. Mix until smooth. Pour this mixture on top of the clear Jell-O in the mold. Break about 100 g tea biscuits into big chunks and add to this last layer. Let it rest in the fridge for five hours or overnight. Dip the mold in warm water to take out the jello. #jello #jellocake #ژله_ویترینی #ژله_مجلسی #ژله

Mango tiramisu 
¾ cup mango pulp, 200 to 225 g mascarpone cheese, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup of granulated sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 2 cups heavy cream, 260 g Ladyfingers or enough to fill your dish
Topping
⅔ cup mango pulp, mango peels, mint leaves and fresh flowers. 
The above is for a nine inch square dish. I used a 9 by 11 inch dish and doubled the ingredients. 
In a bowl, whisk together the mascarpone cheese, sugar, and vanilla extract for about one minute, or until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whisk heavy cream until stiff peaks form. Carefully fold one-third of the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture. Gradually fold in the remaining whipped cream, being careful not to overmix.
Once the filling is prepared, pour in 1/2 cup of the mango pulp and gently fold. Set aside.
Then, pour the remaining pulp into a shallow dish. Dip each ladyfinger into the pulp then arrange them in a single layer at the bottom of your serving dish.
Spread half of the mango mascarpone filling over the ladyfingers and smooth the surface. Add another layer of dipped ladyfingers, followed by the remaining filling. Smooth the top, cover the dish with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight for the best results.
Just before serving, pour the remaining mango pulp over the tiramisu and smooth it out. Then add mango roses to the corner of the dish and garnish with mint leaves as shown. Original recipe with some modifications from @simshomekitchen #mangotiramisu  #fruitcake #تیرامیسو #انبه

The recipe for this Swiss roll, is the best one in my opinion : 4 Egg yolks room temp, 3/4 cup sugar, 40 ml(1/4 cup), 40 ml (1/4) cup oil, 1 tsp Vanilla extract, 3/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup corn starch, 1 tsp lemon juice or vinegar. For the filling we need, 125 ml Whipping cream, 20 g sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. For cover: 200 g white chocolate and color of your choice. Fruit of your choice is optional, I added  a 1/2 cup of raspberries 
Separate the egg yolks from the egg whites. Add vinegar to the egg whites and beat until foamy, gradually add half the sugar and keep beating until stiff. In a different bowl beat the egg yolks with the rest of the sugar and vanilla until pale in color, add the flour and cornstarch to the egg yolks in two batches. Incorporate the egg whites. Be careful not to deflate the egg whites. Line an 18 by 13 inch baking sheet with parchment paper. Pour the butter and even it out using a spatula. Tap the tray several times on the counter so all the air bubbles are out. Bake at 165 C or 325F for 25 minutes. Let the cake cool completely. Peel off the parchment and spread it with whipping cream, which you have beaten with sugar and vanilla. Cut a clean piece of bubble wrap the size of your roll. Melt the chocolate. Take 2 Tbsp of the melted chocolate and color it with the color you like. 
Spread the colored chocolate over the bubble wrap in a random pattern. Then cover the whole sheet with melted white chocolate. Wait a few minutes for chocolate to set then wrap it around the roll and press down to ensure the chocolate sticks tightly to the cake. Let it sit for about 10 minutes and carefully peel off the wrap. Enjoy.

No back cheese cake with jello. Impressive and delicious yet easy to make. You need 200g tea biscuits or gram crackers, 100g melted butter, 200g mascarpone cheese, 200g heavy whipping cream (whipped), 1 tsp vanilla, half cups sugar, 2 tbs agar agar or gelatin, 1 pack strawberry jello, half a cup pomegranate seeds, 1 tbs slivered pistachios. Using a food processor grind the crackers and place one tbs in each cupcake liner and press them. Mix cheese, sugar, cream and vanilla using a hand mixer. Place agar agar and 2 tbs cold water in a bowl and place over a double boiler to melt the agar. Add the mixture to the cheese and cream. Place 1 full tablespoon of the cheese mix over the crust and spread evenly. Put a few pomegranate seeds and sliver pistachios on top of the cream. Mix the jello with one and half cups of hot water. Let it cool completely. Fill up each cupcake liner with jello. Pour the jello slowly so the cheese layer would not dislodge. Place the cakes in the fridge for a few hours. Peel the liners slowly and carefully and enjoy your perfect art work. 😉#jellocake #jello #یلدا #کیک_یلدایی_انار #کیک_یلدا #کیک_ژله_ای

Apple Turnover
The easiest, delicious, professional looking pastry anyone can make in 30 minutes. 
For eight 5" by 5" or 13 centimeter pastry you will need, eight 5" puff pastry squares, 2 medium apple peeled and cut into small pieces, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 20 gram butter, 2 Tbsp walnut pieces. For the top you need to mix 1 egg plus 1 Tbsp milk( I added a bit of saffron) and few almond slices If desired.
Place butter, apples, sugar and cinnamon, and walnuts in a small pot and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, set aside to cool. Dust the work surface with a little flour and assemble the pastry by placing about 2 Tbsp of the apple mixture in the middle of the pastry squares. Brush two sides of the pastry with the egg wash and attach the ends to form a triangle. Press the edges well with a fork. Make 3 cuts on top of the pastry for steam to scape. Place the assembled pastries on a parchment covered tray and let them rest in the fridge for 20 minutes. Then brush them with egg wash sprinkle with Almond slices if desired.

Bamieh is a fried food used in festivities all over Middle East and India. There are many different versions. This one is called "Harandy" and is specially made during the Muslim fasting month of Ramadan. 
بامیه هرندی خوشمزه برای رمضان یا هر موقع 😉
Milk or water 500 ml, oil 50 ml or 1/4 cup, honey 1 Tbsp, flour 250 g or 1 2/3 cup, 1/2 tsp baking powder, vanilla 1 tsp, 3 eggs
For syrup: 2 cups sugar, 1 cup water, 1/4 cup rose water, 1 Tbsp liquid saffron, 1 Tbsp glucose, 3 cardamom pods, 1 Tbsp lemon juice. Bring water and sugar to boil, add lemon juice and glucose. Do not mix with the spoon. Let everything simmer on low for 30 minutes. Add saffron, rose water, cardamom and let it simmer for another 5 minutes. Set aside. For Bamieh, bring water, oil and honey to boil, add flour and baking powder at once and keep mixing the flour on low for about 5 minutes until cooked. Transfer to a bowl and once cooled, add eggs and vanilla and mix with paddle attachment. Use your favorite tip to pipe out Bamieh. Vegetarian eggplant halim, حلیم بادنجان بدون گوشت
1 kilogram or 2 pounds eggplants, 1/2 cup rice, 1/2 cup whey or Greek yogurt,  1/2 cup crushed walnuts, 5 garlic cloves smashed,
2 medium onions peeled and thinly sliced, 2 Tbsp dry and crushed mint leaves, 1/2 tsp each turmeric, cinnamon, 1 tsp each salt and pepper (or to taste)، 1 Tbsp liquid saffron. Make several holes in eggplants and grill them until they are soft and cooked. The best way to grill them is to use charcoal to get the smoky flavor or use store bought roasted eggplants.(You can also peel and fry them on both sides). 
While eggplants are cooking, in a small pot boil the rice with one and half cups of water, a pinch of salt and a little oil until the rice is completely cooked and no liquid is left, set aside. Note, you may need to add a bit more water to insure the rice is cooked and soft.
After grilling, peel them while still hot. Place the eggplants and rice in a bowl and smash them. In a small pan sauté dry mint with 1 Tbsp oil for just 1 minute, set aside. In a large pan on medium heat fry the onions in 3 Tbsp oil for about 10 minutes then add the garlic and all the spices and fry for another minute. Add the smashed eggplants and continue to sauté the eggplants for about 10 minutes. Place the mix in a large bowl and add the 1/4 of whey, half the fried onions, walnuts, saffron, and salt and pepper. Adjust the salt to taste.Then place the mix in a serving dish and decorate with dry mint, herbs, fried onion and liquid whey.

Financiers are petite cakes with crispy top and medium density. They are high in protein due to egg whites. The unique taste is due to the brown butter.
60 g flour, 60 g almond meal, a pinch of salt, 120 g powdered sugar, 5 egg whites, 1 drop almond oil or 1 tsp almond extract, 100g unsalted butter, 1/2 tsp baking powder almond slices for garnish. 
Place the butter in a small pot on medium heat until it melts, lower the heat and let the butter get golden color, be careful it does not burn. It takes about 7 minutes. Use a small fine mesh to separate the liquid butter from the brown solids. You only need the clear liquid. While the butter cools down, mix flour, almond meal, salt, baking powder and sugar in a bowl. Sift once and set aside. In a different bowl, using a hand whisk, mix the egg whites and almond oil a little bit. Add the whites to the dry ingredients with a hand whisk. Then add the butter in three to four batches and gently mix. Cover the batter with plastic and let it rest in the fridge for at least 2 hours or up to 12 hours. 
Heat the oven at 200 C or 390 F butter the cups of a financier mold or muffin mold generously. Decide the chilled batter equally among the cups. Garnish the top with slices of almonds. Bake at 200 C for 10 minutes for cakes to rise, then lower the temp to 180C or 350 F and bake for another 15 minutes or until a tester comes out clean.#financier#petitcake #frenchcakes #minicakes #شیرینی_بوتیکی #shirini #کیک_خانگی #فینانسیه #kadbanoo_basalighe #persianbaking #teatime☕️

Spinach Swiss roll 
رولت اسفناج ، دستور فارسی در کامنت 
4 eggs, 3/4 cup sugar, 3 Tbsp spinach juice ( from 2 cups of blended and squeezed fresh spinach leaves),3/4 cup flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 
Place a parchment paper in a 30 by 40 centimeter tray. Turn the oven to 180 centigrade or 350 Fahrenheit. 
Separate the egg whites from yolks. Beat the whites until foamy then add half the sugar one spoon at the time. Keep beating until soft peaks form. Set aside in the fridge. In another bowl beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar until cream color and double in size,then add the spinach juice. Mix the flour and backing powder and sift twice, then add it the yolk mix using a wooden spoon. Finally add the whites in three batches. Mix carefully not to deflate the mix. Pour the batter in the tray and spread. Drop the tray on the counter a few times to get rid of all the air bubbles. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes. Let the cake cool and turn to peel the paper Then wrap the cake in a clean parchment paper and roll. Let the cake cool. Unwrap the cake and cover with cream, fruits or nuts. Wrap and decorate with fruits or flowers. One large package (about 30) tiramisu, one pound raspberry, 1/2 cup sugar, 200 g mascarpone cheese, 200 g whipping cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla powder or extract,
8" round or square ring. 
Place raspberries and sugar in a pan on medium heat, let raspberries cook for about 10 minutes. Using a blender puréed raspberries and pass them through a sieve.
Toss the seeds and let the juice cool.
Place the ring inside your serving dish. Arrange ladyfingers like picket fence using the ring as support. Cover the bottom with ladyfingers as tightly as possible breaking them as needed to fit the corners. Whip the cream, sugar and vanilla until stiff then add mascarpone and mix. Using a pastry bag, cover the bottom layer of ladyfingers with the cream mix. For the Second layer dip each Ladyfingers in raspberry syrup and place on top of the cream mix. Cover with cream and continue layering until the cake reaches the top of the standing ladyfingers.
Top the cake with cream mix, then a thin layer of raspberry syrup. Decorate with whole raspberries and cream mix. Let the cake stay in fridge over night or at least 12 hours. Dill sourdough 
نان ساور با شوید
80% hydration, 35 g dark Rye flour, 70 g whole wheat flour, 382 g bread flour, 2 Tablespoons dry dill, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 380 g water, 98 g active starter, 10 g salt
Mix all the flours, dill, cumin and water. Cover with a towel and Let sit for 2 hours at room temperature. Mix in the starter and fold the dough for 4 minutes while in the bowl. Cover and let sit for 30 minutes. Mix in the salt and fold for another 4 minutes. Cover the bowl with the towel and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. Laminate the dough by wetting the work surface and hands, stretch to a big rectangle and fold on itself. Place the dough in a clean bowl, cover with towel and rest for 4 hours while Stretch and fold the dough on itself every 30 minutes. After 4 hours, dust the workplace with flour, take the dough out and fold again on itself. Dust the bread basket with rice flour and place the dough top side dawn in the basket. Cover with towel and rest overnight in fridge. Next day heat the oven with a Dutch oven inside at 500 F for at least 30 minutes. Take the dough out of the basket, score your design with a sharp blade, slip parchment paper under the bough and place in the hot dutch oven.
Bake at 500 F for 30 minutes, remove the lid, lower temperature to 475F and bake for another 15 to 20 minutes.

Chicken with sour 
Chicken breast with sour grape is an old authentic Persian recipe. It can be served with both eggplants or zucchini. 
500 g chicken breast cut into long strips, 1 medium onion diced, 6 zucchini, 2 eggs, 1 cup bread crumbs, 1/2 tsp each, paprika, black pepper, coriander powder, lemon pepper, 1 tsp salt, 1 Tbsp liquid saffron, 1 Tbsp tomato paste. 
Cut zucchini's in half and make long cuts all the way down each half. ( look at the pictures and video clip). Dip each half into egg and then drench in bread crumbs. Set aside. 
Place the onion and 2 Tbsp oil in a pan on medium heat and stir for about 5 minutes. Add the spices and chicken. Let the chicken change colors on all sides ( about 10 minutes) be careful not to burn the onions. Add tomato paste and one and half cup boiling water to the pan, cover and cook for about 15 minutes. Add the sour grape and cook for another 5 to 10 minutes without lid.Meanwhile fry the zucchini in oil and drain on paper towel. 
Arrange the zucchini and chicken on a platter and serve with basmati rice and fresh herbs.

Most parents count down the days til their baby arrives, yet everyday we were praying you’d both stay in for another day longer.. 

We waited anxiously to be told you were “better out than in” and with every scan we watched that cord flow slowly go further and further backwards instead of forwards. 

Maternity leave started at 29 weeks, alongside a relocation 5 hours away from your dad, and our family. There was no nesting stage, no meals prepped for the freezer, no deep clean or organisation of the house.. Just a one-way trip to the city and a constant buzz of anxiety, hoping that you would both be okay. 

Your hospital bag was full of 00000 clothes that I knew would be far too big for either of you, my heart hurt that we wouldn’t get that iconic “I’m Here” picture for Instagram in cute, personalised onesies without there being a myriad of cords to navigate let alone the acrylic walls surrounding your tiny bodies. 

My blood pressure was inching higher as the days went on and my previously “normal” iron levels plummeted, resulting in admission to hospital, a concoction of beta blockers and an iron infusion to keep this machine ticking along.. cue the start of my sleepless nights with 4 hourly obs.

A panicked business owner (your amazing Daddy) frantically re-organised work, cleaned the house from top to toe, packed his bag and jumped on a flight to join me as we waited to be told you were both “better out than in”.

On Wednesday the 27th of November 2024, the wonderful Dr who had been looking after us all, told us we were going to meet you both within the hour.. We had made it to 33+1 weeks! We were reassured that you were both going to be just fine and that you can “fatten up” on the outside.

Everything from that point onward changed, I felt like I was watching it all play out from above, the disassociation was real. As they pulled you both out from my tummy, first Henley, then Oakley, I listened for those beautiful cries.. it was then I realised I had the most important job I’ll ever have, raising our sons 🩵🩵

Honestly I think the farm needs like a sage smudge! There’s been negative energy here since we lost our geese friends to a neighborhood dog attack in January. The dogs somehow chewed through a welded wire fence in the few hours that we left the farm on a Sunday. It was so devastating and I haven’t been able to write about it until now. We hatched these geese from eggs seven years ago and the two sebastopols were our engagement present. As goslings, they lived with us Inside the camper that came with the land 😭 They were a big part of the farm. It seems silly to grieve this while so many terrible things are happening everywhere but sometimes it’s the little things that can kind of break you down. Anyway, I just wanted to let y’all know about our geese friends. You won’t be chased by a squonky goose anymore when visitng tbe farm but it’s so quiet here now. 😢😢😢

Preface: we’re deeply grateful for what we have and know there’s a lot of heavy stuff happening in the world but this weekend at the farm was a comedy of errors.

Saturday morning I broke my right hand sledding down the neighborhood hill. Haven’t seen a doctor yet because urgent cares were closed, we don’t have a 4WD family car, and the toddler can’t ride in the truck 🙃 Ortho appointment today 🤞

Meanwhile Jay spent the morning thawing HVAC drain lines in the mushroom building using a hairdryer, a lighter, and a tea kettle. He’s still running around trying to save fruiting rooms that froze overnight.

I did animal chores left-handed and repurposed the broken sled to haul hay to the donkeys while Grandma watched Wren on FaceTime because school’s canceled.

It’s one of those stretches where the all-work-no-play life is getting to us. I’m grateful to be in control of our work and to contribute to local food production, but also feeling very worn down and not totally sure how I’m about to parent a toddler with one hand 🫠

Massospora cicidina

So stoked to find some of these this year!
This fungus infects only 13 and 17 year cicadas. Nymphs are infected by spores in the soil as they climb their way to the surface. The fungus then takes over their body and they develop a plug of spores where their lower abdomen used to be!
The cicadas then fly and crawl around spreading spores over every surface for the next generation. 
The fungus supplies them with amphet@mines to keep them going and attempting to mate with other cicadas. 

This one was found amongst at least half a dozen others dying on the sidewalk in north Asheville.

Helene washed away so much precious topsoil from WNC farms. We’re brainstorming ways to rebuild and remediate the soil with mushrooms.

Last year, we partnered with the SAHC incubator farm to begin trials for a mushroom compost operation using our spent growing medium. Pictured here is the compost after one year of passive decomposition. 

I’m currently writing a SARE grant to use stropharia and oyster mushrooms to speed decomposition of woody debris left by the storm. Inoculated mulch from downed trees could be used to add organic material back to fields relatively quickly. I’m looking for a few partner farms to include in this SARE grant. Please reach out if you’re interested!

Beyond the accelerated debris cleanup and soil building aspects of this preliminary project, I’d like to determine if our mushroom compost can truly boost microbial life in flood depleted soils by “seeding” the soil with mycelium and improving soil structure.

And lastly, I’d like to explore the purported remediation properties of oyster mushrooms. Mycoremediation is a newer and less studied field than phytoremediation. Many bold claims have been made that mushrooms can save the world. But we need much more detail and scientific work to back up these claims! I wasn’t sure what my academic future held after completing my MS this spring, but now my path seems more clear. Please reach out if you’re interested in these projects too, I’d love to collaborate!

Among Inuit communities, babies are traditionally carried on their mother’s back during the first years of life. To keep both warm in Arctic conditions, mothers wear an Amauti — a parka designed specifically for Babywearing, with a built-in pouch in the back where the baby rests safely and close to the body.

Different places, same instinct for closeness

Babies are born with primitive reflexes that help them connect with and respond to the world around them.

The plantar grasp reflex — those tiny toes curling around a finger — is thought to be linked to babies’ instinct to cling to their caregiver, the same way baby apes cling to their mother’s fur. 

And even though humans have evolved beyond fur, it’s  a reminder that carrying isn’t ‘spoiling’, it’s how babies are wired.

🤍 Babywearing basics 

A few simple things to keep in mind when using a baby carrier (any carrier):

☁️ Knees above bum
Your baby’s legs should be in a spread squat position, with the knees higher than the bum, forming an “M” shape.

☁️ Natural back curve 
 A baby’s spine naturally forms a gentle curve. Their back should not be flat, but slightly rounded for comfort.

☁️ Airways clear 
Your baby’s airways should always be clear. Nothing should cover their face, and you should be able to see them at all times

☁️ Close enough to kiss. 
You should be able to kiss your baby’s head. A baby too low may lead to discomfort and back pain.

☁️ Don’t forget to actually kiss 
As much as you want ! Carrying your baby is a beautiful way to bond and stay close 🤍

If a recipe tells you to sauté onions and garlic together for the same amount of time, ignore it!

Onions need time to soften and brown, but garlic cooks incredibly quickly and if it burns, it turns bitter.

Instead, sauté the onions first until they are softened (5ish mins), THEN add the garlic, and sauté for only 30 seconds to a minute. You’ll know it’s good to go when it becomes fragrant.

Then add any other ingredients your recipe calls for!￼

Exception to the rule is if the onions and garlic cook at a very low heat and they are stirred very frequently. Even then, I still would separate them out.￼

Here’s a very obscure piece of Beatles history. Elephant’s Memory was a hard rock band out of NYC in the early 70s. They were also John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s back up band for several years and appeared on some of John’s earlier solo albums. John & Yoko produced their 1972 album, and John even appears on several tracks on guitar and vocals. The album was released on The Beatles Apple records. It’s never been released on CD and is currently out of print. Great stuff and a good example of early hard rock. Very cool album. #vinylcollection #johnlennon #applerecords #1972 #elephantsmemoryband #elephantsmemoryplasticonoband

🎂Happy 1st Birthday Philip Patrick🎂 …Well that was the quickest year of my life! I can’t believe you’ve been here a year my son! Thank you for making me a Mommy, you are the greatest gift ever! #paddymac #firstbirthday @geoffmacmillan

348 days Philip has been alive and finally today we got the answer I’ve wanted from my 20 week scan…it’s not a yes he will have a normal body but for now he can be a normal little baby. ♥️ we can finally plan our days and months ahead of time and not live in fear of the next PCH trip. In his short life my little man has had: 4 operations, too many scans to count, 1 nuclear test, 2 infections, 1 UTI, 3 internal catheters, 9 nights in hospital and he has dealt with it all like an absolute champ 💪 he still has a slightly difficult road ahead but for now all that King Eddies and Perth Children’s Hospital have done for him has paid off. I could not be more proud of my baby and how he has dealt with all this, even if his mother has felt the deepest of darkness in these times. I’m such an anxious person but my Paddy makes me so calm and we just “chuck it in the f**k bucket and get on with it”. The thing is about spending so much god damn time in a children’s hospital is, that if truely humbles you, there is always someone worse off than you and be kind. I am so thankful to live in Australia and receive the best healthcare for me and my son. *this is not a sympathy post. I just want to document my sons incredible journey* #renalbaby #perthchildrenshospital #kingeddies #paddymac #hope #love #motherandson @geoffmacmillan

Sometimes you just need to eat a whole cabbage. 🥬Cabbage is having its moment as the veggie of the year and honestly, we get it. It’s naturally affordable, incredibly versatile, and when you make it like THIS? Absolutely addictive. Toasted sesame oil, grated garlic, ground sesame seeds, and a little chicken powder is all it takes to make a bowl you will NOT stop eating. 
Here’s the full recipe:

Addictive Cabbage
½ large head green cabbage, cubed
2 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds, ground
3 cloves garlic, grated
1½ tsp chicken powder
½ tsp salt
2 Tbsp toasted sesame oil

Wash and dry cabbage, then cut into bite-sized cubes. Grind sesame seeds until sandy. Add everything to a bowl, toss, and lightly squeeze once or twice to help absorb the seasoning. Taste and adjust salt as needed. That’s it!

1 cup finely chopped dill pickles
1 cup shredded cheddar 
2-3 tbsp pickle juice
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp onion powder
1 tsp dried dill

Unpopular Opinion: You SHOULDN’T wash your chicken! 🙅🏼‍♀️

Rinsing raw chicken just splashes bacteria around your sink, counters, dishes… you. 🤢 It increases the risk for cross contamination and does NOTHING to improve the texture, flavor, or moisture content.

The only thing that will kill bacteria is HEAT!

To properly and safely cook your chicken:
Pat dry, season or marinate, and cook until your chicken reaches an internal temp of 165°F 🌡️

If you don’t want to spend the rest of your night sanitizing the entire kitchen, DON’T WASH YOUR CHICKEN ❌

Everyone talks about burnout like it is a personal weakness.
At The Burnout Breakdown, we know it is often a workplace issue, a nervous system issue, and a recovery issue.

So many people are mentally checked out long before they ever stop showing up physically. They are exhausted, overwhelmed, emotionally detached, and running on survival mode while still answering emails, hitting deadlines, and pretending they are okay.

That is where we come in.

The Burnout Breakdown exists to educate workers about burnout, mental health, workplace stress, and the rights people often do not realize they have — including FMLA protections for qualifying mental health conditions.

Because recovery should not begin only after a breakdown.

FMLA can provide eligible employees with protected time away from work for serious health conditions, including mental health challenges like anxiety, depression, chronic stress, and burnout-related conditions. Yet so many workers avoid getting help because they feel guilty, afraid, or convinced they just need to “push through.”

We are here to change that conversation.

You deserve rest before your body forces it.
You deserve support before you completely collapse.
And you deserve to know that protecting your mental health is not failure — it is healthcare.

The goal is not just surviving work.
It is building a life where your well-being matters too.

The pressure to keep performing.

It affects your mind, your body, your relationships, your patience, your identity, and eventually your ability to feel like yourself at all.

Healing starts when you stop treating your exhaustion like a personality trait and start paying attention to what is draining you.

Awareness is the first step.
Boundaries are the next.
Recovery is possible.

Sometimes your nervous system has been trained to brace for the week before it even begins.

You start checking emails early.
You can’t fully relax.
Your mind races while your body stays exhausted.
And somehow Monday already feels heavy before it even arrives.

That’s not laziness. That’s survival mode.

When work constantly feels unsafe, overwhelming, or emotionally draining, your body starts preparing for stress before it happens. Over time, even small routines can trigger tension, panic, or exhaustion.

You deserve more than constantly recovering from your life.
You deserve support, rest, and a routine that doesn’t make your body feel under attack.

Your body whispers before it screams.

The headaches. The tight chest. The exhaustion that sleep doesn’t fix. The panic attacks, stomach issues, brain fog, and constant fatigue… those aren’t random inconveniences. They can be signs that your nervous system has been carrying too much for too long.

Burnout doesn’t just live in your mind. It shows up in your body, your energy, your focus, and your ability to keep pushing through the day.

So if your body is trying to tell you something, listen before it forces you to.

Rest is not weakness. Support is not failure. And protecting your mental health is just as important as protecting your physical health.

The “Sunday Scaries” aren’t always just stress.

Sometimes it’s your body reacting to a routine that’s been draining you for too long. That pit in your stomach, the exhaustion before the week even starts, the urge to avoid everything instead of logging in… those are signs your nervous system may be overwhelmed, not lazy.

We’ve normalized dreading Monday so much that we forget to ask why it feels so heavy in the first place.

You deserve support before burnout turns into a breakdown.
You deserve rest before you hit your limit.
And you deserve a life that doesn’t make you fear the start of every week.

The weekend isn’t just a break from work. It’s a reset for you.

Somewhere along the way, we started measuring our worth by how much we do, how productive we are, how much we push through. But you’re more than your output. You’re a person who needs rest, joy, and space to just exist.

Slowing down isn’t falling behind. Stepping back isn’t quitting. Taking time for yourself is how you come back stronger, clearer, and more like you again.

So this weekend, don’t just “recover” from the week. Reconnect with yourself.

Anxious days don’t need perfect solutions. They need small, steady steps.

When everything feels overwhelming, your job isn’t to fix your whole life. It’s to regulate your nervous system and focus on what’s right in front of you.

Do one thing you’ve been avoiding.
Let go of what you can’t control.
Narrow your focus to the next hour.

And when your body feels on edge, support it. Slow down, reset, and give yourself space before making big decisions.

You don’t have to win the whole day. Just meet yourself where you are.

Relational marketing challenges people’s comfort zones.

you can do your best, love well, 
show up with a pure heart
and still become the villain in someone else’s story.

but because of what they need to believe to make sense of their own narrative.

There are moments in life where things don’t unfold the way you truly thought they would. 🥹

Plans you were excited about… experiences you had your heart set on… and then suddenly, something unexpected shifts it all.

I recently experienced a quiet season and part of that is because I was walking through some unknowns behind the scenes. Things that were out of my control… things I didn’t fully understand at the time… so I chose to pause, pray, and process before speaking on it.

In 15 days, I was supposed to be heading to Hawaii with a few of my partners for a trip that I earned… and that’s no longer where I’m going.

Due to some unexpected circumstances, that opportunity was taken off the table.

And while that felt really heavy, I found myself leaning into gratitude. I’ve had the honor of experiencing Hawaii multiple times in my life… and that perspective helped soften the disappointment more than I expected.

But more than that, this season has reminded me of something deeper…

Sometimes the redirection is just as intentional as the original plan.

So instead of holding onto what won’t be happening, I chose to pivot. To make a new plan. One that still allows me to step away, breathe, and spend meaningful time by the ocean… just in a different place than I expected.

Because I trust this:

God doesn’t waste anything.

Not the unknown seasons.
Not the pauses.
Not even the disappointments.

He uses it all to shape us into who we’re being called to become.

So no… it may not look like what I had planned.

But it will still be rest.
It will still be meaningful.
It will still be exactly what I need.

And maybe that’s the reminder for someone else today…

Just because it didn’t go how you planned doesn’t mean it went wrong.

Trust the redirection.
There is still beauty waiting for you there. 🤍
