When I was 19, I briefly worked in a nursery in Thornton Heath. It's not there anymore, but that's a story for a different time. I was working in the preschool room and got the children ready to go out to the garden attached to the building.

When I realised I'd misread the time and it wasn't our turn yet I apologised to the children for getting them excited and told them I'd read them a story after they went and put their coats and shoes back. While they did that my room leader pulled me aside and quietly told me not to apologise to children, because it made adults look bad and the children had to believe adults were to be obeyed without question. She didn't phrase it exactly like that, but that was the general gist.

Now that just didn't sit right with me. I remembered being a child and noticing when adults floundered and fell back on "because I said so". It made me respect them less, not more. So while I was too young and anxious to contradict her at the time I made a silent decision to always apologise to a child when I made a mistake.

Nearly 10 years later I can now confidently say I made the right decision. In every nursery I worked in after that, and afterwards when I started nannying, I made a point to admit and apologise to the children in my care if I made a mistake. They quickly realised I'd treat them fairly if they did the same, and many children confided in me things they wouldn't tell coworkers who were (let's be polite here) slightly more high strung. 

This decision also changed how I interacted with adults during and outside of work - not just coworkers but friends, family, and loved ones. A lot of issues that could have become arguments instead became discussions about our values and boundaries. Things that could have become deep seated resentment instead became opportunities to explain our viewpoints and be vulnerable with each other. It strengthened my relationships and reinforced people's trust in me because they knew I'd admit when I was wrong instead of refusing to engage. 

So thank you to that room leader. You were wrong, but you provided me with an opportunity to be better as a friend, a partner, and a caregiver.

Let's talk about our surroundings! 

When I first started nannying, I didn't really know what to do while we were waiting for a bus to go somewhere. I was used to nurseries where there were always activities on offer and resources that could be fetched with ease, and floundered for ways to entertain the small child I was looking after. I'd sing, offer paper and pens to draw and colour, we'd play imagination games with any toys we happened to have on us, but all those got old quite quickly and I found myself at a loss.

But then I realised there's an infinite source of things to do at the bus stop! We could watch the cars go past and name their colours, look at the map at the bus stop and see where we were then trace it to where we were going, even practice climbing and balancing on the bench (if no one was sitting there)!

It was surprising how many insightful and engaging conversations could spring from a random occurrence like someone running for the bus or seeing a lorry deliver wares to a nearby shop. Letting the child take the lead, I found myself asking questions I'd never have thought of otherwise, like "What kind of stone are paving stones made from?" and "How does the bus lean over to make it easier for passengers to get on?".

And from these conversations new interests formed - one child became enamored with "second decker" buses and so we planned special outings making sure we could take a double decker. We found difficulty in taking the collapsible buggy up the stairs, so we made a new plan to walk to the bus stop without the buggy and celebrated our mutual resilience and problem solving abilities. He started insisting we didn't take the buggy on every outing and accepted that he would have to carry his "packpack", learning responsibility, spacial awareness, and improving his physical endurance and awareness of time in relation to our walking speed. 

All that from a stray thought at a bus stop.

Hello! I'm Elliott, your friendly neighbourhood nanny. I'm 27 and I've worked in childcare for ten years - starting out with 6 months as an au pair in Germany, then 6 years working in nurseries until 3 years ago when I branched out into freelance nannying.

My approach to childcare is simple. At the root, I aim to be the adult I would have needed as a child in any given situation. If a child is angry, I listen to that anger. If they're sad, I provide comfort. If they're scared, I encourage them to face their fears. If they're confident, I cheer them on. If they're happy, I celebrate with them. I adapt to their mood while maintaining core values of kindness, self respect, and fair play in our interactions with the world.

I believe that every experience is an opportunity for growth and development, and I'm excited to explore those opportunities with you and your children.

If only every girl was taught this growing up, I truly believe we wouldn’t see the level of fertility confusion and complications we’re seeing.

Here’s how to start understanding ovulation:

1️⃣ Pay attention when you go to the bathroom.

As you walk there, what do you SENSE at your vulva? Dry? Damp? Wet? Slippery? 

Your vulva is highly sensitive, when you tune in you will be able to feel changes.

Then check what you SEE when you pull your underwear down. Is there cervical mucus? Dry? Tacky? Creamy? Stretchy? Slippery? This is showing you real-time info about your hormones.

As oestrogen rises as you near ovulation, mucus becomes more watery that’s what we’re tracking. Each day, write down the most fertile sign you notice.

2️⃣ Don’t count days and assume you know when you ovulate.

Every woman’s fertile window is different. Not everyone ovulates on day 14. Even with a 28-day cycle, ovulation could be day 11… or day 16. Charting your signs gives clarity on YOUR unique window. 

NOTE: The rhythm method is inaccurate because it ignores stress, illness, travel, sleep — this is where most apps fail. I do not teach the rhythm method.

3️⃣ Look for patterns.

After a few months, your data will show you your unique fertile and non fertile windows. This is how we time intercourse accurately…. not by guessing, but through informed body literacy.

The problem isn’t the foods, but what modern processing and dietary trends have done to them.

These staple foods don’t need to be feared, butter especially is a nutrient dense super fertility food.

The bog is the oldest organic landscape in Estonia, reaching in some cases up to 10 000 years of age. At the very beginning, this peat accumulation landscape does not have a significant effect on plants. After millennia or two, the peat layer becomes thicker and filters out more demanding plants. The last stage is called a bog or raised bog. Here you can see a lot of bog pools or lakes inside this huge organic sponge. The water in the bogs is acidic because of the sphagnum moss.
Water is really pure and drinkable, but won't take your thirst away (remember, no minerals/nutrients!). That's how @visitestonia introduced the bogs. Allow me to add, they are one of my favorite choices for swimming.

My birth story 🤍

Pregnancy was nothing like I imagined. The first 4 months, I was sick all day, every day. I could barely get out of bed, and sometimes my legs would tremble so much I’d fall trying to stand. I got pregnant while living in the Dolomites, in a tiny village in Italy called Agordo, far away from family and support, with only my husband by my side.

Eventually, we made the difficult decision for me to move back to Montreal to stay with my mom while my husband moved to Turin for work. My mom took such good care of me, and I’ll always be grateful for her. During pregnancy, I became anemic, struggled with very low blood pressure, and had to call an ambulance twice after nearly fainting. I thought I’d stay active throughout pregnancy, but even workouts made me dangerously dizzy.

My husband came back two weeks before my due date, and I was induced so he could be there for the birth. On December 11 I had a stripping and on December 12, contractions started at 4am. The pain was immediate and intense. By the time we drove to the hospital, I felt like I couldn’t survive the ride. I asked for the epidural the second I walked in 😅

I dilated incredibly fast to 9cm… but then came the hardest part. I pushed for 4–5 hours. The epidural only worked on one side of my body, and I was close to an emergency C-section. Then my doctor looked at me and said: “Sabine, your baby is in critical condition. You have to push hard now. You can do it.”

And somehow, I did. 17 hours later.

I’ll never forget her encouragement in that moment. My baby was finally here 🤍 I only held her for a few seconds before they had to rush her away for oxygen for the next 5 hours. Having her taken from me broke my heart. A few hours later, I asked the nurses to wheel me to her. She was crying in her incubator, and all I wanted was to hold my baby.

The hardest and most beautiful day of my life.

Just a rare day I woke up before her and was already caffeinated 😅

Ever since giving birth and moving to a new country, my nervous system has felt constantly overstimulated. Lately, the stress of job searching has made me feel stuck and blocked in so many ways. A friend recently told me that she went for a drive to clear her head on a bad day, but realized that walking made her feel even better. It reminded me why movement is such a powerful way to regulate our nervous system. We see this so clearly in children, yet we often forget that the same principle applies to adults.

When we spend too much time in our heads, we disconnect from our bodies. The simplest way to reconnect is to move — to remind our mind that we have a body, and to rebalance our energy through that awareness. Today, after feeling discouraged about putting effort into job hunting without seeing results, I got up and danced to a song that resonated with how I felt in that moment. You can tell I have blockages in the way I move. My hips ache, my pelvic floor still hasn’t fully recovered, and although I used to dance and work out regularly, I haven’t moved my hips in a long time. But it still felt good — really good. This is your reminder to move your body, in any way, any form that speaks to you, to release energy that is stuck.

I only realised how unequal we still are after becoming a mom. Our work is tremendously valuable. Raising a human is the most difficult yet most rewarding job, but the patriarchal system decided otherwise. In Canada, you get one year of mat leave paid 70% of your salary the first six months and 55% the last six months. In the US you get 12 weeks and in Brussels it’s about the same. Mothers told me they were threatened to loose their job if they took longer mat leaves. We need men to advocate for us as well. We are mothers, we are creators of life. We hold superpowers.

When I was a kid, I stayed outdoors until sunset. Rode my bike to places and distances no young girl should travel alone. I played with stray cats. Loved to dig in the dirt for worms. Helped the neighbors garden. Took any opportunity available through Girl Scouts and church to camp. I found peace in the outdoors because my home environment had always been toxic. Being outdoors was where I found peace. The outdoors has always felt like home. 

I remember one time at band camp…No, sorry. Wrong story... 
I remember one time at church camp I found a baby toad. I tried and tried to catch it. Wasn’t happening. A bunch of kids were near by and one caught it for me. I was happy to have the little guy, but I wanted to catch it on my own. I tried on and off over the years. I cld never catch one. 

Fast fwd through life when I was disconnected from nature until I found rockhounding.

Then it happened. While out collecting I saw the cutest toad. No, this wasn’t the first time I had seen a toad since I was a kid nor while collecting. It was just the right time. I wanted to catch it so bad. I was with a friend and he encouraged me to catch it. Sounds silly, right? How hard is it to catch a frog or toad? I had convinced myself that I cldnt do it. Idk if I was afraid that I’d smush the little guy while attempting to catch it or if I harbored defeat since attempting as a child? I think I said I cldnt do it like 3x. Lol But the encouragement was enough to convince me that I cld. And I did. 

This was the moment I caught a toad for the first time! Again, I know this sounds silly, but it’s something I’ve always wanted to do. And it brought me immense joy. 
I will always remember this moment. 

It’s the little things that sometimes give us the greatest joy. It’s the little things y’all. 
The little things.🐸

❗It is past time that we tell y'all more about our incredible Chef Brooke Adams (she/they).

For 11+ years, Brooke has worked across the Asheville food scene, receiving mentorship from beloved chefs like Terri Terrell of Homegrown and Utopian Seed, Luis Martinez of Tequio Foods, and Michelle Bailey of Smokey Park Supper Club.

They cut their teeth as sous chef to Eric Morris at the Funkatorium & Cultura, helping earn Cultura a spot as a semifinalist in the James Beard Foundation's Best New Restaurant category. Around Helene, Brooke transitioned to the team run by their work wife, Mallory Foster, now Executive Chef at Rhubarb. Brooke chose to leave finer dining for Finest to focus on food that their farmer partners can afford to eat regularly.

Brooke grew up in these mountains in a family of restaurant people, and they’ve stayed in WNC to build a life with their wife and four(!) dogs. They found a second home in the kitchen, among other (self-described) misfits working towards a common goal. Brooke cooks to make people try things they’ve never had or think they won’t like. And they became a chef because they are a leader who invests in the growth of everyone around them. Both of these miracles happen at Finest every single day!

Hopefully next time you eat at Finest, you'll notice Brooke's unique touch; from lunch specials to cozy handmade pastas to fresh market salads, their focus on seasonality, commitment to using the whole plant/animal, and  talent for balancing flavors and textures always shine through. ✨

We love you Brooke and we are so grateful for you!

Most workplaces say the right things about family. The test is what happens when a child gets sick, a parent lands in the hospital, or you become the one everyone leans on overnight.

Here's the practical part worth knowing: FMLA isn't only for your own illness. Eligible employees can take up to 12 weeks of job-protected leave in a 12-month period to care for a spouse, child, or parent with a serious health condition — and that leave can often be taken intermittently, in blocks, rather than all at once.

To be eligible you generally need to have worked for your employer about 12 months and at least 1,250 hours, at a worksite with 50+ employees nearby.

If caregiving is colliding with your job, you may have more protected options than you've been told.

A full calendar can hide a real problem. When there's no gap to breathe — let alone to handle a medical appointment or recover from treatment — the schedule itself becomes part of what's wearing you down.

Here's a practical option a lot of employees miss: FMLA leave doesn't have to be one long stretch away from work. When it's medically necessary, it can be taken intermittently — a few hours for recurring appointments, a reduced schedule during treatment, or occasional days for flare-ups of a chronic condition.

That means you may be able to protect the time you need for your health without stepping away from your role entirely.

About 4 months before getting pregnant -> 4 months pregnant -> 4 months post partum

One of my fears while pregnant, was not getting back into shape afterwards. I realize that should be the LEAST of my worries during my post partum recovery, but I loved my pre-pregnancy body. I worked hard for it, I took care of myself and to be honest, I felt like I took it for granted.

Pregnancy does ALL sorts of things, inside and out, that all the personal experience stories in the world won't prepare you for. Everyone has a different journey. I was so ill that I ended up giving up the gym, eating alot of white refined carb foods and drinking sweet drinks that I wasn't use to consuming. This went on for most of my pregnancy. I felt like I ruined everything I've been working towards the past 7 years.

Little did I know, all those years of discipline, knowledge, and muscle gains would come right back to me. Post partum is rough, but the pregnancy cloud eventually fades. This is when I started to see not my old self, but a new version of me.

Slowly, I'm learning to love this new version of my body. Do I still reminisce about pre-pregnancy Courtney? Sure. Am I sad about my booty fading away with every breastfeeding session? Yes, i am 😅 Truth be told, even in my best shape, my stomach was never that flat, so why worry so much about it now? I realize that in this new stage of life, I have an opportunity to really work on myself and set new goals. I get to appreciate how strong my body really is and not just from an outside esthetic point of view.

My body grew a whole ass human, birthed that human, and now I get to show up for her and myself in a whole new way. There will always be different stages of life and habits, goals and routines must evolve with those stages. So here I am, feeling strong in my mom era. Taking it one day at a time.

Before baby, they were our babies.

Preeclampsia Awareness Day

My preeclampsia story started the day after my baby shower. I ended up in the ER with severe right shoulder pain—something I had been told just two weeks prior was anxiety by my OBGYN. It turned out to be something much more serious, preeclampsia. I was induced and delivered my baby 6 weeks early for both of our safety. This is resulted in a NICU stay, and several complications.

So many women have a similar story—and for some, it doesn’t even start until after birth. Postpartum preeclampsia is real.

Know the signs. Trust your body. Speak up early and often. You are not being dramatic—you are advocating for your life and your baby’s life.

Having a baby is the biggest blessing I have ever experienced. My child is truly a gift from above. But dang… postpartum is HARD, and no one really prepares you for it.

It’s like an initiation into the mom club — where “you don’t know until you know,” and now you KNOW but somehow you still feel completely isolated.

The pressure society — and honestly even medical professionals — place on women to “bounce back” is overwhelming. That 6-week appointment comes and suddenly you’re cleared to go back to life, cleared to exercise, cleared to resume normal activities, cleared to have sex… expected to be the person you were before giving birth.

But you aren’t that person anymore.
And that’s not a bad thing.

There’s so much information, so many opinions, so many voices telling moms what they should be doing. Who do you trust? Who do you listen to?

There’s a quote that says, “To know even one life has breathed easier because you have lived, this is to have succeeded.”

My fourth trimester experience was brutal.

Don’t get me wrong — I was beyond excited to finally have my baby on this side of the womb. But because of complications, I was completely unprepared physically, mentally, emotionally… heck, I barely even had anything for a baby yet.

I found myself at the hospital being told I had to deliver for my safety and baby’s safety, and I hadn’t even brushed my teeth that day — let alone packed a hospital bag.

I want my story, and the things I wish someone had told me, to encourage you. I want to feel like a friend during that 2 a.m. feed, to share a laugh.  Maybe to remind you your experience is valid, shared, and more common than people talk about.

I want to take what I’ve learned from 10 years as a nurse — mixed with my own postpartum experience — and help educate women on the things no one tells you about the fourth trimester.

So here we go.
Welcome to Fourth Trimester Truth.

Hi friends! Just wanted to do a reintroduction post with the fresh flower season getting ready to kick off next month!

My name is Sara (she/her) and I run Freckle Twins' Garden under the strict supervision of the Freckle Twins, Max and Mochi. With a bit of help from my husband, @gregorielrobles . (We will be celebrating our 10th wedding anniversary this August)!
.
We moved to Waynesville in 2022, closing on the farm that April. That first season, I grew almost 100 dahlias in grow bags and sold them to local florists while we worked on building the raised beds in what is now our flower field. 
.
Since then, we've grown thousands of flowers without any chemical inputs or ever utilizing a tiller. 
.
In the years leading up to us buying the farm, I worked on other farms, started a market garden (Freckle Twins' Garden 1.0), attended seminars and conferences and classes, read all the books, listened to all the podcasts, and all in all just tried to absorb AALLL the information. I still do. 
.
In all that learning and all that trial and error, I fell in love with the concept of sustainable agriculture. Sustainable for the environment, and sustainable for the people involved. Working with nature instead of against, and working with my disabilities rather than against them. 
.
I love sharing the information I've learned over the years with anyone and everyone who will listen (I'm really exciting at dinner parties since all I want to talk about is vermicomposting and regionally adapted land race seed trials). I believe with enough determination and patience, anyone can have a green thumb. You just might want to have a good composting system set up first to recycle all the plants you're going to kill. 🤪
.
We are members of the Diversity Business Directory through @ideaofhaywood because we welcome marginalized communities with open arms. 
.
So with every flower purchase, you can rest assured they are 100% chemical free, local (my front yard), and supporting a dream of sharing these beautiful, high quality flowers with the world.

Some days before getting started on school work I like to wake up my brain with a quick painting. Today that looked like messy mark making. No structure, no rhyme or reason, just making marks on the page and letting my brain relax.
.
I've never actually used these watercolor crayons before in a painting. They were gifted to me when I was 9 by a professional watercolorist who took a shine to me when I met her. All I remember of her is the impression of her being short and petite with snow white hair and a no-nonsense countenance. The other thing I remember is how every wall in her home was covered in artwork. I was spellbound by how she captured the heart of the Everglades (we lived in Florida then), the feeling that she had pinned the souls of animals to paper. The egrets, the manatees, the alligators, all seemingly pinned to the walls like butterflies in a shadow box. I don't know how long the grownups spoke, but I was not ready to leave when the time came. I wanted to wander the wilderness of my home in her home forever. She pressed this tin of watercolor crayons and a small travel palette of watercolors into my hands before we left. 
.
The travel palette was lost in one of my many moves over the years, but the crayons remain. I didn't start my watercolor journey until just a few years ago in 2022. The crayons don't work as well as I'm sure they did when they were fresh and new, but the feeling of fated inevitably clings to them. So I'll hold onto them for the memory and as a pseudo museum piece of foreshadowing in my life.
.

😎 Memorial Day weekend marks the unofficial start of grilling season — though, with the temperatures we’ve had earlier this week, you may have been at the grill already! Between the expanse of late spring vegetables, hearty pasture-raised meats, and delicious dinner accoutrement found at market, shopping local makes celebrating the long weekend easy. 

🥩 Pasture-Raised Meats: The FRESHFARM network is full of dedicated livestock farmers who prioritize animal wellness, seasonal recipes, and the freshest protein possible. Not sure what to get? Make sure to check in with the livestock farmers at your market! Honorable mentions to the Jalapeño Cheddar Jumbo All-Beef Hot Dogs from Country Vittles and the Pork Bratwurst from Smith Meadows Meats.
📍Find @countryvittles_ch at Columbia Heights (Sat) and Uptown.
📍Find @smithmeadowsfarm at Arlington and Dupont Circle.

🫕 Dips: The perfect vehicle for farmers market bread and snappy veg alike, dips are great contributions to a potluck table! Try out a FRESHFARM recipe like Herb White Bean Dip or Roasted Beet Hummus — or make things easy by shopping with the professionals.
📍Find @doubledipfood at Columbia Heights (Sat).
📍Find @dipbydipmaker at Arlington and Dupont Circle.

🥖 Quick Sides: Even the yummiest of grilled foods need some supporting cast, like carbs! Shop high-quality local grain inputs like spelt and whole-wheat flour from the Mid-Atlantic Grain Stand. Keep things simple with a mix, like Grapewood Farm's Cornbread Mix or Deep Roots Milling’s Acorn Cornbread Mix (both available at the Grain Stand).
📍Find the Mid-Atlantic Grain Stand at Downtown Silver Spring, Dupont Circle, and Mosaic (5/24).

🍄‍🟫 While you’re shopping, don’t forget the delicious grilled vegetable options at market right now, like asparagus, mushrooms, spring onions, potatoes, and more! We’re entering some of the last few weekends when a visit to the market isn’t a sweat-inducing activity, so don’t wait; we’ll see you there. 😎

@twinspringsfruitfarm has been growing in the rolling hills of Adams County, Pennsylvania since 1979. Today, the family farm produces gorgeous fruit and vegetables for 20 Mid-Atlantic farmers markets, including one of spring’s most distinctive crops: rhubarb. 🩷

❓ Though often treated like a fruit in pies and jams, rhubarb is actually a perennial vegetable known for its tart flavor and multicolor stalks. In the Mid-Atlantic, rhubarb thrives in cooler spring temperatures and can stay productive year after year.

“We grow about an acre and a half of rhubarb,” shared Jesse King of Twin Springs Fruit Farm. “This year, we planted some newer red varieties because our shoppers want the rich red stalks." Rhubarb prefers well-drained soil, plenty of nutrients, and consistent weed management. “They do not like to have wet feet,” King said, noting that raised beds and compost-rich soil help keep plants healthy.

Unlike annual crops, rhubarb plants can take several years to become fully productive, but healthy crowns can continue yielding for 10 to 20 years with proper care. Growers also remove flower stalks throughout the season so the plants can direct energy back into foliage and root development for future harvests.

➡️ At the market, rhubarb’s short season makes it a spring favorite for recipes like our crisp bars, compote, or a simple crumble (with ice cream). Link in bio to explore our recipes. Shop for tender stalks and enjoy it while it lasts!

Not sure what to do with the asparagus you picked up at market? 💚 This vibrant soup celebrates a seasonal favorite at its peak. Silky smooth, it comes together in under an hour and tastes like pure spring!

Save this recipe at the link IN OUR BIO!

INGREDIENTS:
- 3 lbs asparagus
- 2 leeks, white and light green parts only, or 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 sprigs of green garlic, or 3 cloves of garlic
- 4 tablespoons butter, divided
- ¾ teaspoon salt, plus more as needed
- ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock
- ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley (optional)
- 1 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish (optional)
- ½ cup chopped fresh tender herbs, such as dill or chive
- Garnish: reserved asparagus tips, chopped herbs, heavy cream

DIRECTIONS: 
1. Soak the asparagus in a large bowl of water with the tips facing down to dislodge any sand and soil. Remove, rinse thoroughly, and snap off the woody ends. Chop into 1-inch pieces, reserving about ⅓ of the tips.
2. If using leeks, soak them in a bowl of water after chopping to dislodge any dirt.
3. Roughly chop the green garlic or garlic cloves.
4. In a large stockpot, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the reserved asparagus tips, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and sauté for about 5 minutes, until bright green and tender-crisp. Set aside.
5. Melt the remaining butter in the same pot. Add the leeks or onion, ¾ teaspoon salt, and pepper, and sauté until softened, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the garlic and chopped asparagus and sauté for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
6. Add the stock, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes. Stir in the parsley, if using—it will brighten the finished soup’s color.
7. Using an immersion blender or a standard blender, blend the soup until smooth. If using a standard blender, let the soup cool slightly, then blend in batches, venting the lid to allow steam to escape. Return the soup to the pot, stir in the heavy cream if using, and gently reheat.
8. Ladle into bowls and serve topped with a drizzle of heavy cream, fresh herbs, and the reserved asparagus tips.

It's MOREL TIME! 🍄‍🟫

🌱Spring in the Mid-Atlantic brings a handful of highly anticipated seasonal foods, and for mushroom lovers, few are more exciting than MORELS. These wild mushrooms are known for their honeycomb-like caps, earthy flavor, and extremely short growing season. If you spot them at market this month, don’t wait too long, they may disappear just as quickly as they arrived.

This season, we’re excited to welcome @manchesterfungi to the FRESHFARM network. While the farm specializes in cultivated mushrooms year-round, managing partner Iain Davis notes that they bring foraged morels to market each spring.

“Morels are notoriously difficult to grow as they usually form symbiotic relationships with trees,” Davis explains. “They appear for a very short window each year, and while certain species can be more present, they remain rare.”

In the Mid-Atlantic, morels are often found in deciduous hardwood forests near dying elm, ash, and apple trees. Old orchards can be especially productive spots for experienced foragers. Their arrival typically coincides with warming spring soil temperatures around 50 degrees.

If you bring some home from market, Davis recommends soaking morels briefly in salted water before cooking. “Simply sauté them in butter and garlic until they begin to get crispy, then season with salt and pepper,” he says. “Being from Maryland, we also love to add Old Bay!”

If you’ve ever stood at a farmers market wondering when to show up, what’s actually a good deal, or how people seem to know exactly what to buy, this is worth a read.

The Washington Post just published a guide to being a smarter farmers market shopper, featuring experts from across the country, including Cat Oakar, Executive Director of FRESHFARM. (And if the images and videos look familiar, that’s because most of them were captured at FRESHFARM Arlington Market!)

It covers the basics people tend to learn the hard way: go early if you want full selection, later if you’re hoping for deals, and always do a lap before you commit. It also gets into the less obvious stuff, like how to think about pricing in a way that reflects what it actually takes to grow food and why “imperfect” produce is often the best value.

The best piece of advice? Talk to your farmers and producers. Ask what’s tasting best that day, what’s just come in, or what they’d take home themselves. That back-and-forth is where much of the value of market shopping actually lives.

Ramps are almost gone! Many farmers are done foraging for the season, but we confirmed that @chicanoSol still has some (find them at Dupont Circle this Sunday). 

Grab the last of the season to make this versatile okonomiyaki. Okonomiyaki is a savory Japanese pancake traditionally made of flour, meat, cabbage, and other ingredients, cooked on a griddle and topped with various condiments. 

This 🌱 RAMP okonomiyaki features ramps, Brussels sprouts, and carrots, making it the perfect dish to bridge from winter veggies to the first tender crops of spring. 

Okonomiyaki are designed to be flexible, so feel free to throw in whatever crunchy veggies are lingering in your fridge (the season's first asparagus would be a welcome addition!) along with the ramps that give it a garlicky, springy kick.

(Special thanks to @alysekstokes, who developed and submitted this recipe!) 

Save this recipe at the LINK IN OUR BIO! 🔗

INGREDIENTS:
- 2 eggs
- 75g all purpose flour (about ⅔ cup)
- 75ml water (about ⅓ cup)
- a generous pinch of kosher salt
- 1 bunch ramps, chopped with a few greens set aside for garnish
- 1 cup shredded Brussels sprouts
- ½ cup shredded or shaved carrots
- 2 tsp neutral cooking oil

DIRECTIONS:
1. Place the eggs, flour, water, and salt in a medium bowl and whisk until there are no lumps remaining. You should have a smooth batter with the consistency of heavy cream.
2. Add the ramps, Brussels sprouts, and carrots. Using a rubber spatula, fold the veggies into the batter until well coated.
3. Heat the oil in a 10” nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Pour the batter into the pan, pressing to help evenly distribute the veggies. 
4. Cook for 3-4 minutes or until lightly browned on the first side. (You can gently lift the edge of the pancake with your spatula and peek underneath to confirm.)
5. Carefully flip the okonomiyaki over and cook on the other side for 2-3 more minutes, or until light golden brown.
6. Slide the finished okonomiyaki onto a plate and drizzle with your choice of sauces. Scatter the reserved ramp greens over the top to garnish.

We caught up with Gonzalo Diaz Jr. of Diaz Berries and Veggies in Westmoreland County, VA, where the team has been growing fruit and vegetables since 2012. This year, they are tending over 4,000 strawberry plants that were set in the ground last fall and carefully brought out of winter dormancy to produce now.

“Once strawberries start coming in, us farmers know the sweet side of farming is here and the rest of summer crops are right behind them,” Gonzalo shared.

Strawberry season is short but Diaz stretches it by growing multiple varieties. Sweet Charlies are in now (sweet, juicy, and best eaten fast), Festival berries are up next (a bit firmer), and Ruby Junes will round out the season in a few weeks, keeping fresh berries at market into early June.

And freshness matters: “When we're bringing berries to farmers markets, we do all the picking the day before to make sure that they are as fresh as possible.”

Beyond berries, you’ll also find arugula, asparagus, chives, cilantro, elephant garlic, leeks, lettuce, parsley, salad mix, and scallions at their stand.

🌎 What does Earth Month look like at FoodPrints? It looks like this.

Last week, during DCPS spring break, our team came together for four days to completely rebuild the Ludlow-Taylor Elementary school garden — one of our biggest, with 960 square feet of growing space, first constructed back in 2017.

After years of use, the original beds were rotting and needed to be replaced. So our garden team planned every measurement, ordered the lumber, set up a full construction area behind the school, sawed wood to size, assembled raised beds, and hauled a five-foot pile of soil and compost — one wheelbarrow-load at a time — for the new beds to grow many fruit and veggie plants, including strawberries, blackberries, and asparagus.

More than 160 hours of work. Dozens of hands. Coordination with the Ludlow-Taylor PTO. FoodPrints teachers and admin team members. FRESHFARM market staff and volunteers. All showed up and worked hard during an unusually warm week.

"Even though it was hot and the project was a bit daunting in scale, with careful planning, many hands, and persistence, we accomplished this very large project together," notes Beth Bacon, FRESHFARM Education Director. "Now, in this flagship school garden, the beds will be stable and safe for students and will continue to grow many crops year-round for them to learn from, harvest, and eat."

FoodPrints staff put their hearts into their work every day, bringing joyful, hands-on experiences growing, cooking, and eating food together to thousands of Washington, DC, public elementary students each school year. But this project was particularly heartfelt, honoring the memory of Barbara Percival, one of FoodPrints' founders and first teachers, who tended this garden with so much love for so many years. 🫶🏽

🌱 Spring is in full swing, which means one of the most anticipated vegetables has returned to market: asparagus! These fast-growing shoots quickly populate seasonal menus and are a mainstay in springtime cooking.

We caught up with asparagus expert Dana Garner Boyle of @garnersproduce to understand how they grow and reach our tables.

"Here at Garner's, we grow approximately 4 acres of asparagus, with varieties including Jersey Night, Millennium, and Purple Passion. We chose these varieties because they grow and perform well in our growing zone — they are high-yielding with great flavor and tenderness," Dana told us.

Asparagus is a perennial plant with a root system that winters over each year, called a crown. Planting is done in spring by digging furrows about 8 inches deep and laying crowns along the bottom with about a foot of space between plants. "Asparagus rows should be no closer than 3 feet apart," Dana explains. "After the roots are laid in the furrow, they should be covered immediately with 2 to 3 inches of soil," with the trench gradually filled as spears grow into ferns throughout the season.

Because the crown supplies vital nutrients to the shoots, growers must avoid over-harvesting. "Newly planted asparagus should only be harvested for one week in its first cutting year. Once established, we cut for 3 to 4 weeks in the second season, and up to 6 to 8 weeks in following years." This explains the short window we have to enjoy this spring treat! "An asparagus field can produce for 15 to 20 years if conditions are favorable," Dana adds.

Looking for an easy way to prepare these tender spears? Head to the link in bio for a simple FoodPrints recipe for roasted asparagus.

🌱 Ramps are here! 🌱 Ramps are here! 🌱

For a few short weeks each spring, these wild alliums pop up across the Mid-Atlantic, bringing their signature garlicky-onion flavor to market tables. Foraged locally and highly seasonal, ramps are a true taste of spring that doesn't stick around for long!

❓What is foraging?
Foraging is the practice of harvesting food directly from the wild, rather than growing it intentionally. In the Mid-Atlantic, that often means gathering edible plants like ramps, mushrooms, or more from forests, fields, and other natural landscapes.

With ramps, foraging is especially common because they grow naturally in wooded areas with rich, moist soil, conditions that are hard to replicate at scale on farms. Experienced foragers know where to find them and how to harvest carefully, often taking only part of a patch (like a single leaf or a portion of the bulb) so the plants can regenerate year after year.

Spring produce may ~almost~ be upon us, but it's not too late to enjoy the flavors of winter produce in a hearty salad. 💪 Try this FoodPrints French Lentil Salad for an easy and fresh weekday lunch! 

Starting with a base of cooked French lentils, crunchy celery, and sweet dried apples, this salad is finished with a zippy lemon dressing that just gets better with time. 💚

Save the recipe at the link in our bio! 🔗

INGREDIENTS: 
1 cup French lentils (small green lentils, also called Le Puy)
4 cups water
1/4 cup olive oil
2 tablespoons lemon juice
salt and pepper to taste
3/4 cup dried apples, chopped
3/4 cup toasted sunflower seeds
3/4 cup celery, finely chopped

DIRECTIONS: 
1. Gather all the ingredients and equipment. Wash the produce and prepare it as detailed in the ingredients list. When rinsing and draining the lentils, look them over carefully for any small stones.
2. Place the lentils in a pot with the water over medium heat, bring them to a simmer and then reduce heat to low. Cook covered with a lid checking them often to avoid over-cooking.
3. Meanwhile, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Taste and adjust as needed.
4. When the lentils are tender (but not mushy), drain and toss with the dressing and remaining ingredients.
5. Chill salad for at least 30 minutes before serving.

🥬 connect food to farms and their bodies
🔪 build real kitchen skills and independence
👩‍🍳 experience the joy of cooking and eating together
🌱 explore new foods in a supportive, judgment-free space

E.4.T. “Everything for Taurean” a short documentary.

While this doc is on its festival tour I wanted to share some frames of it with you all, this is a project over 3 years of making with director @nisinson and the golden net foundation here in Brooklyn. 

A story of a basketball Player local in Brooklyn who used the game of basketball to bring family, friends, and a community closer together. Before we started filming Taurean sadly had passed away on the basketball court from a heart attack, leaving his new born son and partner, family and community behind. The family and community that he supported and helped so much rallied around his passing and started a tournament to always Remember him, they now seek to change the name of the park to Tauren spears park. 

Thank you to everyone who could be apart of this project. It was such an honor to be able to lens this piece for everyone and help continue Taurean legacy even after his passing. 

Thank you to @jcomfy @sachibahra @jenn.zar @nisinson @meilinbae @arsalaandp any anyone else I am forgetting in this post for helping us on this project. And thank you to @brooklynfilmfestival for showcasing our premiere

Not everyday you can skate at your favorite teams practice facility, go to @the_federal_ftl for happy hour, then back home to watch the #winterclassic - little late and we got blown out but #letsgopanthers!  Lot of hockey left

What can I say.  We are winners.
There’s a lot of hard work involved.
There’s a lot of hatred.
Hardship.  Loss.  Pain.  Doubt.  Disappointment.
All of these things work against the grit of a hockey organization at every level.
I joined as a substitute for #HabanerosHockey.  I didn’t know what impact I would be able to make, but I said I would try my best.  Then I got called up.  Got my sweater.  Played hard.  Didn’t make it all the way that season.
Picked up some friends.  Brought them up with me.  Practiced together.  Drank LOTS of beers together.  Cheered on the @flapanthers together.  Still went to that grind every Sunday.  Paintballers know where I’m coming from.
Then we got cut short.  Again.  I got mad.  Even hostile.  I wanted more out of what I put in.  I asked - nah, @btodhunter would say I demanded - to step up to forward.  I put up some production this season.
But then we hit some brick walls.  Some injuries.  And I was put back where I was needed - on defense.
Sometimes you’re not going to be the man of the hour.  You’re not going to get the touches.  You’re gonna get hurt.  You’re going to lose SOMETHING, if not the game.  But if you do your job, better than others do theirs, you have a shot.  There’s possibilities in the discipline of sports if you never give up.  And after all that - after every time you laced up to skate, pretended you were at a game 7 of the @stanleycup finals and it was all on you, the hours late at night that it was just you and your thoughts on the ice, all the travel, the hangovers, the late nights sometimes, missing friends, being lonely - what does that all get you at the end?

This.

This feeling right here, baby.  The feeling that hard work really does pay off.  The feeling that you have conquered a small mountain of impossibilities.  Doing it with your friends from way back and from yesterday.  Doing it in front of your family.  Doing it for those who couldn’t.  And it means the fucking WORLD to me that it’s with this team.  But you know what they say right?

RUN THAT SHIT BACK

Tríceps paralelo na Máquina: será que você faz certo?

Na Articulação do ombro há muitos tecidos que atravessam o pequeno espaço subacromial, que é o espaço entre o úmero e acrômio (ossos do braço e escápula).

Quando os ombros estão instáveis ou descentralizados, aumentam as chances de compressão ou impactos nesses tecidos e, consequentemente,  aumentam a possibilidade de diversos tipos de lesões, desde bursite até desgastes ou crescimento ósseo irregular,  ou mesmo rompimento de músculos como o supra espinal e ligamentos ou tendões como do Bíceps, sem contar desgastes da própria cartilagem capsular dos ombros. 

Esse exercício para tríceps,  como outros,  pode parecer ingênuo,  mas se feito errado com muita frequência ou muitas repetições,  aumenta as chances de lesões e/ou dores crônicas nos ombros. 

A estabilização e centralização dos ombros começam pela avaliação e correção das escápulas.

Lembre-se,  musculação não é só músculo. Segurança vem em primeiro lugar.

💦 A Importância de Beber Água Durante os Treinos 💪

1. Reposição de Líquidos Essencial: Durante o exercício, o corpo perde líquidos e eletrólitos (sódio, potássio, cálcio e magnésio) pelo suor. Repor é fundamental para o bom desempenho .

2. Ajuste de Temperatura Corporal: A hidratação ajuda a dissipar o calor gerado pelo esforço físico, evitando superaquecimento.

3. Efeito na Performance: Estar hidratado garante um fluxo sanguíneo adequado, oxigenação muscular, controle da frequência cardíaca e melhora do desempenho.

4. Como se Hidratar:

Antes do Exercício: Beba 500 ml de líquidos com sódio cerca de 2 horas antes do treino.

Durante o Exercício: Beba líquidos a cada 15-20 minutos sem esperar a sede.

Após o Exercício: Reponha o volume perdido em até 4-6 horas para manter o equilíbrio hídrico.

5. Monitoramento da Hidratação: Cheque a cor da urina e, se possível, avalie o peso pré e pós-treino para monitorar a perda de líquidos.

👉 Dica: Nos dias quentes, aumente a ingestão de água antes e durante o treino para evitar riscos maiores.

Principais erros na Remada T e como evitar:

Pouca inclinação: Diminui a ativação dos músculos dorsais e limita os resultados, pois redireciona a cargaparao trapéziosuperior.

Falta de controle do movimento: Movimentos rápidos ou descontrolados podem comprometer a eficiência do exercício, diminuindo o tempo sob tensão do músculo alvo.

Controle das escápulas: Não controlar bem as escápulas reduz a ativação muscular e aumenta o risco de lesões, uma vez que boa parte da tensão vai para outras partes. 

Instabilidade ou desalinhamento da coluna: Coluna mal posicionada ou instável pode resultar em dores e lesões graves.

⚠️ Melhorar a execução desses pontos é fundamental para evitar problemas e maximizar seus ganhos. Avaliação funcional e treino adequado são indispensáveis para corrigir essas falhas!

A posição dos pés e o alinhamento do fêmur, tíbia e pé segue primeiro as características estruturais do indivíduo (ângulos do colo do fêmur,  profundidade do acetábulo, restrições ósseas etc), depois a transferência de carga entre eixos, segmentos ósseos e feixes musculares. 

O alinhamento nunca mudará em um indivíduo, seguir o tal "assim pega mais " das redes sociais pode custar lesões  e dores crônicas para o resto da vida, como desgastes ósseos e as famosas "ites" (tendinite,  bursite,  etc)

"Ah, mas não sinto dores". Mas, então, o objetivo é um dia sentir dores nos joelhos, quadril  ou coluna?  Ou evitar que ela venha ao longo do tempo? Pois é assim que lesões não Traumáticas ocorrem,  silenciosamente.

Treinos com dores nos ombros? 

1. Altas repetições: Vamos começar pela pior opção. Altas repetições nunca é boa opção. Esforço repetitivo sem carga é justamente uma das principais causas de LER, seja tendinopatia, tendinite, bursite, osteofitose. Se você somar rotinas de trabalho, disfunção escapular ou postural, e até posição de dormir, é possível que o aluno tenha um alto estresse mecânico sem tempo de recuperação. "-Ah, mas e se não há dores ainda?" Pode ser que esse seja o 1% que falta para o desastre, ou leve aos 99% e um copo d'água seja o 1% que faltava. 

2. Mais carga, menos repetições. Pode até ser uma boa ideia caso você saiba o que está fazendo. Lembra-se daquele 1% que falta para uma lesão crônica? Pois é, o aluno está em recuperação? MANGUITO ROTADOR.

Se você se preocupa com Manguito mas nunca avaliou funcionalmente tuas escápulas, além de perder tempo "aquecendo", ainda continua expondo os ombros a lesões e dores crônicas. 
" Ah, mas o ombro tá ruim " - Assim como joelho, problemas nos ombros são consequências e não causa. Agir nos ombros só piora ou cria um problema que não estava lá. 

Será que existe um músculo chamado Manguito rotador? 
Não existe um músculo chamado manguito rotador.

Manguito Rotador é um complexo de quatro músculos que agem sobre o ombro, tracionando o Úmero em quatro vetores opostos contra a cavidade glenoide, cuja principal função é estabilizar a cabeça do Úmero dentro da Glenoide para, assim, evitar impactos ósseos e compressões irregulares na articulação do ombro, além de luxação e deslocamento. 

Resumindo, MANGUITO ROTADOR é um complexo muscular que cria uma força compressiva ao redor da cabeça Umeral, a estabiliza em todas as direções e ajuda a centralizar a cabeça Umeral na centro Cavidade Glenoide 

Ou seja, se a Função Principal do complexo do manguito rotador é Estabilizadora, por que seria uma boa idéia submetê-lo a uma fadiga e estresse mecânico precoces, quando esses músculos precisam prover estabilidade e segurança articular, não em um, mas em vários exercícios e atividades diárias?

Mesmo que fizesse sentido, porque fatiga-lo só em uma de quatro direções, causando mais desequilíbrio entre essas forças?

A elevação pélvica é um dos exercícios para glúteos mais importantes.

Porém para extrair o máximo proveito há um longo caminho passando por alogamentos, fortalecimentos, correção de desequilíbrios (como pés e quadril), desenvolvimento da técnica e controle adequado da carga.

Mesmo após as correções,  é comum culpar o treino pela falta de evolução, quando na verdade a questão é de como o treino é feito. Há intensidade suficiente? 

Quanto a intensidade, podemos incluir:

✅ Carga: intensa o suficiente para exaurir o músculo sem comprometer a técnica e os alinhamentos. 

✅ Concentração: a mente focada só no músculo, na cadência, na técnica.

✅ Intensidade: o quanto de força concentramos no músculo alvo até a falha ou próximo a ela. 

☑️ Vídeo 2, feito com intensidade, porém o mais comum: desistir ao achar que vai falhar.

✅ Vídeo 1, feito com mais intensidade: quando acha que vai falhar tenta mais 1, 2, 3 repetições 

Lembrando que a intensidade não deve comprometer a técnica e a integridade articular.

Crucifixos estão entre os exercícios mais avançados e difíceis de serem executados. Requerem um longo preparo antes de serem adotados, para que sejam feitos de forma segura e eficiente. Dear Lord Jesus, I desire to come after You and follow You. Help me to deny myself and take up my cross daily. Give me the strength and courage to follow You wherever You lead me. May my life be a reflection of Your love and grace. In Your Holy Nam I pray, Amen.

Dear God,Help me to stand against fear that tries to paralyze me or anyone I know from pursuing You. Remind me that fear is not from You, for You have given us power, love, and a sound mind. Strengthen my heart to move forward in faith, trusting that You go before me and fight for me.Help me to stand firm on Your promises and live boldly in Your truth. I come against every plan of the enemy that seeks to destroy or discourage Your people. Teach me to be an active participant in the spiritual battle... praying, believing, and standing firm on Your Word. With You, victory is already won.  In Jesus’ name I pray, amen.

Dear God,Thank You for another day to walk with You. When the weight of life feels heavy, help me remember that my strength is in You. Remind me that nothing I face today is too great for Your power or too small for Your care. “Cast your cares on the Lord and he will sustain you; he will never let the righteous be shaken.” (Psalm 55:22 NIV)
Help me move through this day with a heart full of trust and a mind anchored in peace. Let my words build others up, my actions reflect Your love, and my steps follow where You lead.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God, please help me to be sober and self-controlled in all aspects of my life. Help me to be watchful and aware of the schemes of the devil, who walks around like a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour. Protect me from his attacks and give me the strength to resist temptation. Help me to stay focused on You and Your will for my life. In Jesus’ name, I pray, Amen.

Dear God, I am in awe when I think about the depth of love You have for me, a sinner, who deserves nothing but condemnation. I praise You for Your grace, and love, and wisdom, and mercy toward me, because through Christ there is no condemnation for those who believe in Him. Lord, I believe. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Dear Lord, I thank You for the promise that You have given us in Your word that we will be hated by all men for Your name’s sake. I pray that You would give me the strength and courage to endure to the end, no matter what persecution or trials may come my way. Help me to stand firm in my faith and to never waver in my commitment to You. I claim the promise that if I endure to the end, I will be saved. Thank You for Your love and faithfulness, and for the assurance that You will always be with me. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Thank You, Heavenly Father, that You laid on the Lord Jesus Christ all my sins, and poured out Your wrath on the dearly beloved Son of Your love so that my sins are forgiven and I have been clothed in His righteousness. I praise Your wonderful  name.  In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.

Dear Heavenly Father, I pray that You would help me to let my light shine before others. May my actions and words reflect Your goodness and love, so that those around me may see Your light shining through me. May my good works bring glory to You, and may others be drawn closer to You through my example. Thank You for the privilege of being a light in this world, and may I always strive to bring honor and glory to Your name. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
Happy 20th Birthday @lando_h_13 I love you!

Dear God, I thank You for reminding me that I am Your temple and that Your Spirit lives in me. Help me to honor and respect my body as Your dwelling place. May I always seek to glorify You in all that I do and say. Fill me with Your Spirit and guide me in Your ways. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God,Thank You for being near and never distant. You are in command, even when life feels chaotic. Help me live today with faith that You are working in the unseen. Quiet the noise around me so I can hear Your direction. Help me respond to interruptions with grace and love. “The Lord is near to all who call on him…”.When fear creeps in, remind me of Your faithfulness. When I feel weak, help me rely on Your strength, not my own. Let my heart be tender to Your leading and bold in my obedience. Fill me with peace that defies my circumstances and hope that lasts through every season.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God, When my body runs on empty and my mind keeps racing, invite me into Your rest. Quiet the inner voice that pushes me beyond healthy limits and remind me that my worth is not measured by productivity but by Your love. Refresh my energy for every task ahead. Help me set wise boundaries, honor moments of rest, and release worries I cannot fix. Let Your peace settle over my heart and my home, restoring what feels worn down and renewing my perspective for tomorrow.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear Lord, I come to You today with a heart full of faith and a desire to grow even stronger in my belief in You. I claim the promise that faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. I ask that You open my ears to hear Your word and that You speak to me through it. Help me to understand Your truth and to apply it to my life. I pray that my faith will continue to grow and that I will become a shining example of Your love and grace. Thank You for Your promise and for Your constant presence in my life. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God, keep me ever mindful of Your Word and the truth that is contained in the plain message of Scripture and the glorious gospel of grace. I praise and thank You that I have passed from death to life, by believing on Jesus. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Heavenly Father, it is my desire to know You more, to learn more of You, and to become a true disciple of Jesus Christ. Give me a teachable spirit, I pray, so that I may grow in grace. And I pray that You would enable me to go and disciple others in Your strength so that together we come to a knowledge of the truth in Christ Jesus, in Whose name I pray, AMEN.
Thank You God we got them both!
Hallelujah He Is Risen Indeed!  Happy Easter!

Dear Lord, I come before You today with a grateful heart, knowing that You have fulfilled Your promise to rise from the dead. We declare with joy that You are not here, for You have risen, just like You said. We thank You for the sacrifice You made on the cross, and for the victory You have won over sin and death. I claim the promise of Your resurrection, and I ask that You would help me to live in the power of your resurrection every day. May I see the place where You were lying and be reminded of Your great love for me. I pray this in Your Holy Name, Amen.

Dear God, Thank You for showing me what true love is through the sacrifice of Your son, Jesus Christ. Help me to understand the depth of this love and to live it out in my daily life. Give me the courage and strength to lay down my life for my brothers and sisters, just as Jesus did for me. May I always be willing to put others before myself and to love sacrificially.
In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
Good Friday Thank You Jesus for Your Sacrifice...

Heavenly Father, thank You that the Lord Jesus Christ was wounded for my transgressions and bore my sins in His body on the tree. Thank You that my guilt has been exchanged for peace with God and the peace of God now rests in my heart. Thank You that I have been forever released from the bondage of sin and death, and that by His stripes I have been healed, clothed in His righteousness, and made a child of God. Thank You that Christ Jesus is my Kinsman-Redeemer and the sinless Substitute for my sins which, by His death and Resurrection, have been flung as far as the east is from the west. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Dear God,When I feel down and weighed by the pressures of life, remind me that You carry what I cannot. You hold the world in Your hands, and You have already overcome it. “In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.” (John 16:33). Thank You for the strength and victory You’ve given me through Jesus. Because You overcame, I can face anything with courage and hope.Lift my spirit when I feel weary. Help me to fix my eyes on You instead of my struggles. Fill me with Your peace and remind me that Your power lives in me. With You, I am not defeated... I am more than a conqueror through Christ.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God I just want to thank You, for Your grace and mercy in sending the Lord Jesus Christ Who loves me and died for me and is the beginning and the completer of my faith. Help me to take my eyes off the things that detract from Him, including myself... and may I keep the focus of my gaze ever looking to Him. Thank You for His life example and His patient endurance in the face of the Cross and make me more like Him, day by day. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Dear Lord, help me to follow in the footsteps of Your Son, who came not to be served but to serve. May I have a heart of humility and a willingness to serve others, just as Jesus did. And may I never forget the ultimate sacrifice he made, giving his life as a ransom for many. Thank You for Your love and grace, and for the example of Jesus.  In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.

Dear Lord, I thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, to take away the sin of the world. I pray that I may always behold him as the Lamb of God and trust in his sacrifice for my salvation. May I live my life in a way that honors his sacrifice and brings glory to Your name. Thank You for the promise of forgiveness and redemption through Jesus. In Jesus' name  I pray, Amen.

Dear Lord Jesus, I must admit that I am a lot like the disciples. I also can look for a material triumph instead of a spiritual triumph. I can look for victory in my external circumstances instead of in my internal attitudes. I can so easily believe the lie that says, “If you are a Christian, everything will go smoothly in life. You will have no more difficulties or trials.” Please forgive me, for looking in the wrong places for Your victory. Your First Coming provided a spiritual triumph on the cross when peace with God in heaven was made possible through Your shed blood. Thank You, that I now have peace with God of heaven and earth through faith in You, Jesus. You now live inside me through Your Holy Spirit Who can enable me to respond in a God-honoring manner to the evil that is flourishing in the world today. I am now trusting You to lead me into this spiritual triumph that can manifest Your attitude in all I think, say, and do. Yes, I am looking forward to Your Second Coming which will usher in Your material triumph when all nations will be brought under Your rule, and there will be peace on earth among all cultures and countries forever! But until then, my focus remains on You to lead me into spiritual victory! In Your matchless name I pray, Amen.

Dear God, I come before You today, claiming the promise that You are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. I thank You for Your constant protection and for being my refuge in times of trouble.  I pray that you continue to be my shield, guarding me from harm and keeping me safe from the attacks of the enemy. May Your glory shine upon me, and may I reflect Your goodness and grace to those around me.  I ask that You lift up my head when I am feeling discouraged or defeated. Help me to remember that You are with me always, and that I can trust in Your unfailing love and faithfulness. Thank You for being my rock and my salvation. I trust in You completely, and I know that with You by my side, I can face anything that comes my way.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God of perseverance and encouragement, I come before You today claiming the promise in Romans 15:5. I ask that You grant me and my brothers and sisters in Christ the ability to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus. Help us to put aside our differences and come together in unity, love, and understanding. Strengthen us to persevere through any challenges that may come our way and encourage us to keep our eyes fixed on You. Thank You for Your faithfulness and for the promise of unity in Christ. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Thank You, Heavenly Father, that I am Your child. I want to know You more and pray that as I seek You through Your Word and come before Your throne of grace, in prayer and praise, You will show me more of Yourself. Instill in my heart a desire to seek You more and search for You with my whole heart, and I pray that I will discover a depth of Your perfect character that I have never seen before. Let me reflect You in thought, word, and deed, as Christ is being formed in me. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Dear Lord, I believe in You as the Scripture has said. I claim the promise that from within me will flow rivers of living water. May Your Holy Spirit flow through me and bring life to those around me. May my words and actions be a reflection of Your love and grace. Thank You for the gift of Your living water. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God,Help me to keep asking, keep seeking, and keep knocking on Heaven’s door. I believe that You hear me, even when I’m unsure or can’t see the answer yet. Teach me to persist in prayer and not lose heart, trusting that You are faithful and working behind the scenes.I believe that prayer is power. I won’t pray once and forget; I’ll come back again and again because I believe and I trust You. Strengthen my faith when waiting feels long and help me find peace in Your timing. You are good, and I know You hear every word I speak.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Loving Father, I realize more and more how much I need You to be the Restorer of my soul. I need the living water from on high to refresh my heart and sustain my spirit. Times are hard, Father, and sometimes the pressures of life seem to encompass me on every side, but I praise Your name that You are my shelter from the heat and You alone revive my weary soul. Keep me and those I love under the shadow of Your wing. In Jesus' name I pray, AMEN.

Dear Heavenly Father, I come before You with a heart full of sorrow and repentance. I know that Godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret. I claim this promise today, Lord, and ask that You help me to turn away from my sins that try to trip me up and keep me fromYou.  I pray that You would fill me with Your Holy Spirit, that I may have the strength and courage to resist the temptations of the world. I know that the sorrow of the world produces death, but with Your help, I can overcome and find true life in You.  Thank You for Your grace and mercy, Lord. I trust in Your promise that godly sorrow leads to salvation, and I pray that You would continue to guide me on this journey of faith.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.

Dear God, when fear rises within me, help me to remember that You are with me and that I can trust You completely.  Quiet my anxious thoughts and fill my heart with confidence that You are my refuge and strength, always near and always faithful.  Help me to fix my eyes on You instead of what scares me. When uncertainty tries to overwhelm my mind, remind me that Your presence is my peace and Your promises never fail. Teach me to respond to fear with faith and to trust that You are working all things together for my good, even when I can’t see it.  In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen!

Dear God,
When frustration builds and things feel too hard, remind me that You are my strength and help in every moment. Teach me to pause before reacting and to look to You for wisdom when I don’t know what to do. Let this truth steady my heart and bring peace to my thoughts when everything feels uncertain.

Give me endurance to keep going when I want to give up. Fill me with faith that believes You are working even when I can’t see it. Help me trust that Your goodness is constant, even in difficulty. Elmina Castle (Dungeon) in Ghana, built in 1482 is one of the oldest buildings in Africa.  Infamous as a major hub for the transatlantic slave trade for 250 years, where hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans were held in horrific conditions before being shipped to the Americas through the "Door of No Return". Now a museum, it serves as a powerful memorial and educational site, operated by the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board, attracting tourists and descendants seeking to understand this dark chapter of history. 

Dungeons held vast numbers of captives in cramped, unsanitary conditions, leading to disease, with the "Door of No Return" being the final exit to slave ships.

Women were repeatly taken advantage off by workers, soldiers and even the govenor who had a private staircase to his quarters... 

You can read about this in books, watch movies but your life will change when you see it for yourself!!!

The "Man in the Clock" in Amsterdam refers to the captivating Schiphol Clock, an art installation by Dutch designer Maarten Baas at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (Lounge 2) that features a man seemingly painting the clock hands in real-time, but is actually a 12-hour looping video of an actor (Tiago Sá da Costa). Building Black Civilizations: Journey of 2,000 Ships continues artist Ekow Nimako’s afrofuturistic reimagining of ancient African kingdoms. Using LEGO bricks as his medium, Nimako explores the mysterious fourteenth century sea voyage of Mansa Abu Bakr II, predecessor of Mansa Musa, ruler of the ancient Mali Empire. According to legends, Abu Bakr II was an intrepid explorer, who abdicated his throne and took 2,000 ships on an expedition into the Atlantic, but was never to return or heard from again. Some accounts suggest the massive fleet reached as far as the Americas, but where they went beyond this is still unknown. Combining architecture, historical accounts, and fantastical possibilities, Nimako transcends the geometric form of LEGO to recreate the epic voyage. And in doing so, Nimako presents an uninterrupted and unco-opted narrative of Black civilizations and imagines liberated futures.

You don’t keep changing strategies because you’re curious.
You do it because staying with one forces you to face yourself.
—
At first, it feels logical.
“This system doesn’t work.”
“I need something better.”
“Maybe I just haven’t found the right strategy yet.”
So you switch.

Again.
And again.
And again.
—
But if you look closely…
The result never really changes.
Different indicators.
Different setups.
Different rules.
Same outcome.
—
It’s not the strategy.
It’s what the strategy forces you to confront.

Because every system, no matter how good,
will eventually put you in a situation where:

You have to take a loss.
You have to be wrong.
You have to follow a rule you don’t feel like following.

And that’s the moment most people break.
Not because the system failed.
But because they did.

So instead of fixing that…
They switch.

To a new strategy.
A new framework.
A new “solution.”

—

Not to improve.
But to escape.

Because as long as it’s the strategy’s fault,
You never have to face your own patterns.

That’s why most traders don’t lack knowledge.
They lack consistency with discomfort.

The uncomfortable truth is:
If you can’t follow one system through losses,
You won’t follow any system long enough to succeed.

You don’t need a better strategy.
You need to stop running from the same problem.

—

I’m Harvey.
The trader who tells you to wash the cup first.

You don’t fail to cut losses because you’re emotional.

You fail because you never defined what “wrong” looks like.

—

Most people enter a trade with a plan for profit.

Targets.
Scenarios.
What they hope will happen.

But almost no one clearly defines:

“What would prove me wrong?”

So when things start to shift…

Price moves against you.
The setup weakens.
Momentum disappears.

You don’t act.

Not because you’re undisciplined.

But because there’s nothing to act on.

No line.
No trigger.
No definition.

Just feeling.

—

So you hesitate.

You wait.

You tell yourself:

“Maybe it will come back.”
“Maybe I just need more time.”

But what you’re really saying is:

“I never decided what being wrong means.”

—

And without that…

There is no stop loss.

Only a delayed reaction.

—

The market doesn’t punish mistakes.

It punishes undefined mistakes.

—

The difference between a trader who survives
and one who slowly disappears isn’t intelligence.

It’s clarity.

Before every trade, the real question isn’t:

“How much can I make?”

It’s:

“What exactly would prove me wrong?”

Not vague.
Not emotional.
Not “I’ll feel it.”

Clear.

Specific.

Decided in advance.

—

Because the moment you define what “wrong” looks like,

You remove the need to negotiate with yourself.

—

And most losses don’t come from being wrong.

They come from negotiating with reality
after you already are.

—

You don’t need more knowledge.

You need fewer undefined decisions.

—

That’s where most people break.

Not in the market.

But in the moment they refuse to define the truth.

—

I’m Harvey.

The trader who tells you to wash the cup first.

You’re not losing to the market.
You’re losing to your ego.

The harder you study investing,
the faster you might lose money.

Most people don’t lose because they don’t know enough.

They lose because they refuse to admit one thing:

“I’m wrong.”

In Think Again, Adam Grant talks about a real tragedy.

In 1949, a group of elite firefighters were trapped in a wildfire at Mann Gulch.

They had to run for their lives.

But many of them died.

Not because they were weak.
Not because they didn’t try.

But because they held onto their tools.

Axes. Saws. Heavy gear.

Even when every second mattered.

This isn’t about strength.

It’s about identity.

Under pressure,
those tools became who they were.

Letting go didn’t just mean running faster.

It meant:

“I’m no longer who I think I am.”

And here’s the uncomfortable truth:

You’ve done the same thing.

In the market,
that “heavy axe” is your losing trade.

You’ve seen it:

The setup is broken.
The direction is wrong.
The logic no longer holds.

But you stay.

Not because it makes sense.

But because closing it means:

“I was wrong.”

So you hold.

You hope.

You wait.

But you’re not protecting your trade.

You’re protecting your ego.

That’s how accounts slowly die.

The best traders aren’t always right.

They’re just faster at letting go of being right.

A stop loss isn’t failure.

It’s the price you pay to learn something new.

Try this:

Before every trade, write one sentence:

“If this happens, I’m wrong.”

Not vague.
Not emotional.
Clear.

Because if you don’t define what being wrong looks like—

You’re not investing.

You’re gambling.

The market doesn’t care how much you studied.

It doesn’t care how confident you feel.

It only cares about one thing:

Can you survive your mistakes?

I don’t teach people how to make money.

I teach them how not to die in the market.

Investing isn’t about becoming stronger.

It’s about surviving your own mistakes.

— Harvey

The guilt I felt around not feeling infatuated with my son early on contributed massively to my mental health. 

We’re made to feel like there’s something wrong with us if we don’t see our child and instantly connect to them. 

The truth is, it’s normal for it to take time, and there’s nothing to feel guilty about when it does ❤️

#honestmotherhood #postpartumjourney #motherhoodunfiltered #colic #highlysensitivechild

We’re told it’s the best phase, “just wait until they’re a toddler..”

But it’s been the polar opposite for me, and so many mothers I talk to. The newborn days were filled with doctors and reflux and colic and purple crying and no sleep and deep mental health lows

Now my toddler sleeps independently, plays for minutes alone, can be distracted, throws tantrums I can manage, and shows me affection back. 

You’re allowed to struggle in the beginning. It’s FREAKING HARD. People who tell you otherwise had a vastly different experience than you ❤️

#motherhood #momlife #postpartumdepression #postpartum #honestmotherhood

It’s everywhere; the sleep advice, the feeding advice, the emotional advice. But has any of it actually helped you? 

More often than not, general parenting advice leads to further feelings of failure, overwhelm, isolation. If ____ worked for everyone else, why isn’t it working for me?

Because it was never made for you. You’re a unique individual, just as much as your baby is. If advice isn’t working, it’s not because you’re doing something wrong. It just never had you in mind to begin with ❤️

#motherhood #parentingadvice #postpartum #honestmotherhood #postpartumjourney

Your sensitive child isn’t “reactive”, they’re processing more. 

They notice the small shifts. 
They feel things more deeply. 
And they hit overwhelm faster than other kids.

They’re capable one minute… 
and completely incapable the next. 

And mothering a sensitive child asks so so so much more of you. 
More presence. More patience. More regulation.

Which is why it can feel so exhausting… even when you love them deeply.

If this sounds like your child, you’re not imagining it. Please reach out if you are struggling to cope 🫶🏼 

#motherhood #toddlermom #gentleparenting #honestmotherhood #postpartum

The first few months with my son sent me into the deepest, saddest, loneliest place I’ve ever experienced. 

The endless screaming. The minutes of sleep a night. The shock of becoming a mom. 

I questioned if this was a mistake. Not my son, but me being a mother. I didn’t think I was cut out for it. At least not the mother of an extremely sensitive child. 

 But oh my gosh. A year and a half later, these images feel like a different lifetime ago. A blip in my relationship with my son. The love I have for him now, for us together, it’s the love I desperately longed for those first few months. 

Things WILL change for you, but if you’re stuck in the struggle, please reach out. I now work with other mothers in similar positions because colic is extremely traumatic, and you need support just as much as your baby ❤️‍🩹🫶🏼

#colic #motherhood #honestmotherhood #newborn #postpartum

is changing you.

And even if it doesn’t feel like it right now…

No one seemed to understand the reality of what happens to your nervous system when you’re being screamed at for 8+ hours a day, while your heart breaks because it seems like there’s nothing to do to ease your baby’s distress. أنا وصنع الله ابراهيم
بدأت علاقتي بصنع الله ابراهيم منذ سنوات الثانوي حيث كان ذهني قد بدأ بعد  يتفتح للأدب ولقضاياه  فتراني أبحث بين طيات الروايات التي أقرؤها عن صدى لما يعتمل في صدري وذهني من مشاعر وأفكار مبكرة عن الخير والشر والحق والعدل . ثم وقعت بين يدي رواية اللجنة. فقرأتها وأعدت قراءتها مرات، إلى أن شارفت على التماهي مع بطلها. تحدثت تلك الرواية بما في نفسي وأشارت بشجاعة لسيطرة النظام الواحد ووجهت أصابع الاتهام بقلم جريء لإمبريالية أمريكا دون مواربة وإلى علاقتها بالأنظمة المحلية العميلة لها، صنيعتها ،فانبهرت أمام هذا الكاتب الشجاع وبدأت أستزيد من القراءة  له  وعنه.  وعرفت رفضه للمصانعة ورفضه للجوائز حين تتبناها أنظمة استبدادية، وعرفت عناده وشعرب به يسير في مسالك الإبداع والأدب ذئبا منفردا لا يتردد في خسارة رفاق أو معارف أو أصدقاء إذا كان قربهم يتقاطع مع الحق. عرفت أن هذا النموذج هو الذي أحب أن أقرأ له وأتعلم منه. 
عرفت أن صنع الله ابراهيم هو المثقف النقيض لنموذج المثقف صنيع السلطة الذي تصطفيه وتبجله وتفرضه على مناهجنا الدراسية وتدفعه إلى ساحة النجومية مقابل أن يكون بوقا دعائيا لها أو مقابل أن يسكت عما يجري لشعبه وعما تفعله به تلك الأنظمة.
أحببت صنع الله ابراهيم دون أراه وأحببت قبضته الرمزية التي يشرعها في وجه  الباطل . وظل واحدا من أبطالي وأبا من آبائي الروحيين إلى أن كتبت أولى رواياتي، سنتها عاهدت نفسي أن أظل وفية لنهج صنع الله ابراهيم وأن أظل ذئبة وحيدة قابعة دوما على يسار السلطة  لا أتبع نظاما ولا أصفق لأحدا ولا أكتب لجائزة ولا أوالي أنظمة تعتقل الأدباء وتحبس الشعراء باليمين ثم تبيض وجوهها بجوائز مبهرة باليسار.تشهرها أمام المبدعين كجزرة أمام حمار. 
عاهدت نفسي أن أجتهد ما استطعت وأرتقي بقلمي ليكون إبنا وفيا مخلصا لنهج صنع الله ابراهيم الجريء الذي خاض مسالك التجريب منذ عقود ولم يهب ناقدا ولم يكف عن مساءلة الذوق العام وخلخلته. 
شفاء عاجل لك يا أستاذ صنع الله ابراهيم. شفاء عاجلا لك يا معلمي. شفاء وسلاما ومودة لا تموت أبدا.
