It’s been weeks since mum passed 🙏
I thought I should give a special thanks to my friend @kevoparsons @yahgenfurnitureau for the painting representing mums passage through life with her large extended - “every colour of the rainbow family”, as she put it. Also Kevin for arranging @colinappo to do a beautiful emotion and funeral site cleansing ceremony, with smoke and didgeridoo. It was a unique service thanks to that and the fact a top shelf piper on the bagpipes as escort walking her to and during the departure of the hearse. Absolutely amazing and she definitely would have approved. It was interesting to see that cute little chapel in the greenest of valleys, by the idyllic pond. After driving through blinding rain it was suddenly clear, the moment we got there - perfect day. And when she passed with her final breath, our sisters left the hospital only to see a rainbow form right before their eyes. My son laughed and said it was Grandma letting us know “she made it”…. Merely coincidence for most, but as we grieve we attach our emotions to so many things. Like the cicadas suddenly now noticeable as tears run down my face, the connection to nature as real as ever thanks for sharing mum. 
My sisters and brother shared just a few of our many treasured memories that evoke every emotion. A common thread being the physical and cognitive resilience, a tale of a woman of substance who shared herself without hesitation nor expectation. Times change more rapidly than expected and it is now our turn to be the older generations. Can’t express enough gratitude for the simple nature based teachings you passed on to us all mum…❤️
She was no angel but she had a heart filled with the capacity for absolute fearlessness, ferocity, passion and loving nurturing ways. Providing for us so well that poverty was never a problem, it was cruelty, heartlessness, corruption and greed among other negative things that she despised. 
-

Hope you enjoy the gifts of our love and gratitude for your eternity mum, yes the special ones too… 🌻 
As it was at your creation, nature now embraces you again as her own. 🌹

​If you’re looking for a low-mess, high-engagement activity, this DIY window sun catcher is the winner. It kept her occupied for over an hour and looks so beautiful when the sun hits it! 

​What you’ll need:
• ​Paper, card, or craft paper
• ​Marker or crayon
• ​Scissors
• ​Packaging tape (or clear contact paper)
• ​Confetti, tissue paper, cellophane, or pompoms 

​How to do it:
• ​Draw a large butterfly on your paper.
• ​Cut out the inside of the wings.
• ​Flip it over and cover the wing gaps with packaging tape (sticky side facing the front).
• ​Stick it to a window or glass door.
• ​Let them go wild sticking their colourful bits to the wings! 

​Hot Tip: This works beautifully with nature, too! Try using small flowers or leaves (fake, fresh or pressed) for a gorgeous earthy fairy version. 🌸🍃

Been a minute. Almost a year off social media. I must say time off has been fulfilling to say the least. 

3 years ago life set me on a path of solitude. Initially I had know idea what was happening until a year ago. I recognized it was happening internally, whatever “it” was. The only way I could I identify it was to search inward. So I went ghost. Just me, my dog, work, books, YouTube, and long conversations w/ Momdukes. I am not who I was, no not in the slightest. Enlightened? Perhaps. I prefer recognition of true self. I found myself. I know myself. I truly love myself. I am now who I am to be. 

Not a book worm but I always found comfort in reading. This past year however, it’s been mind opening. These have been my favorite maybe I read them while being intentional if that makes sense. 

“The Power of Now” helped me identify my Ego, which I found has been on auto pilot my whole life. So much bs in my past derived from it. Also released me from the clutches of my past and future but rather see the peace in the here and now. 

“The Alchemist” taught me purpose. So long have I struggled finding my own or even what purpose was. I complicated it so much thinking it’s all about desires and wants, money & material things smh. Probably my all time favorite.

“Who Moved My Cheese” A simple book but has so much depth. So much meaning. It’s about 2 mini people and 2 mice trapped in a maze in search of cheese lol like huh? But in their journey identifies the type of people and their behaviors today. There’s lessons  on fear, complacency, unwillingness to change, visualization, foresight, visualization, risk, belief and so on. Dope book.

“How to Win Friends & Influence People” so many 💎 in this book. My biggest takeaway is the power of positive reinforcement, being kind. One of my favorite excerpts “The greatest asset I possess, and the way to develop the best that is in a person is by appreciation and encouragement”.

Today is #WorldKindnessDay and I’m so grateful for the community of people who follow me on this page. 
Thank you to everyone who runs into me at various events and comes over to chat! 🫶🏽
Here are a few ways to spread kindness in your community:

1. Send a sweet message to someone and put a smile on their face. Everyone loves a genuine compliment. I’m a huge fan of mailing thank you cards and sending random text. 
2. Give someone the benefit of the doubt. I always choose to think well of people with good intentions. It prevents me from overthinking or thinking the worse. It also prevents wrinkles. 
3. Let someone go ahead of you: In Houston traffic, at the check out line, at the airport…. Let’s be patient with each other.
4. Put in a good word. I love good gossip in a quiet way. Finding out that people are looking out for me without my knowledge always melts my heart. 
5. Be open to others. We have new people arriving to our city all the time: new jobs, new neighbors, new friends. While people figure out the culture of our very social city, be flexible to learning new perspectives. 

Lastly, smile! Pat yourself on the back for everything you’ve pushed through. It’s been quite a year! Be kind to YOURSELF, you’re doing a great job. 💋

October is breast cancer awareness month. 💕Mammograms save lives and keep women healthy. 

When I was just 19 years old, I found a lump in my breast the size of a golf ball! Thanks to a mammogram, I was able to have a biopsy to remove what would later be determined as a benign tumor. Finding a lump in your breast can be scary, but with early detection, it doesn’t have to be. Early detection for breast cancer changes the game, so let’s kick off a new era of breast health. Please check your breast and schedule your mammograms! 

Thank you for this amazing organization @imasurviveher and for your donation @harrishealthsystem

Wenn ich mit Unternehmerinnen über ihre Finanzen spreche, frage ich oft:

„Kennst du deine monatlichen Mindestkosten?“

Viele kennen ihre Umsatzziele.
Viele wissen, was sie gerne verdienen würden.

Aber die Grundlage fehlt oft.

Dabei ist genau diese Zahl eine der wichtigsten Orientierungsgrößen im Business.

Nicht, weil sie Druck machen soll.

Sondern weil sie dir hilft, Entscheidungen auf einer klaren Grundlage zu treffen.

Wer weiß, was tatsächlich benötigt wird, kann Umsätze, Preise und Angebote deutlich realistischer einordnen.

Für mich gehört diese Kennzahl zu den wichtigsten Zahlen für ein nachhaltiges Business.

Erzähl mir doch gerne, ob du deine monatlichen Mindestkosten bereits kennst. Das würde mich wirklich interessieren.

Ich baue gerade selbst an dieser Klarheit – und merke wie viel sie verändert, noch bevor die Zahl „groß genug" ist.

Die Liquiditätsreichweite ist eine der Zahlen im Business, die ich lange vor mir hergeschoben habe. Nicht aus Faulheit. Sondern aus einem leisen Unbehagen.

Was ich jetzt merke: Das Wissen – auch wenn es noch nicht perfekt ist – ist leichter zu tragen als das Nicht-Wissen.

Im Karussell teile ich, was diese Zahl emotional bedeutet. Und warum sie vielleicht mehr mit Selbstfürsorge zu tun hat als mit Controlling.

💬 Wie ist das bei dir? Schreib mir gern.

Viele Selbstständige verfolgen höhere Umsätze, ohne zu merken, dass ihr Nervensystem eigentlich nach etwas anderem sucht:

Vorhersagbarkeit.

Kurz und knackig: Der Nettoumsatz ist das, was übrig bleibt, wenn du von deinem Bruttoumsatz (also dem gesamten Betrag, den du eingenommen hast) die Mehrwertsteuer und eventuelle Rabatte oder Rückgaben abziehst. Klingt schon mal gar nicht so kompliziert, oder? 💸

💡 Warum ist der Nettoumsatz so wichtig?
Ganz einfach: Er zeigt dir, was du tatsächlich verdient hast und womit du dein Business nach vorne bringen kannst! Ohne diese Zahl zu kennen, verlierst du schnell den Überblick – und wir wollen doch alle eine gesunde Work-Life-Balance und weniger Stress, richtig?

Hier ein paar Punkte, auf die du achten solltest:

1️⃣ Genau rechnen: Der Nettoumsatz ist nicht das, was du auf deinem Konto siehst, sondern was nach Steuern und Abzügen bleibt.
2️⃣ Verwende ihn für deine Planung: Er hilft dir dabei, realistische Entscheidungen zu treffen – von Investitionen bis zu Gehältern.
3️⃣ Der Blick aufs Wesentliche: Lass dich nicht von großen Umsatzzahlen blenden! Was zählt, ist das, was am Ende für dich übrig bleibt.

Also, wenn du die Finanzseite deines Business mal nicht vernachlässigen willst, schnapp dir deine Zahlen und schau dir deinen Nettoumsatz an. 🧐

Wie immer: Wenn du Unterstützung beim Finanzmanagement brauchst – ich bin da! Lass uns dafür sorgen, dass du den Kopf wieder frei hast für die kreativen Dinge, die du liebst. 💻✨

Kostet dich Multitasking wertvolle Zeit? 🚨 Lass uns über den unsichtbaren Zeitfresser sprechen, der deinen Fokus zerstört und deine Produktivität in den Keller zieht!

Vor einiger Zeit habe ich bereits über Multitasking geschrieben. Dort war unter anderem diese Grafik zu sehen. Heute möchte ich genauer auf ihre Bedeutung eingehen.

Die Grafik basiert auf eine Untersuchung von Gerald Weinberg zu der Auswirkung von Multitasking auf die Produktivität (im Bereich Projektmanagement).

Er hat festgestellt, dass mit jedem zusätzlichen Projekt im Schnitt 20% der produktiven Arbeitszeit verloren geht. Dies passiert durch den Wechsel zwischen den Arbeiten. Wir müssen uns NEU in die Aufgabe einarbeiten und es kostet uns Zeit bis wir wieder voll konzentriert sind.

Das bedeutet bei 1 Projekt entspricht unsere produktive Arbeitszeit 100%.

Bei 2 Projekten verlieren wir 20% unserer produktiven Zeit, so das nur 80% unserer Zeit übrig bleibt. Bei 1 Std. Arbeit verliehren wir also 12 Minuten. Übrig bleiben 40% für jedes Projekt. Was in einer Stunde 24 Minuten pro Projekt entspricht.

Bei 3 Projekten verlieren wir 40% produktive Zeit. 60% bleiben übrig. Auf 3 Projekte verteilt, erhält jedes Projekt 20%.

Ab 4 Projekten wird es richtig unprodukiv. Die unproduktive Zeit liegt nun bereits höher als die produktive Zeit. Wir verlieren bereits 60% unserer Zeit. 40% bleiben übrig. 10% pro Projekt!

Bei 5 Projekten entspricht der Zeitverlust 75%. Bei einer Std. also bereits 45 Minuten. 25% unserer Zeit bleibt übrig! Auf die 5 Projekte verteilt, erhält jedes Projekt 5% unserer Zeit. Das wären gerade mal 3 Minuten.

Nehmen wir uns mal ein paar Minuten, um über ein Thema zu sprechen, das oft für Verwirrung sorgt: Umsatz vs. Gewinn. 🤓💸

Stell dir vor, du hast eine großartige Woche hinter dir und dein Umsatz ist durch die Decke gegangen. 🍾💃 Klingt fantastisch, oder? Aber bevor du jetzt die Champagnerflaschen öffnest und den Urlaub auf den Malediven buchst, lass uns einen kleinen Realitätscheck machen. 🛑🌴

UMSATZ ist das, was du insgesamt eingenommen hast. Es ist der Betrag, den deine Kundinnen für deine Dienstleistungen gezahlt haben. Aber hier kommt der Haken: Umsatz ist nicht gleich Gewinn.

GEWINN ist das, was übrig bleibt, nachdem du alle Ausgaben abgezogen hast. Das sind die Kosten für deine Software, deine Internetverbindung, das schicke Canva-Abo (wir wissen alle, wie wichtig das ist!), und vielleicht auch der Kaffee, der dich durch die langen Arbeitstage bringt. ☕💻

Also, worauf kommt es wirklich an?

1️⃣ Kostenkontrolle: Behalte deine Ausgaben im Blick. Ein niedriger Umsatz kann dir dennoch einen höheren Gewinn bringen, wenn deine Ausgaben gering sind.
 
2️⃣ Effizienz: Nutze deine Ressourcen klug. Automatisiere, delegiere (hallo, virtuelle Assistentin hier! 😉), und optimiere deine Prozesse.

3️⃣ Preiskalkulation: Versteh den Wert deiner Dienstleistungen und setze angemessene Preise. Dein Ziel ist es, Gewinn zu machen, nicht nur Umsatz zu generieren.

4️⃣ Finanzplanung: Plane voraus und lege etwas für steuerliche und unvorhergesehene Ausgaben beiseite. Ein gut geplanter Finanzhaushalt ist dein bester Freund.

Also, meine Liebe, lass uns den Umsatz feiern, aber den Gewinn schätzen. Denn am Ende des Tages zählt, was auf deinem Bankkonto bleibt, nicht nur, was auf deiner Rechnung steht. 💪💡

In diesem Sinne: Happy Planning und lasst uns gemeinsam erfolgreich sein! 🎉✨

A grinding stone excavated from an archaeological site in southern Vietnam was used to prepare spices. Microscopic traces of plant material found on the stone included traces of turmeric, ginger, clove, cinnamon & nutmeg. One seed still produced the familiar smell of nutmeg after 2000 years. The site, Oc Eo, was a city that lay at the crossroads of a trade route that spread to the Mediterranean Sea. These same ingredients are still used in curries today. Interesting to note, coconut was also found at the site. Curry recipes have remained relatively consistent throughout time.  Cultural trade between Southeast Asia & South Asia created a cuisine with lasting appeal-Evidence of time honored deliciousness. You should definitely make some for dinner! #curry #coconut #vietnam #southeastasianfood #traderoutes #smellssogood #archaeology #cuisine #celebratefood

Trying to change your body while demanding so much from it is no joke + honestly something I didn’t think I’d struggle so much with. 

Trail running requires a crazy amount of energy + learning how to balance fuel, rest, a calorie deficit on some days + not on others is one of the hardest things I’ve had to figure out. Especially when that post run hunger hits + it feels like pregnancy cravings all over 🙃 

Some days I think I could just stop running for a couple of months, lose the weight like I know how then get back to running when I’m at my goal weight. But honestly, I’d be miserable because running is my happy place! And becoming smaller isn’t the only goal - if it was I’d probably just sit on the couch + inject myself with GLP-1s 💀

But we’re getting there. Slowly figuring it all out - without injuries!

The night before last I was out for a run. Not a speed session. Just a plain, easy run to get the weekly distance up. When I was almost home, a young guy ran past me - or more like flew past me. He looked at me with the most pitiful look on his face. Almost like he despised me + how dare I take up space on the footpath while I struggled at a 7:00/km pace. 

Honestly, it made me feel super crappy. “He probably thinks I’m brand new to running or that I’m super unfit”, I thought. Yeah, I was on struggle street for sure. But he had no idea that I’d completed Tarawera the week before. That I run 5 days a week + bike the 6th day. He had no idea I’m a Mum to a young kid + that I work full time out of the home (while also currently studying towards a work promotion). He had no idea that I’m a week out from my period + all I want to do is eat potato chips while being rolled up in a blanket watching Twilight on the couch. Or that on the weekend, I’m doing more study, taking my son to extra curricular classes, cleaning our home, meal planning + cooking all while hearing “Mum, you’re not watching good enough” 🙃 

All that to say, yeah life is so busy right now. It’s hectic AF. It’s my choice but it’s still a struggle. So if you see someone struggling on a run, maybe don’t just assume they’re failing. Maybe they’re just carrying a bit + they’re exhausted. 

Also, maybe they are actually new to running or maybe they’re not + they just enjoy running ‘slower’. Wild concept, I know.

Tarawera T21 🌲 race recap:

It started with @_sophiarietema forgetting her vest, flasks + poles at home. I then realised I’d left my shoes back in Auckland. Luckily I’d brought an extra pair however they were ✨ BRAND NEW ✨ We then received an emergency weather alert + had a terrible nights sleep (thanks drunk hostel goers).

Fuelled up on red bull + bagels we headed to the start line in the pouring rain. After meeting the amazing @k8__nz + @waiora_pai + having some photos it was start time! 

We looped around Blue Lake which was stunning + felt like a breeze. Into the first aid station I had a bit of a wait for the bathroom but had some good yarns with the amazing volunteers! 

Onto the 2/3rd of the course where it started bucketing down. The trail turned into a mud party + there were plenty of “oh my gosh are you okay?!” + “ahhhhhh” ⛈️ up a big hill + down the other side (or slide?), I laid eyes on the glorious redwoods aid station. I can only imagine how much more glorious it looks after a longer run. Quick toilet break + I was into the final third of the race.

Pulled out a note Mr 4 had written me which gave me a bit of a boost until the pavements of the city started killing my legs. The last 2kms were struggle city. I was welcomed into the finish chute by amazing supporters and almost knee high deep flooding.

Finished with a time of 2:52:30 + placed in the top 29% of runners from my distance, which I was super pleased with, especially considering how good I feel today.

Huge thanks to my coach, Kerry from @squadrun + of course @_sophiarietema for keeping me company + putting up with all my BS.

Race story:

I signed up for the half marathon, which was only my second time doing a half marathon in a race. My first was back in March at the @hunua_hillbilly, which was also my first ever trail race. So I went in using this race as a comparison to see how far I’ve come, with a goal of somewhere between 3:00 and 3:15.

At the 10km mark I was perfectly on track… and then the skies absolutely opened. Torrential rain + a 700m descent that instantly turned into a slip-and-slide mud fest = pure chaos 😂

I ended up finishing in exactly 4 hours which was well over my goal but honestly, I’m content with that. I ran on 3 hours sleep (cheers to the neighbours’ all-night rave) and literally got my period in the portaloo right before the race started 🫠 Add in the downpour, and I decided that this wasn’t going to be a race race, it was going to be a ‘have fun and send it’ race.

When we try to deny, shame, avoid, and shut down our emotions or any ‘part’ of us, we may think it just goes away. But the truth is, it is basically the same as shoving an old sandwich in a closet… the mold grows. 😳

Emotions that are unfelt and parts of us that we do not accept about ourselves grow and become dis-ease in our body. This one thing we thought wasn’t a big deal or we shouldn’t be upset about, can actually lead to physical and mental health issues. This is the actual manifestation of the unfelt emotion. 😢

So if you want to know how to feel the most free, alive, and happy in this life? 

Let yourself feel it all. Accept it all. And LOVE it all. 

And if you’re not sure how to do that or are scared to start (what if I can’t stop - is a common question I get), please reach out. I help my clients through this work and to the other side of freedom every single day. 😍🔥

You are beautifully human and that means all aspects of human emotions exist and are beautiful within you. 🥰😍

The next time you find yourself worked up over an old trauma, something you feel you’ve done “the work” to heal, and you start getting frustrated that it’s coming up again…. 😔😤

I want you to try this.😍

Try to think of this as one PART of beautiful you. The part of you getting triggered is not YOU, it’s one part of you and the version of you that lived through this big and potentially horrible experience. 

This part “coming up” doesn’t mean that you aren’t healed and it does NOT mean that you are any less lovable!

These hurt parts of us can be triggered by so many things - someone’s tone of voice, a smell, a sound… but whatever it is, this part of you is coming up to be seen and accepted. It’s coming up because it feels safe to do so. And by seeing it as one part of you, it’s much easier to then have compassion and love for this part.

Because guess what… all of that work you have done means that there is another part of you that is more healed and wiser and who can hold this other part with love. 😍💗

This is how you become your own healer and the one you have always needed!

Once you can do this, the more healed parts of you get to say to this other part, “I see you.. it’s valid that you’re here. You’re safe here, I’ve got you! I love and accept you!” 

And the beauty of this, is often that’s exactly what this part needs to fully integrate and no longer “come up”. 

This is the exact type of thing I teach my clients everyday and I hope it can be helpful for someone reading this. 🥰

One of my clients was SHOCKED when I told her I will never ever speak badly about myself…

It has become so normalized in our society to bash ourselves, and judge every inch of ourselves, that it is literally shocking when someone doesn’t do that…

There is so much NOISE about how we should look, how we should dress, how we should act, how we should talk…. The “bullying” is everywhere, why do we do it to ourselves too?

I remember in high school, I had amazing friends… and… I was also fairly frequently teased for “always being happy”… I was teased for having a bubbly personality, for exploding with joy when I was excited, for being expressive in my tone and how I spoke… 

And you know what I did? I quite literally changed myself… I lowered my speaking voice, I held back excitement, and I tried to act less happy…. How wild is that? 

It took years of inner work and putting in time with my self-love practices… I learned to fall in love with all of the things that make me, me! I retrained my mind to LOVE those special things about me..
I would get excited and jump up and down, and then say to myself “ I love how excited you get, it’s so cute when you get so excited!” 🥹🥹
And the healing happened..
It doesn’t happen overnight but a really good start is just making a promise to yourself..

I WILL NOT BE MY OWN BULLY. 

And when you notice those thoughts coming up, judging yourself, your body, your voice, your anything, you pause… you notice it… and you change it to… “I LOVE ……” whatever the thing is.

I spent hours sitting in front of a mirror looking at my “flaws” and saying I LOVE YOU to everyone of them until my curves became something  I didn’t hate but actually I felt sexy for.😊

So again, it doesn’t happen overnight but this is some of the most important work we can do… especially as women - with the insane standards put on us before we even hit puberty… 
When we show up to love ourselves deeply and truly, we give others permission to do the same. And I truly believe the world would be a totally different place if we all learned how to love ourselves.

If a healthy masculine man is interested in you, he will come to you. He will tell you, he will come to see you, he will ask you out… you will know.

You see, men are biologically programmed to go after what they want… in fact, this brings them great joy..😍

Obviously this does not apply to every single man, as humans are all unique and beautiful in their own way.

So if he is not pursuing you in the way you desire, he is most likely either not that interested or quite honestly he is not ready… because when he has done his own inner work and can feel proud of who he is when he rises to pursue you, you will have total clarity in how this man feels about you. And quite possibly end up in the more masculine role in the relationship (not attractive to anyone). None of which create a loving and healthy relationship… and often both result in your own pain.

But the beautiful thing is, for the healthy masculine who is ready for you, you won’t have to control, nag, or beg for his attention..

When an old wound or story comes up *again*, it is completely valid to feel frustrated, disempowered, even angry.. we might want to quickly shut it down and invalidate it because “I’ve already healed that”😤. 

But I’d like to invite you to try a practice the next time this happens.

Rather than seeing this wound or story coming up as YOU, I want you to see this as one PART of you. 

This is a single part of the beautiful kaleidoscope of you.

When we see it as one part, we can much more easily accept it and move through it from an empowered place.

And often these stories or wounds don’t make complete sense for the situation now.. but they do make perfect sense for this living part of you that experienced everything he/she did. And the truth is, if it’s still coming up, it needs to be loved, validated, and befriended.

The urge to shut it down really only serves to keep this wound growing mold in the closet. 😢 we might think if it’s quiet, it’s healed… until it comes out again in an explosive trigger moment.

So rather than shutting it down, we acknowledge this one part of us and treat it as alive and valid (because it is!).

Disempowered and Invalidating Mindset
❌ I should be over this 
❌I already did the work on this
❌This is so silly

Empowered and Validating Mindset
✅I see this part of me and it’s valid that it’s here
✅I’m sorry you did not feel safe at one point, you’re safe now. I’ve got you.
✅I love you. I see you. Thank you. 
✅I will keep you safe now. Is there more? 

It’s quite powerful to be able to see these waves that come through as parts of us and not US. This is a place of empowerment where you get to now be the older, wiser self, validating the story and the wound in the way that you always deserved. And truly, this is how deeper healing and integration happens. 🥰🥰

There is not a single part of you that is not worthy of being seen and loved.

I hope you’ll try this and I hope its helpful.🥰💗✨

Of all of the healing modalities and practices and tools and books and ceremonies I’ve done, one of the most truly life changing has been the practice of sauna/cold plunge. When I say it changed my life, I mean it literally changed my life by changing my nervous system. 🥹

I started doing this practice over four years ago hoping to help my ptsd symptoms and have been consistent with it ever since.. on the low side, 1-2 days per week and on the higher, 5-7 days per week. I do around 15 minutes of sauna and 1-3 minutes of cold plunge (honoring my cycle & listening to my body). 

Putting your body in a controlled “stressful” environment is a tool that allows you to train your nervous system to become better able to adapt to stress and triggers. 
When you enter the cold, your nervous system initially wants to freak out.. to put it simply, the nervous system interprets this as “I’m dying”. But in that moment, when you choose to not listen to that, to not go down the path of freaking out, you can actually go deeper and deeper into the peaceful state that ALWAYS exists within.. you find your breath and your center and then it becomes actually amazingly enjoyable.

Because of this practice, I would notice that loud noises wouldn’t jolt me, or my daughter having a big emotion didn’t take me with her… I can be the rock to hold it all.. I can handle discomfort. And I even find in actually stressful and big triggering moments, I can so easily find my peace - truly thanks to this practice. 🥹

Of course there are tons of other benefits to sauna and cold plunge that I’ll let you find on your own but this is my experience and it has been so profound that I hope many others will find inspiration to try it.

I am so grateful for the beautiful space of Drip Sauna here in Asheville. My new friends, the owners, Daniel and Evan are incredible guys with a beautiful passion for the tradition of sauna and cold plunge and they could not have done a better job creating an absolutely stunning space to experience it. From the lights, to the fire, right by the river… and to the gratitude and prayers they have spoken over the space. Everything about it feels nourishing and healing.

Bamboo of Trebah.

I have had a growing interest in bamboo in the last few years since moving into a property with a garden where the previous gardener had planted around 20 species of bamboo. I speak with said gardener, Melissa, regularly. Unfortunately, the bamboo in my garden has been badly maintained over the years (since Melissa lost control of the garden due to landlord changes) and I'm only now working with a few species, which I'm working on bringing back to thinned out and tall, where they had been cut into hedge form and essentially ruined. 

I mentioned to Melissa I was travelling to Falmouth and she recommended I check out Carwinion gardens as they were previously famous for their bamboo, and Melissa knew the previous owners through the National Bamboo Association. I contacted them and they'd sold a lot - but still apparently have beautiful gardens so I will likely visit them next time I go down that way, which I intend to next year.

Anyway, one of the places Carwinion bamboo went to was Trebah, which is how it made the shortlist for our visit. I definitely feel the bamboo was a highlight of this garden.

I went to Falmouth with brother Juddy at the weekend. I've got some photo dumping to do but I'm feeling a bit too reminiscent to get on that just yet.

Falmouth was my vibes all round. A bit too much so - it encapsulated all of the things I'm mega passionate about in a mega dose. I'd say to the point I'm a little overwhelmed.

The food, EXTREMELY vegetarian friendly (one of the best places in my experience), was incredible. The coffee shop choices were too many (in a good way). The bars are quirky and hugely vibey. There are books everywhere. The music of the general ambience is incredibly eclectic. The people are kind. The live music is top tier. The horticulture is endless.

It did all feel very "me". It's too far away from everything in my life to make a residence of, but it warrants a committed yearly holiday. 

I think takeaways are that I need to finally commit to getting a record and CD deck set back up and start moving towards physical as my default listening habit. I need more nick nacks and antique furniture in my flat. I need to double down on gratitude; something I practice daily anyway but want to get deeper with.

Ibiza diary: @eddiecraigmusic at @obeachibiza for Kisstory opening - probably the best party I've ever been to.

Ibiza diary: flora. Absolutely huge cacti and succulents, Bougainvillea and lots of coastal plants.

Something that struck me was that the idea of "drought tolerant" is probably a bit of a myth, even for these drought tolerant plants. Consider this is the very start of high season, and most plants I saw (other than those that were very clearly looked after properly) were in a poor state. Admittedly I'm talking mostly about wild plants or "plant and leave" approach, but it was notable how unhappy the plants looked in their habitat compared with our own native plants in their natural habitat and how luscious and happy they look.

I got back to my garden and it was sunny all day and then it rained whilst I was pottering around. It made me very conscious of why foreign invaders have always loved this country so much. It's made for luscious plants - i.e. food. If you want your tribe to survive, South East England is a dream home.

Ibiza diary: my first trip to Ibiza! Pretty crazy considering I've been in and involved with the electronic music industry for 20 years.

I always had conflicting preconceptions of what it might be like.

I'd always craved what I hoped Ibiza would be in my early teens - all of that amazing electronic music I grew up with in the 90s and early 00s, and happy free-spirited euphoric vibes dancing under the sun.

But I always worried that had probably been lost to the materialism and Reality TV-inspired plasticity that took over mainstream club culture. I thought it probably would have lost that Soul, the same way lots of music has since then.

Drugs too - I expected lots of people absolutely zombified off their face - one of the reasons I gave up clubbing regularly. 

Flying directly into the nightlife, I was going in at the deep end. Endless nightlife here. We flew in at night so managed to see the night view of Sant Antonio from our balcony before heading out. Thankfully, the people I was with included seasoned VIP veterans and headline DJs so I knew I could follow without ending up in the wrong places amongst stuff I was trying to avoid.

I was hugely pleasantly surprised by Ibiza nightlife. Everywhere is very clean, people feel generally very respectful and it just had an overall feeling of being fun without being in your face about it.

Don't get me wrong, there's a couple of strips which are exactly what I'd rather avoid - balloons, coke, young people falling over, rowdiness etc. but it surrounds particular places you can spot a mile away so it's easy to swerve.

Walking into a bar where Lewis Bones was DJing, him warmly welcoming us all, and us vibing and dancing getting in the vibe with Eddie Craig before he headlined Kisstory, then Lewis dropping Sambuca and the whole crowd going bonkers was a vibe. It's the first time I've seen Ed on the dance floor rather than behind the decks haha.

This set the precedence of what nightlife in Ibiza would be like every night (and day) I was there. Just very good, warm vibes; eating, drinking, dancing, surrounded by genuinely kind and instantly friend-level people.

I'm obsessed with electronic music all over again. ♥️

Saturday morning I facilitated a women’s circle on the topic of “your authentic life.”

And holy moly, the things I learned from the women in the room!

It reminded me (again) that authenticity isn’t about becoming someone new.

It’s about coming back to who you were before you started second-guessing yourself.

Before you started performing.
Before you started holding back to make other people more comfortable.

We went deep, and some of the things the women shared in our closing circle will stay with me for a long time:

💛 “Life is short. The quicker we take action, the quicker we create our own reality.”
💛 “I want to check in and ask myself: am I being authentic?”
💛 “I want more belly laughs with my friends.”
💛 “I want to love myself without conditions.”
💛 “Where am I still ‘shoulding’ when I can do it my way?”

And one that really landed:
“I want to remove fear.”
To which I gently added:
Instead of removing fear, what if we added courage?
Added trust?
Added self-compassion?

That shift alone can change everything.

I walked away feeling empowered. Humbled. Grateful.

For the opportunity , and because I got to hold space for what was already inside them.

Every single woman is carrying a unique vision for her life.
Something that tugs at her heart.
Something that feels just for her.

If that’s you, trust it!
It’s not random. It’s not silly. It’s not “too much.”

You’re here to live it.
And maybe even change a few lives along the way.

この度「BEHIND THE WALL」は、壁画の観覧を目的とした展示会『Wallternatives #2』を開催いたします。
『Wallternatives』は、本来空き家となる遊休物件を期間限定のミューラル(壁画)スタジオとして活用し、アーティストの自由な発想のもと描かれたミューラル作品を公開する、「BEHIND THE WALL」主催のプロジェクトです。第2回目の開催となる本展では、フロアを増やしさらに多くのミューラル作品を展開します。また、前回より参加していただいた作家自身による「ミューラルの更新」、新たな招待作家による「既存のミューラルに対する拡張表現」など、場所に帰属するミューラルだからこそ可能な様々な表現をぜひご高覧ください。

We lost my Dad this week after a 4+ year battle with cancer. He passed away after fighting hard and teaching us many lessons along the way. My Dad taught me about the world and how to find my place in it. He always set a high bar, but understood when things don’t always go as planned. He taught me to work hard, and enjoy the good things in life. You could often find him with a big camera — his passion for photography starting early. And he was never without a project. He gave me every advantage he could, including some he didn’t have. He challenged me to overcome my fears — comforted that he was behind me. Dad — I’m so happy you slept peacefully. We will all feel your loss every day, and miss your jokes and laughter, but I know you’ll always watch over us. I will carry you in my heart always.

One day when I’m gone, it brings me so much happiness that little pieces of me will be cherished and loved on others bodies forever🥹💖✨
Tattooing is a deeply personal energy exchange between two people. I don’t take this responsibility lightly. 
Every tattoo I have on my body I remember the session. I might not remember all the words that were said but I remember the feeling of our time spent together. Some good, some bad. And I’m reminded of those feelings when I look at my tattoos. 
I knew when I stepped into this industry that one of my main goals was to provide a safe and inclusive space for my clients. I not only want to give people a piece of artwork that will love flower, but the feeling of being safe with me. 💖

✈️ Taking to the skies once again — 90 years after its legendary first flight!

This beautiful two-seat Spitfire (registered BS410), painted in the iconic light blue-grey colours of the original prototype K5054, is setting off from Southampton Airport today on the first leg of the Spitfire 90 UK tour.

On 5 March 1936, test pilot Joseph “Mutt” Summers took off from this very airfield (then Eastleigh Aerodrome) in the prototype Spitfire, famously saying after landing: “Don’t change a thing.” Designed by local genius R.J. Mitchell, the Spitfire went on to become one of the most iconic aircraft in history and a symbol of freedom during the Battle of Britain.

Now, exactly 90 years later, BS410 is embarking on a special 9-leg circumnavigation of Great Britain (7–17 April), visiting historic RAF bases and overflying key Spitfire sites, with modern RAF aircraft joining in formation for parts of the journey.

A true tribute to British aviation heritage. What an incredible sight! 🩵

Roaring up the Goodwood hill in true Bentley Boys spirit! 🔥

This legendary Bentley Barnato Hassan Special is a one-off pre-war masterpiece. Built in the early 1930s for Bentley chairman and racing legend Woolf Barnato, with engineering genius Wally Hassan at the helm. Created with the sole mission of conquering the Brooklands outer circuit, it delivered — setting a blistering Class B lap record of 142.6 mph (with unofficial speeds over 143 mph) and capable of more than 150 mph on the straights.

At the 2025 Festival of Speed Timed Shoot-Out, this raw 8-litre beast showed its heritage hasn’t faded, thundering through the pre-war front-engined open-wheel class with unmistakable power and presence. Pure British racing history in motion!

A huge thank you to the owner and driver for keeping this icon alive on the hill.

The Southsea hovercraft (operated by Hovertravel) is such a cool piece of British engineering history! 

🚀🌊 Here are some fascinating facts about this iconic Solent crossing:

It's the world's only year-round commercial passenger hovercraft service still running today – and it's been going strong since July 1965 (that's over 60 years!). No other place in the world offers scheduled hovercraft trips like this all year round.

The route zips between Southsea (Portsmouth) and Ryde (Isle of Wight) in just 10 minutes – the fastest way across the Solent from land to land, no piers needed!

Hovertravel started with leased SR.N6 models seating just 38 passengers, and now runs modern 12000TD craft that carry more people comfortably (including bikes and mobility scooters).
Invented by Sir Christopher Cockerell in the 1950s (who tested the idea with a coffee tin and cat food can!), the first cross-Channel hovercraft trip happened in 1959 – but Southsea-Ryde became the enduring success story.

It's not just for tourists – commuters love it for the quick, direct shore-to-shore ride, plus easy connections via the Hoverbus to Portsmouth trains and city centre.

🌋✨ Hi, from the magical depths of Lanzarote's volcanic caves in Cueva de los Verdes 🌅

Stepping into places like Jameos del Agua and Cueva de los Verdes feels like entering another world—ancient lava tubes formed by the eruption of Volcán de la Corona around 4,000-5,000 years ago. These incredible tunnels stretch over 6 km long (one of the longest volcanic tube systems on Earth!), with parts extending 1.5 km underwater as the legendary Tunnel of Atlantis.

The harsh volcanic history of Lanzarote shaped this surreal landscape: massive eruptions created vast lava fields (malpaís), extreme aridity, and nutrient-poor soils. Yet, nature and human ingenuity thrive here! César Manrique, the visionary artist, transformed Jameos del Agua in the 1960s into a stunning art-nature fusion—think emerald pools, a turquoise seawater lake filtered through the rock, lush gardens, and even the world's only auditorium carved inside a volcanic cave (seating 550!).
Unique facts that blow my mind:

The crystal-clear subterranean lake hosts the tiny, blind, albino crab Munidopsis polymorpha—an endemic species found nowhere else on Earth! These little white dots adapted to total darkness and the brackish water over millennia.

"Jameo" comes from the ancient Guanche language, meaning natural roof collapses in the lava tube that create open caverns letting in dramatic light.

The caves served as natural shelters historically—locals hid from pirates, and shepherds used them for refuge.

The play of golden sunlight filtering through the collapsed sections, reflecting off emerald-green waters and rugged black lava... it's pure magic and a reminder of how beauty emerges from fire and time. Lanzarote's volcanic soul is unreal! 🔥

🌋✨ Lost in the lunar landscapes of Lanzarote's volcanic caves! 🌿 As I hiked around the iconic Cueva de los Verdes and Jameos del Agua, these resilient succulents caught my eye, thriving in the harshest conditions imaginable. Picture this: black lava fields from explosive eruptions in the 18th century (like the Timanfaya volcanoes that blanketed the island in ash between 1730-1736), relentless trade winds whipping through, scorching sun, and barely 150mm of rain a year. Yet, life finds a way!

These plants have epic adaptations to survive the arid, nutrient-poor volcanic soil that's super porous but rich in minerals. Many use Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) photosynthesis—opening stomata at night to save precious water during the hot days. Deep roots or mulch-like ash layers help trap dew and moisture from the air.

Spotlight on a few stars:

Aeonium lancerottense (endemic to Lanzarote!): These rosette-shaped succulents store water in their thick, fleshy leaves, blooming with delicate pink and white star flowers in summer. They've evolved to handle extreme drought and wind, often perching on rocky lava outcrops.

Euphorbia balsamifera (Tabaiba Dulce, Lanzarote's official plant symbol): A shrubby endemic with knobby stems and latex sap that deters herbivores. It clings to dry slopes, adapting to low water by shedding leaves in tough times and regrowing when conditions improve.

Aloe vera: Not native but perfectly at home in the volcanic terrain—its gel-filled leaves are a natural healer, and it flourishes without much irrigation thanks to the ash's moisture-retaining magic.
Nature's toughness here is inspiring—reminds me how we can adapt and thrive too! Have you braved Lanzarote's volcanic wonders?

IAB 25 – It’s a wrap

Ich hab die letzten 48 Stunden nur geschlafen (und geheult) und denke immer noch, dass ich das alles nur geträumt habe. Ich bin sprachlos.
Samstagabend habe ich glaube ich zum ersten Mal realisiert, was da eigentlich passiert und wie groß das alles ist.
Ich wurde zwei Tage lang mit so viel Liebe überschüttet, dass ich nicht weiß, wohin damit.
Eine so große Veranstaltung. So viel Solidarität. So viele Artists. So viele verschiedene, individuelle, tolle Menschen. So viele Besucher:innen. Ausverkauft. Und trotzdem so ein safer Space mit unbeschreiblichen Vibes. Alle für einen gemeinsamen Zweck.

Unser Spendenziel wurde bei weitem übertroffen. Jeder Stress, jede Träne, jeder Nervenzusammenbruch der letzten Monate hat sich mehr als gelohnt und war es wert.

Ich habe keine Ahnung, wie ich das verarbeiten soll. Ich bin einfach nur dankbar für das, was wir da gemeinsam erleben durften. Dafür, zu sehen, was wir als FLINTA*s auf die Beine stellen können. Zu sehen wie viele wir sind.

Ich schlafe jetzt noch ein paar Tage weiter und versuche irgendwie wieder klarzukommen.

DANKE an jede einzelne beteiligte Person.
Ihr habt mein Herz und ich werde dieses Wochenende wahrscheinlich mein Leben lang nie vergessen.

Alerta!

#inkagainstborders

It’s not that they hate the cot.

It’s not that they’re being difficult.

It’s not that they’re “just a bad sleeper.”

Here’s what’s actually happening 👇

Your baby has learned to fall asleep WITH you - your warmth, your smell, the rise and fall of your chest, the rhythm of your rocking.

About 10-15 minutes after they fall asleep, they transition from light sleep into deep sleep. 

Their brain does a quick environment check:

”Am I still where I fell asleep?” Asleep on you? Yes. 

Everything matches. Stay asleep ✅

In the cot after falling asleep on you? 

No. Something’s wrong. WAKE UP 🚨

This is called a sleep association. 

And it’s the #1 reason babies wake the second you put them down.

If you’re:

👉 Doing the 45 rock transfer dance every night 
👉 Laying under a sleeping baby for hours
👉 The only person who can get them to sleep
👉 Watching your evenings disappear before they’ve even started…this is the missing piece.

A quick note: if your baby is under 4 months, enjoy the snuggles. Self-settling isn’t something I’d push in the fourth trimester - they need your closeness to feel safe, and that’s developmentally appropriate. 

But from 4 months onwards? 

This is a skill you can help them to learn. 

Self-settling means your baby falls asleep in the SAME place they’ll spend the whole night - their cot. 

So when their brain does that environment check at the cycle transition, everything matches. 

They stay asleep.

It’s NOT leaving them alone to cry without reassurance.

I taught both my girls from 4 months.

They both literally learnt this skill within days.

From 4 months onwards, your baby can learn this too (if it’s important to you!).

The catnap cycle is one of the most exhausting phases of parenting 😭. 

Your baby falls asleep, you finally exhale… and 30 minutes later they’re up and screaming. 😮‍💨

Here’s what’s (probably) keeping them stuck - and what to do instead:

1. They’re overtired going into the nap

An overtired baby produces more cortisol, making it harder to link sleep cycles. A routine really helps from 4 months! 

2. They don’t know how to resettle themselves

This is by far the most common reason - and honestly? It’s simpler to change than most parents think. If they need YOU to fall asleep, they’ll likely need you again at every cycle, about every 30-40 minutes. Teaching them this one skill helps everything shifts.

3. The sleep environment isn’t optimised

Light, noise, and temperature all affect sleep. A dark room + white noise can be a total game changer.

4. They’re undertired

Yep, the opposite problem is just as real. If wake windows are too short, there’s not enough sleep pressure to carry them through a full nap. This can actually happen because parents are scared of them getting overtired so they put the down a bit early! 

5. They’re in a 2 nap structure when they need 3 (or vice versa)

The nap schedule creates an imbalance that almost always shows up as short naps. Timing and length of each nap matters more than most parents realise.

Change these five things and 2 hour naps become possible - not a fluke.

To the partner who feels like you can’t help settle baby - I see you. And you CAN help, in so many ways. Whether mum is breastfeeding or not! 

Here are 10 things that make a real difference in the first 3 months:

1. Take baby after feeds for burping and settling
After Mum feeds, you can take over. Burp, hold upright, and settle back to sleep.

2. Do nappy changes half way through feeds
That way at the end of the feed, baby doesn’t need to be fully woken up with a change.

3. Take baby out for a carrier/pram walk
Pop baby in the carrier or pram for an hour so Mum can shower or nap. Do this daily or as often as you can. If it’s in the morning - you could bring her a coffee back too 😉

4. Swaddle baby and pop them down
After Mum feeds, you do the swaddle and pop baby in bassinet. Get confident so Mum doesn’t do every single sleep.

5. Set up the sleep space
Dark room, white noise on, baby dressed right for temperature (use a TOG rated swaddle to guide you on layers). 

6. Offer a bottle feed at night
If Mum is expressing/combo feeding, do the 10-11pm feed so she gets some solid sleep. That unbroken stretch is life-changing.

7. Do the bedtime routine
Bath, nappy, swaddle—you do this while Mum rests or showers.

8. Clean up 
Dishwasher on, load of washing, wipe benches. Lighten Mum’s mental load.

9. Prep easy snacks
Make protein balls or stock grab-and-go snacks!

10. Be the voice of reassurance
Remind her she’s doing amazing and ask what you can do to support her. Be the calm when everything feels chaotic.

You’re a team 💪

Sick days.

An event. 

Travel. 

Sleep regressions.

You’ve followed the wake windows, you’ve nailed the timing, you’ve finally got some predictability back in your day.

Meet Alexis Eniola, the Heart Behind Eniola Hair

Alexis Eniola’s journey into the hair industry began not as a business plan, but as an act of love. When her sister faced the difficult battle of brain cancer, Alexis shaved her head in solidarity. It was a bold and deeply personal gesture that revealed not only the emotional impact of hair loss, but also the need for realistic, high-quality wigs that could help restore confidence.

Determined to make a difference, Alexis, an Australian self-taught hairstylist, wig expert and curve model began creating wigs that blend artistry with empathy. Her mission was clear: to ensure that anyone experiencing hair loss, whether from medical conditions or personal choice, could feel beautiful, empowered and like the very best version of themselves.

The brand name, Eniola, is a Yoruba word meaning “wealth” or “very important person.” It reflects Alexis’s belief that every client she serves deserves to feel valued and celebrated. Each wig, topper, and extension is designed with this philosophy in mind, offering not just style, but dignity and confidence.

Today, Eniola Hair is known for its premium, natural-looking human hair products. These pieces are crafted for comfort and realism, catering to everyday wearers as well as those navigating medical hair loss. The brand goes beyond beauty by offering a $100 medical hair loss discount to support clients undergoing cancer treatment, experiencing alopecia, or facing other hair loss challenges.

Alexis’s success is built on more than skill, it’s driven by compassion, resilience and the courage to turn a personal hardship into a platform for change. In doing so, she has created a brand that stands out in the beauty industry, not only for the quality of its products but for the heart and humanity at its core.

Through Eniola Hair, Alexis is redefining what it means to be a beauty entrepreneur showing that true success comes when creativity, craftsmanship and care go hand in hand.

A super easy activity that kept my 3 year old busy for 40 minutes. 
 
Before heading off to bed, pop some small dinosaurs (or any small toys) in a muffin tray with water and a drop of food colouring. Put the tray in the freezer overnight.

I’m not very good at cooking but I am good at making super easy snacks that I call ‘healthy’ because they’re not packed with sugar 😂

🥛1 cup of greek yoghurt
🌾1.5 cups of self raising flour
 
Mix and knead into a dough. Add extra flour if needed until it’s the right consistency.
Roll the dough out, spread with vegemite and sprinkle with cheese.
Roll it up, slice into scrolls and pop into the air fryer.

Air fry: 185°C for 12 minutes.

Pause and reflect before speaking

Sometimes our role is to be best friend
Sometimes our role is to be a brother or a sister

The 3 secrets to healing yourself and your relationships⁣⁣
⁣
When it comes to healing yourself and your relationships, some people make this mistake of having expectations on their partner to bend to their beck and call and every need and want, and quite frankly this is uncalled for and not healthy inside relationships.⁣⁣
⁣
If I have triggered you, read on.⁣⁣
⁣
Having unhealthy expectations of yourself or another person is the first mistake when trying to heal yourself inside your relationship.⁣⁣
The consequences from  holding these expectations are sometimes hurt, pain, suffering and even resentment to the person who had these high expectations of their partner.⁣⁣
⁣
Instead, focus on your thoughts and why you want what you want?⁣⁣
⁣
Focus inwardly on why you think you need and want the things you want⁣⁣
⁣
Start an open conversation and communicate with your partner about why you have all these expectations.⁣⁣
⁣
Perhaps through simply opening up, being vulnerable and asking for what you need and want from a place of openness and receptivity, you and your partner may feel a whole lot better and can work together to create a resolution so both of your needs are met.⁣⁣
⁣
So next time you think you need or want to nag him or her for not doing something or not doing enough, take a look inside yourself first, is there a better way of approaching your partner, communicating to your partner and a better way of asking for what you want without any expectation of the timing and the order it is done in?⁣⁣
⁣
Take away the control, take away the⁣
⁣
 expectation = takes away resentment⁣⁣
⁣
= better communication, trust and teamwork ⁣
⁣
= healing yourself + your relationships⁣⁣

undry tips that actually helped my loud brain 🧠
Take it or leave it 👋
• Laundry doesn’t leave the room unless it’s folded. Clothes oven → Fold → DONE
• Fold into people. Hand them their pile. Job = finished
• Take hangers TO the laundry. Sort as you go (game changer)
• Kids outfits get hung together — shirt + shorts (unless you’re a beige mum, then carry on 🤝)
• Kids can help. Mine’s on floor patrol + basket duty. It’s not just mum who needs clean clothes
• Bedding, towels & pet stuff = separate day. Always tub clean after the dog chaos or fifo clothes 🐶
• Fold bedding into “bed parcels” + store where it belongs
• 1–2 loads at a time. 7 loads = depression pile for a week
• Same day every week/fortnight or it’s stanky sheet roulette 😅
Not aesthetic. Not perfect. Just works. For me.
Peace out ✌️

The chaos my body has felt the last two days has been intense.

The dysregulated, overstimulated, on-the-brink kind.
I found myself genuinely angry over a poo stool.
A literal plastic stool.
Getting frustrated because my 2-year-old “wasn’t listening”...
when in reality, he just takes a little longer to process what I’m saying.

But when my nervous system is fried, everything feels like resistance. That doesn't mean that it is, but that's how it feels.

Everything feels loud.
Everything feels urgent.
I could feel the menty b coming in hot.
The snappy tone.
The tight chest.
The spiral.
So today I did something unplanned… but very self lovey-intentional.
I took myself to the beach after a tattoo touch up.
Alone.
Just the sound of the water and birds 🐦 
Food in front of me.
Silence.
The kind of silence where you can actually taste what you’re eating.

This picnic rug has holes in it because it’s been around since the dawn of time, that's the only thing I'm allowing to bother me right now.

And honestly… that feels manageable.

On the brink? This is your reminder that stepping away isn’t selfish.
It’s maintenance. Us parents forget that, often!

Sometimes the most responsible thing a loud brain parent can do
is ground yourself by the ocean
and breathe. 🌊🤍

I am back at it!!

Back on home turf, for good this time and getting out and about.

I have spent hours scouting for new areas, rock hoping, early morning freeze and 41km winds with rain, and only walked away with a handful of photos, how amazing & there is a reason for it.

How amazing is this spot. The weather rolled in as the sun set, allowed for some nice images.

This is a 8 minute exposure.....yep that's right, 8 minutes. This is why I only end up with a few images.

I love the super long exposures for these scenes, as I am a lover of rock formations, I love to showcase the beauty of them. And it gives me plenty of time to sit and enjoy the views.

Windy Mornings & Rainbows 🌈

Earlier this week was an early start for sunrise down at Binalong Bay, the weather was terrible, extremely windy (41km), very high crashing tides, rain set in, but what a morning to get some amazing photos. 

Elements make every image interesting.

This not the location for sunrise, in-fact I was driving home, hanging for a warm coffee and to get out of wet clothes and boots, but then this scene sprung on me. It would have been rude to keep driving and not get the shot!! So much going on, but it works.

I’m sitting in a dark room, two pudgy cheeks pressed into my stomach, marvelling at how these tiny bodies—not so tiny anymore, really—used to fit inside of me. 

On this day last year, 20 weeks pregnant, I hadn’t yet felt their kicks and now, somehow, their wobbly little legs are standing and climbing and their brains are learning faster than I ever thought possible. They’re just like me, really; still the same people that existed last year, and yet transformed into something entirely new. 

I didn’t think becoming a mum would change me for the better. Quite honestly, I thought I’d become some lesser version of myself; fractured, frazzled, run down & afraid, poor on time and desperately lonely. And though I’ve felt snippets of all of those things since their early arrival 9 months ago, I’ve found that, unquestionably, these boys have changed me for the better. 

My head carries more than it ever did before, and yet I’m learning to slow down; to focus on moments; to find joy in the in between. My friendships have shifted, but rather than dwindled, they’ve multiplied, stretched, and deepened. 

I’m quicker to laugh, to go with the flow, and to show grace. I’m less anxious, which is truly a miracle for someone who’s grown up with an active imagination and a jittery brain, and although there’s no performance review or pay check for this role, I feel more fulfilled than I ever have before.

Today, my first Mother’s Day as a mum, I’m so grateful for everyone who has helped me on this journey to motherhood; my mum, who has shaped who I am; my mother-and-sisters-in-law, who’ve shown me beautiful versions of motherhood, my family and friends, new and old, who’ve cried and laughed and made meals and sat with me, and Matt, who makes me want to have lots more babies so the world can have more people like him (only slightly kidding). 

And finally, I’m grateful to Reuben and Judah, who I somehow miss even while I’m holding them — thank you for helping me grow.

To the mum celebrating her first Mother’s Day… 

I hope you know that you are incredible.

I see the sacrifices you’ve made,

the friendships you’ve felt shift,

the body that doesn’t feel like you anymore,

the dreams that have been placed down, picked up again, altered, or forgotten.

I know it’s been overwhelming in the best and worst ways,

and you’ve carried the weight of fear and hope and expectation and exhaustion.

You keep showing up, smiling on the hard days,

and I want you to know that you’ve done it, you’re doing it; you’re their whole world.

I’m so proud of you,

—of this person you’ve become.

You deserve to feel seen,

to be celebrated,

to be cherished.

Happy first Mother’s Day, you beautiful woman.

They’re so lucky to have you. 🤍

Asking for help is hard; it’s something I’ve never been good at, and a muscle I’m having to exercise more and more these days since becoming a mum.

Recently Matt was away for a few days, and a few of you asked how I went about asking for help in that time— I thought I’d share what I did here for anyone who wants to get better at it with me 🫶🏼

1. I made a list of people who’ve offered to help in the past. I tried to think of the people I’d feel the most comfortable coming into my home and being with the boys.

2. I added those people into a group chat. I did this for two reasons; firstly, it meant that no one person felt like they HAD to help or that all the pressure was on them alone; they could see they were part of a bigger group effort, and secondly, it just simplified the organising of it all.

3. The hardest bit was to brainstorm *exactly* what I needed while Matt was away, so that instead of just vaguely asking for help, I could communicate really clearly HOW people could help. (I ended up saying “I would love someone to come over and help me with our dinner, bath & bedtime routine from 5:30-7pm.”)

4. I then gave everyone in the group chat a few different options (literally in a poll), so they could pick and choose what suited their schedule & capacity.

5. Finally, I made it really clear that I would really appreciate the help, but tried to also give an out (e.g. “I’d be so grateful for an extra pair of hands, but I completely understand if you aren’t able to this weekend!”). I didn’t want to downplay how much the help was needed, but I also wanted them to know I’d survive if no one was available — it’s a tricky balance to strike haha.

I’ve been learning that so many people want to help but just don’t know what to offer, so it’s really up to us to be able to communicate exactly what we need!

I hope some of this encourages you to be bold in asking for the help you need, and in learning to accept it when it’s offered, too 💛

One shot, then it’s put away. No distracting screen. No retakes to get it ‘just right’. Waiting patiently to see what I captured. Real moments, as they are.

Oh, so much joy. 🥹

Today marks three months with our “mini boys” (as dubbed by one of their little cousins haha). 

Becoming parents has been slow, chaotic, gentle, busy, difficult, natural, and a complete unfolding of ourselves, and all those things cancel each other out until it’s just you and your babies and blearily whispered “I love you”s at ungodly hours.

I’ve been surprised in the most beautiful ways, and the gap between what I expected motherhood to be and what I’ve felt so far has been huge.

I thought I’d feel cooped-up; I feel free. 

I thought I’d feel anxious; I feel at peace.

I thought I’d feel left out; I feel content.

I thought I’d feel overwhelmed; I feel capable.

I thought I’d feel out of place; I feel like I’m exactly where I’m meant to be.

It’s been three months of losing ourselves and finding them again and figuring out how to be a whole new family — something we’ll keep figuring out for the rest of our lives. 

Put simply? We’re so thankful for these boys and everything they’re teaching us. 

p.s. To all my friends still longing, waiting, hoping, praying — I see you. I’m praying with you. 🤍

Dear Judah & Reuben, 

You’re only 19 days old so you don’t know this fully yet, but you have the best dad in the world.

You have a dad who loves teasing and pulling pranks on people; a dad who finds humour in silliness and whose eyes disappear when he laughs. 

You have a dad who’ll take you camping and fishing and hunting, who’ll teach you about the world with wisdom and patience.

I’m so excited for you to grow up understanding just how lucky you are to be his sons.

Am I a mother yet? 

And if so, when did I become one?

Was it when I first saw that line, or the first night I stayed awake dreaming about my baby, who they would become, who they would make me become?

Was it the morning I looked into the toilet bowl, throat raw and insides empty, tears on my face, telling myself “this is for you”?

Was it the day I first saw the little jelly bean shapes on the screen, or the moment he told us “you’re having twins”?

Was it the first time I felt a flutter, or when one of the boys’ little kicks took my breath away? 

Was it at the appointment where they took six vials of my blood and left me dizzy, and yet all I could do was smile that my boys were growing?

Was it the first time a stranger touched my stomach and I winced, or the first time I met eyes with a mother in public and she glanced at my growing bump and smiled knowingly?

Did I become a mother when I bought the onesies? Or was it the nappy change table, or the cot?

Was I a mother the day we installed the car seats, or the day we learned how to fold down the pram?

Was it when we looked at the computer through tears, realising parenthood would take more sacrifice than we’d known and we gave up on our plans, our timing, our financial security?

Did I become a mother the day we hit ‘viability week’ and breathed a small sigh of relief, while knowing nothing is guaranteed? 

Was it the moment we sat on the cliff edge at sunset, whittling down our shortlist until we picked the boys’ names and said them aloud into the canyon?

Am I a mother now, when I look down and can’t see my toes, when rolling over in bed takes all my effort, when I don’t have the energy to sit upright at my desk, when my blood nose drips all over the serviettes at the restaurant, when I pee a little every time I sneeze, when I start to feel more like a vessel than a woman?

Am I a mother yet? 

A mother before they’re here? 

Does motherhood come upon me the moment the first of my babies enters the world and I feel their skin on mine, and hear their cries?

No. 

Because I’ve known so many women who never got to hold their baby in their arms and, even still, all of them — mothers.

I’m a mother, too.

6 months sober today! 🌟🌟🌟 I don’t post much personal stuff on social media, but here it goes.  I had my last drink in June on the way back from a wedding. At a place I drank at often, in a town where I drank too much. I had been talking about quitting drinking for years, and after my 40th birthday, I finally did it. It took a couple of years to gradually quit by taking longer and longer breaks and only drinking alcohol that I liked. I used alcohol to deal with almost everything from sadness to happy events. It was a little bit of an emotional struggle finding out what to fill that void with. Who knew that I could just exercise and go outside 🙃. I didn’t realize how much I was using it to cope with daily life until I quit. Realizing what’s working and not working in my life right now is also a struggle. I’ve got a lot to work on, but at least I’m headed in the right direction. 6 months doesn’t seem like much in the scope of a lifespan, but it’s a start, and it’s something I thought I could never do. I’m not looking for any congratulations, I just wanted to share a life update ❤️ if anyone needs to talk or have someone checking in on them from time to time, Reach Out! I also have a ton of quit lit I can send or recommend to you. Thanks to the friends I’ve gotten support from it means everything. See you in June when I hit my 1 year 🥰 #soberliving #soberlife

“Why ‘be more strict’ made everything worse with ADHD…”

“Be more consistent.”

“Be stricter.”

“Set clearer consequences.”

I heard this so often as a mother.

But with ADHD (and especially neurodivergent children), constant pressure and escalation often lead to *more overwhelm*, not understanding.

When the nervous system is already dysregulated, consequences in that moment rarely create learning — they usually increase stress on both sides. 💔

What actually helps is what comes *after* the moment:

calm co-regulation, reconnecting, and gently replaying situations without pressure.

Not to shame.

Not to punish.

But to build understanding. 🤍

You don’t need to become harsher.

You need tools that work with the nervous system, not against it.

Have you ever thought about the importance of setting boundaries for your mental health? Establishing healthy boundaries can be a game changer in your personal and professional life. They help you create a clear distinction between your needs and the demands of others, allowing you to prioritize your well-being.

Consider this: when you say "yes" to every request, you might feel overwhelmed and unable to focus on what truly matters to you. Setting boundaries empowers you to communicate your limits effectively, which can reduce stress and enhance your relationships. It’s not selfish; it’s a necessary practice for maintaining mental clarity and emotional balance.

Start small. Identify one area in your life where you feel stretched too thin and practice saying "no" or setting a limit. How do you feel afterward? The more you practice, the easier it becomes to establish boundaries in other aspects of your life.

There’s always a version of you sitting quietly underneath the noise…
the expectations, survival mode, wrong environments, wrong relationships, self doubt.

This post is for her.

Learning who you are and accepting yourself and finding peace of who you are becoming  is the actual GLOW UP. 

Not the outside 
Only the inside ❤️

For a long time I thought maybe I was “too independent.”

You hear it all the time, especially as a woman.

“You’re intimidating.”
“You don’t need anyone.”
“You’ve built your own life, you are too much in  your own strength… maybe you struggle to let people in.”

And I sat with that.

Because I don’t actually feel anxious when I’m not in control. I can go with the flow. I can trust. I can laugh when things don’t go to plan.

But when it comes to the really big things — marriage, children, building a life with someone — something shifts.

Not because I need to control every outcome.

But because some decisions aren’t small.

You’re not choosing a dinner spot. You’re choosing who sees you at your lowest. Who raises your children. Who shapes the atmosphere in your home. Who stands beside you in grief, stress, growth and the ordinary days in between.

Maybe some of us aren’t “hyper-independent.”

Maybe we just know what it feels like to carry heavy things alone.

Maybe we know what it feels like to be disappointed, to rebuild, to start over, to become our own safety net.

And when you’ve spent years building yourself back up, you become careful with what — and who — you hand your future to.

There’s a difference between not needing anyone and wanting to choose wisely.

I’m curious…

What’s one thing you became “too much of” because life asked you to be?

Too independent? Too strong? Too guarded? Too understanding?

I’ll read every one 🤍

10 Eastern European Woman Stereotypes That Are Suspiciously Accurate 😂

1. She’ll tell you she’s “not that pretty” while looking like she accidentally walked off a Vogue shoot.
2. Emotional support?
 No.
 Practical support?
 She has already solved the problem, made a spreadsheet, and packed snacks.
3. Her love language is feeding people.
 If you’ve left her house hungry, she considers it a personal failure.
4. She can survive a breakup, move house, start a business, and attend brunch looking completely unbothered.
5. Trust is earned.
 The application process includes references, a probation period, and ongoing performance reviews.
6. “I’m fine”
 can mean anything from “life is amazing” to “I’ve mentally buried three people and rebuilt my life this week.”
7. She was raised to be independent,
 then spends her 30s learning that accepting help won’t actually kill her.
8. If she likes you, she’ll roast you.
 If she’s polite, start worrying.
9. Her beauty routine looks effortless.
 It actually involves enough products, treatments, and discipline to launch a small corporation.
10. She’ll say she’s had a normal childhood,
 then casually tell a story that explains her resilience, trust issues, work ethic, abandonment wounds, and why she’s carrying half the world on her shoulders.

AND A MAIN ONE 

“I don’t need a man.”
Translation:
“I can survive without one, but I’d quite like a good one who communicates properly and doesn’t become my third job.” 💅😂

I spent years thinking I had to choose between two women.

The woman who wants peace.
And the woman who wants adventure.

The woman who wants to be home by 9pm.
And the woman who thinks 9pm is when the night starts.

The woman who wants marriage, babies and stability.
And the woman who wants to see the world and collect stories.

The older I get, the more I realise maturity isn’t killing one version of yourself.

It’s learning how to let them coexist.

Because a beautiful life isn’t built from choosing one identity forever.

It’s built from knowing which version of you needs the microphone in each season. #balance

I’ve realised something about myself.

I love conversations.
Profoundly deep and meaningful ones.

I love talking about relationships, human behaviour, personal growth, and all the messy, beautiful parts of life that make us who we are.

Messy beautiful and all so craving for acceptance.

For years, working in the beauty industry, I thought my job was lashes, brows, and treatments. But what I quickly realised was that people come for the service and stay for the conversations.

I’ve sat across from hundreds of women and heard stories of heartbreak, love, loss, resilience, dreams, marriages, divorces, betrayals, healing, and hope. It taught me that beneath what we look like, we’re all navigating the same human experience.

Then last year, I took the biggest leap of faith of my life.

I put myself into one of the most intense, unpredictable, public experiment imaginable. An emotional rollercoaster. An open forum where strangers had opinions on my relationship, my personality, and my life.

And somewhere through all of that, I realised I wasn’t just interested in relationships—I was fascinated by them.

Why we choose who we choose.
Why we stay.
Why we leave.
Why we sabotage.
Why we love.

This podcast feels like a natural extension of conversations I’ve been having for years.

It’s exciting.
It’s vulnerable.
It’s a little scary.

But it’s also one of the most authentic things I’ve created. 

I don’t know where these paths are leading me to but I know I have my ride or die by my side & suddenly nothing feels scary anymore.

Welcome to Love, Life & Lie Detectors 🎙️❤️

If you’ve ever questioned yourself, your relationships, or how to navigate this thing called life, I think you’ll feel right at home here ❤️

Find us all major platforms & please  share your feedback & show us some love !

Get your pep back in your step.

Not by becoming someone else.
By becoming more of yourself.

Find the pockets in your life where you filter yourself.

The room where you laugh a little quieter.
The opinion you don’t share.
The dream you downplay.
The joke you don’t tell.
The outfit you don’t wear.
The boundary you don’t set.

Pay attention to where the fear of not belonging is running the show.

Because every time you shrink to fit, you trade authenticity for approval.

And approval is expensive.

It costs you your fire.
Your creativity.
Your magnetism.
Your joy.
Your people.

The irony?

The things you hide are often the very things that create real connection.

Your quirks.
Your ambition.
Your weird ideas.
Your passion.
Your truth.

Not everyone is supposed to get you.
Not everyone is supposed to stay.

But the people meant for you can only find you if you stop performing and start showing up as yourself.

So ask yourself:

Where am I editing myself to be accepted?

And what would happen if I gave myself permission to take up the space I was born to occupy?

Your confidence isn’t missing.

It’s waiting underneath all the places you’ve learned to make yourself smaller.

Too much. Too loud. Too confident. Too emotional. Too seen. Who are you? How dare you? But we did this like that for 100 years before you ? But how did you daaaaaare?!!!

I used to think if I explained myself better, people would understand me. Now I know some people understand perfectly—they just preferred me smaller.

That power can be reclaimed.

Mindfulness: Practice being fully present in the moment. Notice the details of your surroundings, the sensations in your body, and your thoughts and feelings without judgment.

Slowing Down: Intentionally slow down your pace. Walk slower, eat slower, and give yourself more time to complete tasks.

Enjoy Simple Pleasures: Notice and appreciate the little things that bring you joy, like a cup of tea, a beautiful sunset, or a good book.

Disconnect: Take breaks from technology and social media. Instead, engage in activities that allow you to be fully present.

Prioritize: Focus on what truly matters to you and let go of things that don’t align with your values or goals.

Nature: Spend time in nature. Nature has a way of slowing us down and helping us feel more connected to the world around us.

Limit Distractions: Identify and reduce sources of distraction in your life, whether it’s clutter, noise, or too many commitments.

Practice Gratitude: Regularly take time to appreciate the good things in your life. This can help you feel more content and present.

Learn to say No: Don’t overcommit yourself. Saying no to things that don’t align with your priorities can help you slow down and focus on what’s important.

Breathe: Deep breathing can help you relax and feel more grounded. Take a few moments throughout the day to focus on your breath.

Dear Community,

For the past few years, I’ve had the honor of sharing breath work, cold plunges, and healing practices with so many of you. What began as a personal practice and a way to support myself has grown into something far bigger than I could have imagined.

However, I’ve come to realize that in pouring into others, I’ve forgotten to refill my own cup. The last two years have taken a toll, and I’ve been giving from a place of exhaustion. As much as I love helping others, I can no longer continue at this pace without first giving myself the space to heal and reconnect with my own practices.

With this in mind, I’ve decided to take a break from hosting workshops and events for the rest of the year. This isn’t a goodbye forever, just a necessary pause to focus on my own well-being, spend time with friends and family, and rediscover the joy that brought me into this work in the first place.

For those of you who have already given me deposits or have something booked with me, I will honor those events as I wind down my practice. I appreciate your patience and understanding during this time.

I won’t be active on social media during this period, as I feel the need to step away and create some space for myself. I encourage everyone to take moments for themselves as well, because sometimes the greatest healing comes when we step back and allow ourselves to simply be.

Thank you for all the love, and I’ll see you when the time is right.

With gratitude,
Miguel
