Emotion

We have a toxic, emotional relationship with food. There is first off healthy food, unhealthy food, there is okay food, sweet cheating food. There is indulging food… how about this. 

Throw all of those old negative fearful, hurtful thoughts about food out and just think… “food is food” it is nourishment for when you are hungry. It will help lead you to how you want to feel after being hungry, which is satisfied. 

Culture

Our culture is embedded with unhealthy food thoughts. They want you to eat their food at a restaurant because it gives them money. They make nothing off you having a glass of water. 

Bakeries display their food to make you think about eating. Cinnabon makes fresh cinnamon rolls to make you want to eat it. 

Our culture says bigger is better and have a “lunch deal” 2 for 5. 

Remember, before you indulge, ask yourself, “am I hungry?”

We don’t need to fear the scale. I know we have seen some high numbers. 

The number is just a number that measures your density between the earth and our gravitational pull. 

It is just a number. That number can either help us out hurt us. It isn’t the scale we need to throw away it is out negative self image.

How is it with our kids, they get on a scale and we are happy at their weight? But with ourselves, we are fearful, holding our breath and filling ourselves with anxiety? 

It is because of how we think. 

With our kids, It means they are growing… it is confirmation that we are not completely failing at this parenting thing. 
Even when a child is overweight or underweight, we don’t think like a failure. We think “what does our child need next?” 

But with us, we somehow think that the scale means we are a failure. We think the number is telling us we are ugly, not good enough, unworthy of accomplishing our dreams. 

Here is a new thought. 
The number is just a number. It tells us what is working or what isn’t working. What did you do differently the day before to be down a pound? What did you do to go up a pound? 

When we start thinking with curiosity, let go of the expectations of anything our weight, we can then finally move forward with love, respect, and grace day by day with our weights numerical number.

💫Healing old wounds,
💫 being overwhelmed with the desire to create and develop, 
💫feeling a lot of calm and joy in the work: 

💜its all been there the whole time waiting for me.💜

"Mollo" was my childhood nickname that my mom gave me. Im taking it back full force now and giving that little girl permission to do what she dreamed to do!

It was an absolute🧡 pleasure 🧡to finish off this project this week. My client wanted to tell the story of the goddesses of the norse mythology without being too obvious. 

After a lot of prep work, we came up with this design, and I am thrilled to share it with you all!

I am absolutely in live with mythology. 🤩

Norse and Greek are my favourites. The Norwegian broadcasting service NRK has a series made for radio that I listened to as a child called "Stjernene forteller" and as a small kid I was absolutely💥 BLOWN💥away by the dramatic retelling of Greek mythology. 

As a kid, I spent a few summers obsessed with the viking age and would only wear my viking dress! Haha! 🙈

As an adult I live Neil German's re retelling of the Norse myths in his book "Norse mythology " and I listened a lot to that book read by the author this week in preparation for this tattoo session.

Telling stories and expressing something that lives only in the imagination through a drawing, a painting, or a tattoo is absolutely magical. 

Bringing into view what can't be seen: the stuff of dreams, nightmares, and fairytales: that's what this is all about!

I hope you enjoy it and that your own imagination runs wild and travels to wonderful places.

🥰Hei dere!😀Her er et prosjekt jeg har jobbet på i det siste. Det er ikke helt ferdig, men må måtte jeg bare vise det likevel!

Viss du blar gjennom bildene vil du se tegningen som ble gjort på planleggings timen sammen med bildet av det arbeidet vi har gjort til nå. 

Det kan være spennende å se hvordan det ser ut som tegning ved siden av resultatet. 💕🩷

Ofte på tegne timer blir det mye kaos på huden og feite streker som ser ut som en tusj spagetti. 
Men ut av det kommer en tatovering tilpasset kroppen på en unik måte og det er veldig viktig: formene er tilpasset personens anatomi. Det er derfor vi tegner rett på huden i planlegging fasen.

💌 Del med noen som du vet går med tattoo drømmer: det å komme å ha en konsultasjon er gratis! Full tegnetime koster litt, men er en god måte å komme i havn på hva man vil ha. 

Små og mellomstore tatoveringer er jeg også utrolig glad i. Store prosjekter er kjekt, men de små eller mellomstore gir helt andre kreative utfordringer og jeg ELSKER å lage de! Ikke tenk at din tattoo ide er for " liten og kjedelig". Det er den ikke.💜

Spør i DM eller i kommentarfeltet dersom det er noe du ønsker å vite!😀

Hei mine venner! Hello everyone!

Her ser dere en ferdig cover-up jeg har laget nå i høst. For å dekke en veldig mørk "grim reaper" laget jeg en svart rose med hvite detaljer.

I fotoet her ser det hvite litt rosa ut: det er fordi det er helt ferskt og det er litt rødhet og blod. Jeg bruker ikke filter på så da ser det litt sånn ut. 

Med to sessions og veldig god pleie mens den grodde (mellom sessions) blir resultatet veldig bra!

Det er givende og spennende å jobbe med cover-up. Ikke alle tattoo artister liker det og det skjønner jeg veldig godt: begrensningene ligger der før man starter arbeidet. Det er ikke for alle. 

Men av en eller annen grunn så bare elsker jeg å lage cover-up. Det er en utrolig spennende prosess der jeg må bruke alt jeg har av kreativitet, teknikk og erfaring for å redde noe som allerede er permanent på noen sin hud og så gjøre det vakkert: det er utfordrende, spennende og veldig tilfredsstillende bår man får det til!

Å se en kunde lyse opp forran speilet og innse at det de trodde var håpløst kan bli noe fint: det er en utrolig god følelse!

Har du en tattoo som du tror er håpløs, som andre tatovører har sagt du må ta laser på eller bare gi opp? 

Sjansen for at jeg kan hjelpe deg er stor. Og kan jeg ikke det så skal jeg være ærlig med deg.

Gi en lyd så ser vi på det!

Gleder meg masse✨️🥰❤️

"Vidar (eller Víðarr) er i den norrøne mytologien sønn av Odin og jotunkvinnen Grid. Nest etter Tor er han den sterkeste av alle gudene."

ENGLISH
"In Norse mythology, Vidar (or Víðarr) is the son of Odin and the Jot woman Grid. Second, only to Thor, he is the strongest of all the gods."

I recommend anyone who's interested to search for info on Norse myths. Online, at the library and the bookstore.

 They are both entertaining and interesting.
I also love the retelling that Neil Gaiman created, where the myths are retold in an easy to read and enjoyable way.

I hope this can maybe spike your curiosity and have you do some reading and looking around of your own. Personally, I'm digging into some old fairytales from my childhood that I love. 

Sometimes, the treasures of the past can ignite the present moment✨️

Im having tea and snuggling in my blanket while looking at yesterday's work: One of my regulars and favourite clients through my years in Bergen came by for his appointment yesterday and got some work done. 

He has had a challenging few years, and it was so good to see him again! I admire people a lot for how they can still smile and get through the day when life gets hard.

This work is an example of something I do a lot, but I dont really talk about it, and thats free hand drawing and tattooing. 

It is such a normal part of my day. I didn't really think about it as something to mention,  but then my darling Carmensita @@blekknroll reminded me that freehand is cool to share! And of course it is. To someone who does not tattoo every day, say a client, it might seem wild to just draw on someone with a marker and then tattoo that design without any other stencil or tool. 

But we do it a lot. For one: it's a tattoo so personal, so deeply in the ownership of the client that no other tattoo in the world is the same. The client gets to see it take shape then and there: and there is no doubt this came directly to them from the artist #no AI haha! But that is very special. 

And for the artist: to make a tattoo sice and shape flow with the body, one of the most helpful things is drawing on the actual body. 

You can draw something stunning on a piece of paper and then when you stick it on the client with a stencil sometimes it's looks wonky and weird: it looked fine on a flat surface ,but bot on the anatomy of the client!

So drawing on the body from the start helps get that flow and helps the artist make the tattoo work for the body shape very quickly!

I hope this was interesting, my friend:  I'm here to answer any questions you might have about this way of creating tattoos!

Thanks so much for checking in on me: you know it helps me and inspires me tons when you like my posts or share them with your people😀 it helps a lot in continuing my creative work!

Thanks so much, and have a great day!

Hello fresh introduced this basic cottage pie to me! And I still use the basis for it.

I pan fry 400 grams of lean mince with 1 onion and garlic
I finely cut 1 carrot and 2 celery stalks with my Tupperware turbo chef (so my picky eaters cant see the veggies) add and cook off
Add 1 tablespoon of tomato paste, 1 teaspoon chicken stock paste and 1 teaspoon thyme
Cook off and thicken with a slury of Maggi rich gravy powder
Stir through a bag of spinach and layer in a baking dish 
Top with mash and sprinkle with parmesan cheese and grill til golden brown.

Two weeks today since our beautiful boy Zac passed away. Writing that makes me sick. I miss him so much. I will never not be wishing he was in my arms. I can barely breathe at this point the pain is so intense.

This is something I never thought I could survive. I kept saying there’s been a mistake I can’t actually survive this. There’s just no way. But because of my four other babies, I have to. They are the reason I get out of bed everyday - even if it’s not til midafternoon. 

Zac was so loved & so incredibly wanted. My body aches for him. My arms physically yearn to hold him. My milk is leaking. My face is raw from the constant stream of tears and tissues. My nose has been blocked for weeks from non stop crying. I just want to feel him on me - his soft white hair on my face - his big beautiful buggy eyes.

I’m trying to keep living for my other four children, while also letting them see what real grief looks like - the grief is so intense because our love for Zac was so big.

I want to thank everyone who has reached out, cooked meals, donated, sent flowers, cleaned our home, and packed away the baby things so gently. A total stranger baked me a certain cheesecake because it has a special meaning for Zac. People have been so kind. My friends and even strangers have literally carried us through so far.

And the community of bereaved mums on social media: a group no one ever wants to join - you are my lifeline right now. It feels like you are collectively throwing me a rope to hold onto. Seeing your posts shows me that it’s possible to keep walking through this, to still be a good mum, to still give my children a happy childhood, even with a hole in my heart. I cannot tell you how important that is. It is everything right now.

Zac - Mummy loves you more than words are capable of even expressing. Like I promised you, I WILL find you, please wait for me: My soul knows your soul baby and I WILL find you xx

I see Down Syndrome is all over social media  and international news right now because of the influencers who made the decision to terminate a second trimester pregnancy because of a Down syndrome diagnosis. 

It breaks my heart that we live in a world where that still happens. 

They say people become defensive when they feel judged and listen more when they feel invited in - so I wanted to invite people into the impact of losing someone with Down Syndrome has had on us…

Decades ago, before becoming a mother, I studied special education and planned to work with children with additional needs. 

Long before Zac existed, I knew first hand the EXTRAORDINARY joy, warmth, kindness, and light that so many people with Down Syndrome bring into the lives of those around them. 

I always say it feels like we won the lottery and somebody burned the ticket. 

Did you know that there are studies where people who have family members who have Down Syndrome report that they have higher levels of happiness because of their family member with the extra chromosome? 

I wish more people could sit down with families who love someone with Down syndrome before making assumptions about what that life looks like. 

I see so often in the Down syndrome community that when parents are given a diagnosis, they are given such bleak outcomes for their child and their other children’s lives. But when you ask the siblings themselves, they consistently report higher levels of joy and happiness due to their sibling with the extra chromosome. 

One of the things that I really struggle with and one of the greatest sources of pain for me comes from knowing the joy my other children have missed out on. 

And yes, I know better than most that Down Syndrome can come with a host of difficult, complex medical complications, but that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t give them a chance. It doesn’t mean we should take the opportunity off our other children to experience such joy. 

People talk about what families might have to sacrifice. I spend my days thinking about what my family lost.

The slogan for Down Syndrome families is “The Lucky Few” for a reason 💙💛

October is both Pregnancy & Infant Loss Awareness Month and Down Syndrome Awareness Month - and today marks four weeks since Zac died.

Zac had Down syndrome. We didn’t know before he was born. Every scan was “normal.” I’ve checked - and so has the team at Mater, one of the best in the country. Not even one soft marker. Even the scan minutes before he was born - nothing.

I wish so badly we knew. He would have been classed as high-risk and monitored more closely & maybe had a chance. I never knew that sometimes - extremely rare, incredibly “unlucky” & “almost unheard of” - there can be no signs at all.

Did you know the NIPT test can sometimes miss it, and that some babies show no visible signs on any scans at all? Me either. I’m not trying to spread fear - I just didn’t know. I think most people don’t.

What I’ve learned since is that the extra chromosome can affect everything - including the placenta and umbilical cord - sometimes making them fragile in ways you can’t see. That’s meant to bring comfort the professionals tell me - to hear “there’s nothing anyone could have done with the information we had” - but it doesn’t. It just brings heartbreak. It just seems so unfair.

They say understanding “why” is meant to help. But all I feel is pain, because I wish I could have known sooner. I would have done anything to save him.

There are quite a few potential risks associated with Down syndrome pregnancies - not just heart issues like I once thought - & if known, those pregnancies should be watched closely. Sometimes babies need to come a little earlier or need extra support.

I share Zac’s story not to create fear, but to share his truth - and how deeply he was loved. His siblings adored him. I would have devoted my whole life to him. He would have been idolised in our family. I just wish we knew.

Zac, my beautiful boy - I think of you in every breath, every heartbeat, every minute of every day. I miss you SO much. I’m sorry I’m not showing up the way I promised. Mummy just needs more time. 🧡

Three weeks without you.

Three weeks since I held you and felt your beautiful soft white hair on my lips for the last time my sweet boy.

Today, I moved freely for the first time. I sat on the floor with your big brother, rolling to reach balls, and realised I could move like “normal” again. Except nothing is normal - and nothing will ever be normal, ever again.

Today the bleeding has officially fully stopped as well. It feels like another punch in the guts. I haven’t pumped in 4 days. I know this is my body healing, but it feels like another step away from you - like losing the home that once held you. The body that I dedicated to you for almost a year and wanted to for many more - took a while to catch up, but it’s realising that you’re not here. The thought breaks me.

It feels like my body has quietly closed the chapter that was ours.

The walls that sheltered you have dissolved,
and your home is gone. I know biologically that pieces of you remain - your cells are still within me - in my blood, my bones, my heart - but my arms are empty - so I have to try to focus on knowing parts of you will never leave my body - and will be with me for life - until we meet again.

You’re woven into me forever - and maybe, one day, if my body builds another home, I pray it will do so with the memory of you.

I love you so much Zac Jacob White - with every breath until my dying day when I get to see your perfect face again 🧡

One month old today... I should be putting your one month milestone disc down and taking photos of you on my bed. The bed I had envisioned taking photos of you on with the light shining in from the window I stare at every morning wondering how this is our story. Instead this is the only photo we will ever have with any discs. 

Zac baby I miss you with every breath I take. I miss feeling your little feet under my right rib. I miss the excitement your siblings had every day waiting for your arrival. I miss the innocence. As a mum I want to shelter all my babies from pain - I desperately wish I could have saved you and I desperately wish they didn’t have to endure this pain. We are hurting in ways I don’t think was possible to even comprehend before losing you. 

I’ve had panic attacks for the first time in my life this last week and it honestly feels like my body is trying so hard to get me to you. The thought of living the rest of our lives without you is unbearable. The sounds that escape my body when I think of that are just gut wrenching. I want to scream “He should be here!!! He was meant to be with us!!! He was real and he was wanted and I don’t understand what is happening!!!!” 

A whole month without feeling you inside me. How can I possibly keep breathing when you don’t? It’s like I’m in a dark tunnel and the only hope is that one day I’ll be with you again - our family will be whole - and I feel guilty for that because your siblings need me too and you were so pure and full of love I know you’d want me to be there for them but HOW? HOW can I do that when I’m broken in ways that can never be fixed? There’s a giant gaping wound in my heart in the shape of your soul Zac & the pain of knowing our family will never be all together in this lifetime is the most awful thing. 

Your siblings start football today. I would give ANYTHING to be taking you strapped to my chest and have them proudly show you off. You were the most wanted baby. They miss you SO much baby. I love you with every cell in my body and my whole heart and soul.

People say the kids will surprise you with how resilient they are. Maybe. But maybe they’ll surprise you in how deeply they can feel pain as well. 

I think it’s probably hit Hunter the hardest. From the start of my pregnancy to the end he had the biggest growth and just became the sweetest kid - he absolutely loved on my belly daily. Talked to Zac every single day for at least the last 5 months telling him he was his big brother and he loves him so much. 

He just really was the most excited I think. Not the most obvious - that will always be Joey - but I think he thought about it the most and was so ready to hold his baby brother and love him on the outside.

Every morning he’d be the first to wake up and he would climb into my bed, kiss my belly, and say, “I love you, Zac.” The last few days, he’s gone to do it out of habit… and then remembered. And his little heart breaks all over again and he cries.

I watched back a video from the hospital yesterday and realised (that I didn’t realise at the time) he was quietly asking me if there was anything we could do so Zac could stay. It broke me.

You grieve for your baby - but as a mother, you grieve a different loss all over again for each of your surviving children too. I don’t know yet how I’m going to show up for them to be the mother they deserve… I just know that at some point, I have to.

You need to understand this technology. Period. Happy to answer any questions I can in DM’s - Why? Because in an increasingly uncertain world, understanding diversification is crucial so that moving forward, more “good guys” can win.

“Never take advice from someone you wouldn’t trade places with.” That’s it. That’s the quote I try to live my life by. 

How cool is it that you can just hear something one day that resonates so deeply with you & then decide to live your life by it.

Whether it’s in motherhood, relationships, health, finances, work, lifestyle - anything. If they aren’t living a life I would be happy to look back on & claim as my own, I’m taking their advice with a grain of salt. If they don’t have what I want - WHY would I listen to them?

So many people are stuck living lives doing things that they don’t actually want to do -  but they’ve been told that they “should” - should get good grades, should go to uni, should get a secure job, should get married and settle down - should should should - so they don’t take a chance & try something new and live the life that they really want to live because they’re stuck taking advice from people who - are often genuine & well-meaning 
& care for them - but haven’t achieved what they really want in the first place. 

That’s madness. We get one life & it is SO short. Don’t waste it listening to the advice of people who aren’t living the way you want!

I seek out people who have what I want. I model them. I do all the courses, listen to the podcasts, read the books (or more accurately listen to the audible books because mum life), jump on the trainings, join the groups. Even when it’s inconvenient (when is anything ever convenient with four young kids at home 24/7?!) My social media feed is curated to specifically follow the people that I know will feed my mind & inspire me to continue to go after the life that I want to create for my family first. I’m intentional with it. 

Your journey is yours alone. It doesn’t have to make sense to everyone currently around you. Surrounding myself with those who inspire me & have achieved what I aspire to has been the most impactful thing in my life to date. Let go of the noise from those who don’t understand your vision. You don’t have to live life the way you’ve been led to believe you do. You can do whatever you want! We all have the power to create the life we desire - choose your influences wisely x

Grateful to the Mexican American Civil Rights Institute (@somosmacri) for inviting me to speak at their 7th Annual Symposium in San Antonio.

MACRI is the nation’s first museum and archive dedicated to preserving, documenting, and sharing the history of Mexican American civil rights, a critical mission at a time when so many stories are being challenged, erased, or forgotten.

This is an excerpt from my opening address:

“They believed in a future they would never see. They believed in us.

And that is why I want to begin this morning not with politics, statistics, or policy.

But with memory. Because memory matters.

Memory tells us who we are. Memory reminds us where we come from.
Memory whispers that even in moments when the world tries to erase us, diminish us, or silence us, we belong to something larger than fear.”

We belong to a people, to a legacy, to a story.

And this morning, I come before you carrying the memory of a people who have always been here.

Because our story did not begin yesterday.

Before there was a border, we were here.

Before there was a debate about whether we belonged, we were here.

Before our stories were politicized, criminalized, distorted, and erased, we were here.

Can you say that with me?

We were here.

Mexican people.
Indigenous people.
Campesinos.
Workers.
Dreamers.
Inventors.
Students.
Organizers.
Artists.
Families.

We have always been here.

Not as a footnote in someone else’s history.

Not as newcomers seeking permission.

Not as strangers in a land we helped build.

We have always been here, helping shaping this nation with our labor, our culture, our courage, our sacrifice, and our dreams.

And yet, for generations, this country has struggled to fully recognize the humanity, labor, sacrifice, and brilliance of Mexican people in the American story.

But despite every attempt to erase us, we endured."

My brother, Edwin Raymond @e.raymond_ 

Today, New York City sees Sheriff Raymond. But many of us remember the years before the title.

I remember meeting Edwin in the aftermath of the President Obama’s Task Force on 21st Century Policing, during a moment when our nation was wrestling with questions of accountability, legitimacy, and trust. What struck me was not that he wore a badge. It was that he was willing to risk everything that came with it in service of the truth.

When speaking out would have been easier to avoid, Edwin chose courage. When silence would have protected him, he chose integrity. When retaliation came, he kept going.

At @nyjusticeleague we stood with Edwin and NYPD12 because we understood that his fight was larger than one officer’s experience. It was about whether people who tell the truth would be punished or protected. Whether accountability could exist inside institutions and whether courage still mattered.

There were moments when the road ahead seemed uncertain. Moments when the cost of doing the right thing appeared greater than the reward. Yet Edwin never abandoned his principles. He never stopped believing that public service should be rooted in justice and humanity.

Today, as he takes on this new role, I am reminded that integrity is not a dead end. It is a longer road. A harder road. But sometimes, if you stay faithful to your values, it leads exactly where you were meant to be.

Edwin, thank you for showing us that courage is not the absence of fear, but the willingness to move forward despite it. Thank you for reminding us that truth matters. And thank you for proving that even in difficult times, character still counts.

I am proud to call you my friend, my brother, and a fellow believer in justice.

As Dr. King reminded us, “the arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice.” Today, we celebrate one of the people who helped bend it. Congratulations, Sheriff Edwin. ❤️✊🏽

Almost 15 years ago, Mr. Belafonte sent me to Mexico to find my roots.

When I arrived in Zacatecas to meet my parents for their wedding anniversary, my father had our driver stop in the middle of the highway so he could show me an agave plant growing in the fields. The man tending the agave cut a piece and my father handed it to me to taste.

Standing there, he told me the beautiful story of the agave, how for centuries it has sustained Mexico. How our people used it for food, medicine, fiber, and for the spirits that bring families and communities together. A plant that survives in the harshest conditions, rooted deep in the earth, resilient and enduring.

That moment stayed with me. It was about more than a plant. It was about understanding where we come from, the land that nourished our ancestors, and the quiet strength that runs through our story as Mexicans.

When I returned to Mexico City last year and saw agave again growing beside bold modern architecture, I was reminded of that day on the highway with my father. How the past and present live side by side in Mexico. How our roots remain, even as we continue to grow. Circa March 2025 📷 by @argelia23

“Intersectional Feminist Organizing: An Intergenerational Epistemology Rooted in Liberation Movement.”

The article explores how intersectional feminist organizing is rooted in lived experience, collective wisdom, and the intergenerational leadership that has always powered movements for justice.

Women of color have long carried the labor of freedom movements, often without recognition, yet our organizing traditions continue to shape how communities build power, sustain resistance, and imagine liberation.

This work reminds us that movements are strongest when we honor the knowledge passed from one generation to the next, when we center those most impacted by injustice, and when we organize not just for reform, but for transformation.

As we mark International Women’s Day, I invite you to revisit this piece and reflect on the role each of us plays in building movements grounded in care, courage, and collective liberation.

The struggle for justice has always been intergenerational. And the future of our movements depends on how we nurture the leaders rising now.

She dreamed of becoming a doctor, to help people, to heal. She loved the sea. She loved the color pink. She loved her family. She loved to play. She was a child, exactly as children everywhere are: full of tenderness, curiosity, and big dreams for a future she never got to live.

This portrait is a moment of remembrance, and an act of refusal. Refusal to let her be reduced to a statistic. Refusal to let the world look away.

Hind’s story, told in The Voice of Hind Rajab (@thevoiceofhindrajabfilm), is not an exception. It is the story of tens of thousands of Palestinian children whose names we will never know, whose dreams were never recorded, whose lives were stolen in silence.

Remembering Hind is a call to action, to do everything in our power to protect and fight for the millions of Palestinian children who are still trying to live. To show up and demand every child be afforded the right to live. To play. To hope. To dream. To live in dignity and not constant fear.

Today and every day, we remember Hind and every child who has been killed and every child who needs us to show up for them.

I keep thinking about Liam.

He’s five.
In kindergarten.
Still has all his baby teeth.
Still believes grown-ups will do the right thing.

I have a five-year-old too. His name is Damacio.

They’re the same age.
Same grade.
Same smile.
Same brown skin.
Same hope tucked into their small bodies.

When I drop Damacio off at school, I watch him walk in with his backpack bouncing, already thinking about recess and snacks and whatever small adventure the day will bring. I expect to pick him up. I assume he’ll come home.

Liam didn’t.

Instead, he stood outside his home in the cold while adults with power refused every option that would have kept him safe. His mother was inside. Neighbors were there. School officials begged to take him. Someone kept saying, “I will take the child.”

And still, ICE took him.

People are arguing about policy and procedure. But Liam is not a policy.

He’s a little boy who should have been allowed to go inside his home, take off his shoes, and ask what's for dinner.

When I look at his face, I see my son. I see how easily this could be Damacio. How easily it could be any of our children.

This is what breaks me:
Five-year-old black and brown boys don’t get the benefit of innocence.
They get suspicion.
They get handled.

No child deserves this type of treatment.

Liam deserves to be home.
He deserves to feel safe.
He deserves a childhood that doesn’t include fear.

And so does my son.
And so do yours.

There’s a particular kind of fear that settles in your bones when you realize your body, your brown skin, your accent, your existence, has been marked as suspicious. When the simple act of living, of loving your family, of driving to work, can make you a target.

Lately, I find myself, and my own family, walking around with our passports in hand, as if a piece of paper could prove our belonging. We carry them like armor, hoping they might protect us if questioned, detained, or profiled.

But deep down we know, it won’t save us.
Because to them, our brown skin still reads as foreign. Our existence still feels like a threat.

A U.S. citizen detained while his toddler cries in the backseat.
A pastor shot by ICE while pleading for mercy.
Children zip-tied on the pavement.
A father having a seizure while clinging to his baby.
A mother dying in detention, her newborn laid on her chest.
A daycare teacher dragged away in front of terrified children.
ICE agents firing on a man warning them that kids were arriving for school.

They call it law and order.
We feel it as fear and humiliation.

We deserve to live without that weight, without having to prove our right to be here, to breathe, to exist.

Because we didn’t cross the border, the border crossed us. And our ancestors crossed back to reclaim what was already, rightfully, ours.

For every family that clutches papers like lifelines, for every child taught to “stay calm if they stop us,” for every ancestor who crossed borders so we could live free, we remember:

Our existence is not the crime.
The system is!

Quran 4:145 Tafsir Ibn Kathir
The Prohibition of Wilayah with the Disbelievers Allah forbids His believing servants from taking the disbelievers as friends instead of the believers. This includes being friends and associates of the disbelievers, advising them, being intimate with them and exposing the secrets of the believers to them. In another Ayah, Allah said, لاَّ يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَـفِرِينَ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَىْءٍ إِلاَ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنْهُمْ تُقَـةً وَيُحَذِّرْكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ ( Let not the believers take the disbelievers as friends instead of the believers, and whoever does that, will never be helped by Allah in any way, except if you indeed fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you against Himself ). meaning, He warns you against His punishment if you fall into what He has prohibited. This is why Allah said here, أَتُرِيدُونَ أَن تَجْعَلُواْ للَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَاناً مُّبِيناً ( Do you wish to offer Allah a manifest Sultan against yourselves ) meaning, proof against you that warrants receiving His torment. 
Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Ibn `Abbas commented; سُلْطَاناً مُّبِيناً ( manifest Sultan ), "The word Sultan in the Qur'an means proof. " There is an authentic chain of narration for this statement, which is also the saying of Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Sa`id bin Jubayr, Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and An-Nadr bin `Arabi. The Hypocrites and the Friends of Disbelievers are in the LowestDepth of the Fire, Unless they Repent Allah then states that, إِنَّ الْمُنَـفِقِينَ فِى الدَّرْكِ الاٌّسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ ( Verily, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire; ) on the Day of Resurrection due to their tremendous Kufr. Al-Walibi `Ali bin Abi Talhah said that Ibn `Abbas said, فِى الدَّرْكِ الاٌّسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ ( in the lowest depths (grade ) of the Fire;) means, in the bottom of the Fire. Other scholars said that the Fire has ever lower depths just as Paradise had ever higher grades.

FYI….Pgh has the chance to pass 18 weeks of paid time off for moms, people experiencing loss, temporary disability or anyone who needs time off when life changes.

Ask me about how to make this happen if it’s important to you.

A couple questions for y’all…

Did you get time off work after having your first baby? Your second? Your third?

Did you get time off after losing someone you deeply loved?

If you experienced a disability, whether it was temporary like a broken leg or something you still navigate today, did you get the time and support you needed to adjust to your new reality?

If the answer is no, it’s because Allegheny County still does not have mandatory paid leave protections for workers.

But we have a chance to change that.

On June 2nd at 5:30 PM, there will be a public hearing at the Allegheny County Courthouse regarding mandatory paid leave. Then on June 16th, Allegheny County Council will receive a proposal to either pass or deny 18 weeks of mandatory paid leave in Allegheny County.

Brown Mamas and I will be there advocating for families, caregivers, workers, and everyday people who deserve time to heal, grieve, recover, and care for themselves and their loved ones without risking their livelihood.

We would truly love your support and presence.

Because rest, recovery, caregiving, and healing should not be luxuries.

If we don’t show up now and put forward clear recommendations in the Comp Plan, we will see more of the same.

If we want sustainable, community-centered growth, the Comprehensive Plan must continue — and our voices must be in it.

Another life saved!! Cecal Volvulus>>dead bowel.  A colonic volvulus occurs when a part of the colon twists on its mesentery(blood supply) resulting in acute, subacute, or chronic colonic obstruction. The main types of colonic volvulus are sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus. This was a case of cecal volvulus. 

2 conditions must be present for the development of a cecal volvulus: (1) an abnormally mobile segment of cecum and colon and (2) a fixed point around which the mobile segment can twist. The second condition occurs by normal ileocolic (small to large intestine) attachments, but also by  abnormal adhesions( scar tissue) after surgery or appendicitis.

More swarm traps!
Why catch wild #bees? 
Well, hopefully they come from bees in trees, not bees from neighbors. That means the colony they came from lived without being fed or treated for at least a season. So we are collecting varroa and disease resistant genetics to keep from feeding sugar (the bees have good foraging timing and instinct for raising babies at appropriate times) and treating with mitucides (the bees can handle a parasite load and can clean themselves). 
Even organic bees can be fed sugar and are almost always treated for mites. They say it's essential oils or plant derived, but what they don't tell you is it's synthetic oils and super strong. Also expensive. And then the sugar feeding. Which is wild. I may be on a learning curve not treating my bees that way, but it will pay off. My goat herd is treatment free too. So are my birds and bunnies. It took a few years to learn how to keep them healthy. So in a few years I'll get it with the bees too. 
My birds sleep in trees. My bunnies sleep in holes in the ground. Our goats eat wild foods. I'm sure it's possible with the bees to get out of the treatment system. It's genetics and husbandry.

We're almost home from Missouri and the Natural Beekeeping conference with Dr Leo! The truck is full of Layens bee equipment, thanks to @wncagoptions and I am really ready to hang the rest of these swarm traps!
What an enlightening and enlightened weekend. 
I wasn't sure what I was getting into. Fifty people in a workshop sounded large. I don't love crowds or strangers. 
@gs_glass reminded me that it was fifty people wanting to keep bees naturally and were willing to travel and pay to learn about it. 
They were my kinda people. It was fantastic. I learned lots about bees, and am recharged and inspired and changed. 
Dr. Leo is an engaging teacher. I feel equipped. If you don't believe you can keep bees treatment free on a commercial scale, you're incorrect. I saw it myself. I was in an apiary of completely treatment and sugar free bees, saw the first spring inspection. Saw the healthiest brood patterns and most beautiful comb.  I have had bees long enough to recognize the robust health of this bee operation. 
My hive equipment is equally stunning. Dr Leo gives away the plans on horizontal hive.com but what they make is so much nicer than what I am able to construct - I'm still building more but I got to see the woodworker hand sanding the boxes. I'll share pictures after it's unpacked this week.

I'm buying and building a version of all the Layens equipment- hives, swarm boxes, frames. The bee beds we (I'm going to not be able to do them alone) are building from scratch. 
Follow for our treatment free bee adventures!
We have had bees for years now but treated one year out of the five. We have lost them all twice. 
So I'll be candid about our experience. For this to be successful a lot of learning has to happen. 
This switch to Layens Horizontal Hives is part of healthier bees without intervention. The frames allow for a deeper honey band above their winter cluster to sustain them in the winter.
I don't use pharmaceutical intervention in our livestock or family unless it's a last ditch effort.  And that doesn't mean we or our animals suffer from disease or problems. It's the opposite. We're super healthy and so are our animals and plants. The bees will be the same - learning curve but not an impossibility.

Those of you who know me know I'm for kindness to ourselves and Earth first. I'm sorta wild in the forest sense. Don't wear plastic, and hate the plastic bags mushrooms are grown in. I haven't solved everything, but our oysters are grown in reusable buckets. But lions mane has been trickier to ditch the bags. I thought. I have tried buckets and runs but since the accident can't lift heavy sawdust out of a sterilizer. So I tried jars. Super easy. Honestly it's easier than bags. I didn't even fully sterilize these jars of locally milled sawdust. I didn't do it long enough. The mycelium didn't care. Colonized quick. As always, it's just grain spawn on millet put into a sterilized sorta jar of sawdust and incubated a week. I put them in the room with the lids cracked for a week before removing the lid. I left a hole in the middle of the sawdust in the PC and put a spoonful of spawn in it. Voila.

Der „Kontextmismatch“ (Kontext-Missverhältnis) in der Psychologie beschreibt bei Diaspora-Gemeinschaften während eines Krieges in der Heimat das Phänomen, dass die psychische Realität der Migranten im neuen Land drastisch von der täglichen Lebenswirklichkeit der Menschen im Kriegsgebiet abweicht. Dies führt zu spezifischen psychischen Belastungen, Identitätskrisen und oft zu einer „unsichtbaren“ Traumatisierung, da die Betroffenen physisch in Sicherheit sind, psychisch aber im Krieg leben.

Auswirkungen auf die Psyche:

Trauma trotz Distanz: Diaspora-Mitglieder erleben „indirekte Traumatisierung“ durch den ständigen Kontakt mit Nachrichten, Videos und Schilderungen aus dem Kriegsgebiet.

Chronische Angst und Depression: Die ständige Sorge um Angehörige, die Ungewissheit und die mediale Konfrontation mit Gewalt führen zu Schlafstörungen, Angststörungen und Depressionen.

Entfremdung: Die Diskrepanz zwischen der „normalen“ Welt des Aufnahmelandes und der apokalyptischen Realität der Heimat erzeugt ein Gefühl der Entfremdung von der neuen Umgebung.

Frogs were a significant part of my life while I was growing up in San Jose, a creek (all walled in cement but still one of the area’s natural paths for a creek) runs behind my family’s home and every spring, we would start to hear ribbits from the creek until it would grow into a chorus and we would see tiny green frogs hopping around our backyard. My sibling, family, friends, and I would spend many evenings catching frogs in the backyard and playing ping pong. They would love to hop into the house even and we’d have to let them back outside. These frogs helped teach me how to care for the natural world we’re all a part of. “Kaeru” means frog in Japanese and it also means “to return home,” which struck me as so fitting for these little creatures. Even though now the county doesn’t leave the creek “on” enough to allow the frogs to return, I still think of them often and they remind me of home.

🚨Warum AI „Kunst“ problematisch ist und ich sie jetzt schon nicht mehr sehen kann.

💜Ich bin Künstlerin – ich erschaffe meine eigenen Werke. Warum sollte ich einfach copy-pasten, was eine Maschine mir ausspuckt? Ein Tattoo ist mehr als ein Bild auf Haut. Es ist Handwerk, Seele und Absicht.
Und lass uns kurz ehrlich sein – AI-„Kunst” hat ein paar ernste Probleme:
⚠️ Diebstahl ohne Einwilligung – KI-Modelle werden auf den Werken echter Künstler trainiert, ohne deren Erlaubnis oder Vergütung.
⚠️ Kein Urheberrecht – AI-generierte Bilder gehören rechtlich niemandem – und können nicht wirklich geschützt werden.
⚠️ Keine Aussage – Eine KI kennt keinen Schmerz, keine Freude, keine Geschichte. Was sie produziert, ist leer.
⚠️ Entwertung von echtem Handwerk – Wenn Kunden AI-Outputs als Vorlage bringen, wird jahrelange Ausbildung und Können auf einen Klick reduziert.
⚠️ Irreführung – Vieles, was als „Kunst” verkauft wird, ist generiert – und das wird oft nicht kommuniziert.
Meine Kunst kommt aus mir. Und das wirst du auf deiner Haut spüren. 🖤🪡

UND! Stell dir vor du möchtest richtige Anpassungen der AI Vorlage… dein „ARTIST“ wirds womöglich nicht richtig hinbekommen, wenns nicht selbst gestaltet ist…

VERSTEHE: Der Unterschied zwischen Tattoo Artist und Tätowierer*in ist Kunstwerke selbst zu gestalten und nicht einfach nur fremde Vorlagen zu kopieren (was strafbar ist, außer bei AI).

NUTZT KI um schneller ne E-Mail zu schreiben, nicht als tattoo Vorlage. Frag Deinen Future artist, ob eigene Designs erstellt werden. Leider verzichten viele auf die verpflichtende Kennzeichnung.

Du willst ein echtes Kunstwerk auf deiner Haut, mit Kreativität, ganz einzigartig, nur für dich gestaltet?
Dann bist du hier genau richtig ✨

A user reportedly lost 386,300 USDT after sending funds to a fraudulent wallet address embedded within their transaction history. 

According to reports, scammers had previously inserted a nearly identical address into the user’s wallet activity, making it appear as a legitimate past transaction. 

The attack relied on subtle manipulation —
the fake address matched the original at both the beginning and end, with only minor differences hidden in the middle section, which users rarely verify carefully. 

As a result, the victim unknowingly copied and transferred funds to the malicious address, leading to an irreversible loss.

This incident highlights a growing threat known as address poisoning, where attackers exploit user habits and interface design to create misleading transaction records.

In crypto markets, where transactions are final and non-reversible, even a moment of inattention can result in significant financial damage. 

Always verify the full wallet address — not just the first and last few characters.

I didn’t just work out during pregnancy, I trained with intention.
Heavy lifts to stay strong.
Slow movements and hip openers to stay mobile and connected.

The mix of strength & mobility was on purpose.
I was preparing for labor and when it came, my body was ready.
Quick. Unmedicated. No tears. Empowering.

That said, this was my approach.
I had been training consistently before pregnancy, and I always listened to my body every step of the way.
What worked for me might look different for you and that’s okay. Prepare for the birthing experience you hope for.
✨ Be intentional.
✨ Respect your body.
✨ Train for the season you’re in.

The fourth morning in a row I've woken at 5am to the unmistakable combo of glossy black cockatoo screeches and the sound of cones dropping on our timber decking.

These birds are a listed threatened species and their population is still declining. The pressures they face include the felling of very old and tall trees (they need large hollows which take hundreds of years to form). There's also pretty fierce competition for these hollows between sulphur crested cockatoos, corellas, galahs and the introduced common myna. 

Glossy's are also very selective feeders and rely heavily on she-oaks like this one as their primary food source. She-oaks have a complex relationship with fire, and although many species are somewhat dependent on fire for regeneration, others are highly fire-sensitive and do not survive severe fires, something which is becoming increasingly common with climate change. It was well documented that there was a significant reduction in foraging habitat availability post the megafires of 2019-2020. 

These beautiful birds are very long-lived and they mate for life, only producing one chick every two years. This pair produced their chick last year 🥹 I'm utterly enamored by this species and I'm so grateful each morning that I get to see them. Given they seem to love the cones from this particular tree, if anybody in SEQ or FNE NSW would like some seeds to plant on your property, please DM me. 🫶🏼

Central Queensland, 12:30am, 12/5/24. 
I got back from glider tracking late, curled up in bed and opened social media to see auroras firing all over the world. Georgia, Spain, Arizona, California, England and ... reportedly Mackay Australia?! What the fuck. 

I got myself out of bed and peered out of my donga to the southern skies. Couldn't see anything. It was nearly midnight, I looked at the aurora forecast and it was almost off the scale, "largest geomagnetic storm in 20 years" happening NOW. Uhmmmm... I don't think I could live with myself if I didn't "just go and see". 

So I drove up the road to a higher elevation and shot some snaps with MY PHONE! I never saw much of a reason to bring my astro lens to work... 😆 Ffs. Anyway, this is what my phone captured so forgive the average quality. It was not visible to the naked eye, but utterly remarkable that this phenomenon was recorded at this latitude. Not gonna lie the fomo of not being amongst it in Tassie or even Victorian latitudes was heavy, but I still feel pretty chuffed to have captured this from Central freaking Queensland! 🤯

Here are some things that might be normal to some people, make some scratch their heads, be totally unconventional to some, and still the obvious way to go to others. The more I grow into motherhood, the more friends I make, the more I realize that “normal” is relative 😂🤪 but these are things we’ve sort of settled on, make us feel empowered, and how we’ve decided so far to raise our kid(s). Subject to change of course, always!

• Nutritionally dense meals — 90-95% of the time we eat homemade with whole ingredients, no sugar, no dyes, no processed foods. That other small percentage is reserved for social gatherings or a treat out of the house. For us that feels super balanced.
• Extended rear-facing in the car seat (at least until age 4)
• Daily time outside.
• No screens for Amos, at all. Maybe we’ll do a family movie night someday but for now, no screens. (We exposed him to screens once during a long nebulizer treatment and it was a disaster… more on that another time)
• Probiotic foods daily for me and Amos — usually sauerkraut or fermented dairy.
• Reading to Amos daily, whether that’s one book or five… my goal is to read everyday but it doesn’t always happen. 
• Love of Torah, HaShem, and Israel. Pretty straight forward.
• Quality time as a couple — daily connection, sometimes with Amos but preferably just us after his bedtime.
• Having friends who aren’t just like us (as long as they’re not antisemitic). More religious? Great. Totally secular? Great. Not Jewish? Great. More liberal? Great. More conservative? Great. As long as there’s mutual respect.
• Including Amos in daily chores — laundry, dishes, wiping messes. He is a part of our household and it empowers him to help out as a member of the team!
• No toy rotation — only age-appropriate toys in sight; others go into storage for the next child.

My Ashkenazi ancestors fled before the Holocaust. Those who didn’t were made martyrs.
I don’t know why G-d allows tragedies like the Shoa to happen. It’s one of life’s big unanswered questions:
Why did G-d harden Paroh’s heart?
Why did the Shoa happen?
Why did October 7th happen?

And so on.

What I do know is that we have a choice in how we respond to tragedy. I’m not separate from those who were lost. None of us are.

I find it particularly striking that Ashkenazim share the same 300 ancestors. We multiplied into millions… and we were nearly wiped out.

But our soul is eternal.

I don’t know why I belong to a family that survived pogroms. Why they got out of Europe faster than others. But I do know that by deepening my love for my fellow Jew, and by trying to make the world— even just my own little world— as good as I can, I hope to honor the memory of the 6 million we lost.

Never forget.
Never forgive.
Never again is now, every day.

If you asked me to use one word to describe her, it might be “strong.” Sometimes I see people longing for more representation in media, more strong women characters, more strong women politicians, more strong women generally. And that is true. We do need that.

But strength is useless in and of itself. Strength without patience, strength without convictions, strength without determination is far less remarkable. But Lena has all of these things, and of course it doesn’t make her perfect - but this is her birthday and not a day to be nuanced and careful about my portrayal.

And Lena, at the same time, isn’t only her strength - sometimes she is silly, sometimes she is the best person to go to for advice, and sometimes she is the person you need to have an argument with.

Here’s to another year of her existence! Love you, bestie.

His larger than life memory lives on in all the lives he touched.  It’s been two years and I still run into people who ask if he was my father and share a story about his impact on them.  He was one of a kind.  I still can’t believe he is gone but thankfully I see signs of him everywhere I go and I know he is always with me.  We carry on his legacy through our involvement with the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society.  This year our Wicked Strong Team raised $28k and another $12.5k in corporate sponsorships in honor of dad. Absolutely devastated to hear of the loss of this man, someone who made such a big impact on me as a young person.

When I was in high school I had the opportunity to spend several years in Richard’s Black Music Ensemble. He always made it so clear what the music was really about from day 1.

He put me on to everyone. Coleman Hawkins, Wardell gray, Jon Hendricks… literally everyone. Without him, my foundation would not have been set. He put me on my musical path, and even wrote my letter of recommendation to MSM lol.

When I showed up to his UW class as a high schooler with a tenor saxophone, he told me to put it away and come back with a clarinet. He even called Eddie Daniel’s in the middle of class to chew me out for not learning clarinet.

He was a hard ass because he could be, and wanted to always get the best out of his students, and never let them forget what the music was about.

The knowledge, stories and music history riddles this man shared with us were endless. 

I could go on forever about his impact on me and so many countless others. 

I wish I could play him Coleman Hawkins solo from body and soul one more time. Back in the day he always told me it wasn’t quite right, “listen to it again”. Lol

He was an absolute GIANT of this music. 

I am forever blessed to have spent time learning this music from him. The true source.

Rest in absolute power Guru Ji 🙏🏽

The reason why many people can't grow their Rear Delts is because their lats are taking over most of the movement. They typically lift too heavy, so the lats need to overcome the load. They usually lift too fast (due to the heavy load), which takes away RD recruitment. 
Slow down, reduce the load a 🤏🏽 and focus on the end range squeeze.
Work to Real Reps In Reserve and not to numbers.
Focus on the tissue, not the ego.

Tämä on esimerkki, jonka annan usein ja johon myös törmää usein.

Tiedäätkö sen tunteen asiakkaan kanssa kun tuntuu, että pitäisi tehdä ENEMMÄN ja PAREMMIN, antaa neuvoja tai jotain ”kättä pitempää”. Olo on riittämätön. Asiakas saattaa osoittaa tyytymättömyyttään tai sit tää on enemmän tunnelma, joka ei tule sanoitetuksi.

Tottakai voi olla kyse siitä että teidän yhteistyössä on tullut kupruja tai ettet ole saanut ihan kiinni siitä mitä asiakas toivoo tai mikä häntä auttaisi.

Joskus tuo riittämättömyys on kuitenkin vastatunne, joka kumpuaa siitä että asiakas ei mentalisoi ja on esimentaalisessa teleologisessa moodissa. Tuossa moodissa ”vain teot ratkaisee” ja mielen tiloille pitää pääsääntöisesti pyrkiä tekemään jotain. Asiat pitää ratkaista. Se että kuulosteltaisiin omia ajatuksia ja tunteita ja siedettäisiin ne, on teleologiselle moodille ihan hepreaa. Ja kaikkihan me joskus päädytään tohon tilaan, esim. kun tuntuu siltä ettei paskaa fiilistä paranna mikään muu kuin tekeminen, vaikkapa hikilenkki tai siivoaminen tai tunnesyöminen.

Tämänkaltainen keskustelu asiakkaan kanssa (tässä tietysti typistettynä versiona):

Asiakas: ”Kuormittaakohan minun asiat sinua ja miten ylipäätään jaksat tätä työtä?”

Minä (hämmästyneenä asiakkaan huolesta): ”Itse asiassa mä pidän työstäni enkä koe että kuormittaisit minua” 🧡

Läsnä oli siis klassinen transferenssi eli se, että asiakas kokee minun kanssa jotain samaa mitä muissa ihmissuhteissaan. Että muut ei jaksa häntä tai hänen täytyy suojella muita ja olla vahva. Transferenssit ei siis vaadi sitä, että kyseessä on pitkä terapia vaan erilaiset olettamukset vuorovaikutuksesta herää jo lyhyissä kontakteissa, usein jo ensitapaamisella.

Mutta miksi tuo keskustelu oli päivän ellei viikon paras juttu?

Siksi, että pystyin sanomaan 100% rehellisesti ja sydämestä, että pidän työstäni enkä koe olevani asiakastyöstä erityisen kuormittunut.

Voi kuulostaa itsestäänselvyydeltä mutta sitä se ei todellakaan ole esimerkiksi kuormittuneena, ei ole ollut omallakaan kohdallani. Omakin polku on sisältänyt kaikenlaisia vaiheita ja lyhytkestoisen uupumuksenkin. Olen tuntenut riittämättömyyttä, liiallista vastuuta työstäni, sitä kuinka vastaanottojen jälkeen on ihan uupunut tai ylivireä, sitä etten osaa auttaa jne… Ja välillä tunnen noita inhimillisiä tuntemuksia edelleen eikä tässäkään asiassa tarvitse tulla valmiiksi.

Esimerkki: kaveri vastaa viestiin viiveellä ja hypementalisoiva oletus on, että syy on jokin vanha väärinymmärrys välillämme eikä hän oikeasti edes tahdo olla tekemisissä kanssani. 

Super yleinen hypermentalisoinnin merkki onkin tulkinnat hylätyksi tulosta.

Millainen on mentalisoiva auttaja? 

Aloitetaan sillä, mitä ei kannata tehdä.

😰 Älä yritä tehdä hienoja ja syvällisiä tulkintoja asiakkaasta
😰 Älä tarjoa monimutkaisia interventioita tai harjoitteita
😰 Älä mene mukaan pretend modeen, jossa vuorovaikutus on näennäisen toimivaa mutta jää pinnalliseksi ja ei-aidoksi (muista että terapian tavoite on kyky kärsiä❗️)
😰 Älä oleta, että tiedät mitä asiakkaan mielessä liikkuu
😰 Älä esitä näkökulmiasi totuutena
😰 Älä keskity vain siihen MITÄ puhutaan vaan myös siihen MITEN puhutaan, teidän välillä, tässä ja nyt
😰 Älä tee oletuksia asiakkaasta tai käytä transferenssi-näkökulmaa siten, että oletat asiakkaan käytöksen johtuvan vain jostain menneisyyden tapahtumasta ja sillä siisti (ilman että sinulla vuorovaikutuskumppanina olisi vaikutusta asiaan)
😰 Älä ole hiljaa pitkiä aikoja
😰 Älä reagoi tai vastaa asiakkaalle jostain omasta intensiivisestä tunnetilasta käsin, vaikka tunteet on siis auttajallekin täysin sallittuja (ne täytyy vaan tuoda ilmi säädellyssä muodossa, kuten vanhempi tuo parhaimmillaan lapselle)

Nämä vinkit perustuu mentalisaatioterapian brittiläisten kehittäjien teksteihin, jotka on siinä mielessä hauskoja että he uskaltavat antaa tällaisia konkreetteja ”do’s and dont’s” -listoja 👌🏼 Myös huumori on tärkeä osa mentalisoivaa terapiaa ja asennetta.

Psykoanalyyttisen teoreetikon Wilfred Bionin mukaan psykoterapian tavoite on asiakkaan kyky kärsiä. 

Kuulostaako oudolta tai pessimistiseltä? 

Kyvyn kärsiä voi ajatella kuitenkin myös:
🩵 kykynä olla yhteydessä omiin aitoihin tunteisiin ja sietää ne 
🩵 kykynä surra se, mitä on menettänyt tai ei koskaan saanut (esim. turvallinen lapsuus)
🩵 kykynä kokea tervettä vihaa sitä kohtaan, mikä ei ole ollut oikein tai reilua
🩵 kykynä tunnistaa myös se, mistä itse olemme vastuussa
🩵 kykynä olla haavoittuvainen

Ilman kykyä kärsiä olemme jumissa erilaisten oireiden kuten ahdistuneisuuden kanssa. Toimimme itselle haitalliseen tapaan kuten suoritamme tai ohitamme omat aidot tunteet ja tarpeet. Samalla saatamme pitää muut tunnetasolla ja psyykkisesti ikään kuin ”käden mitan päässä” (ja olemme ehkä vältteleviä). 

Mentalisaation näkökulmasta olemme ehkä ei-mentalisoivassa moodissa nimeltä pretend mode, joka voi tuntua siltä, että elää omassa ei-aidossa kuplassa jossa ei ole mitään tuntemisen arvoista, syytä surulle tai vihalle saatika tarkemmalle tutkimiselle. Pretend mode kieltää kärsimyksen ja omat kohtaamattomat tarpeet: ”what’s done is done”, ”menneitä ei voi muuttaa joten miksi niitä miettisi” tai ”mitä hyötyä on surkuttelusta”. 

Kyvyn kärsiä sivutuotteena on kuitenkin erilaiset sävyt kärsimyksen rinnalle kuten toiveikkuus, rauhallisempi sisäinen olo ja myötätunto. Kokonaan kärsimys ei kuitenkaan koskaan poistu koska se on osa aitoa elämää.

Transferenssia voi ajatella myös ”väärinä tunteita väärässä paikassa, vääriin henkilöihin kohdistettuina” (Muurinen, 2011).

Elikkä suomeksi ➡️ Auttamissuhteeseen tulee aina mukana myös menneisyys (sekä asiakkaan että auttajan). Yleisimmin transferenssilla kuitenkin tarkoitetaan sitä, että asiakas saattaa odottaa/nähdä/kuulla/kokea auttajassaan ja heidän välisessä suhteessaan jotain, joka on tuttua hänen menneisyytensä ihmissuhteista, eikä niinkään ajankohtaisesta auttamissuhteesta (tämä ei tarkoita etteikö auttajallakin olisi oma roolinsa siinä millaiseksi suhde muodostuu). Varsin usein nämä olettamukset ovat kielteisiä.

Mikäli näitä ilmiöitä ei oteta puheeksi on vaarana yllä olevassa sitaatissa kuvattu itseään toistava näytelmä, josta klassinen esimerkki on vaikkapa asiakas joka pettyy auttajiinsa toistuvasti ja pahimmillaan siirtyy ammattilaiselta toiselle kykenemättä luomaan syvempää suhdetta. 

Puheeksi ottaminen ja ylipäätään transferenssin huomaaminen on tietysti auttajan vastuulla. Moderni näkökulma on se, että itse asiassa transferenssista voi olla myös suurta hyötyä, kaikkine riskeineen. Transferenssia puretaan korjaavilla kokemuksilla, eli sillä, että auttaja toimiikin parhaansa mukaan toisin kuin asiakkaan menneisyyden näytelmä olettaa.

‼️ Ps. mitä näihin epämentalisoivien moodien nimiin tulee niin mentalisaatioterapian yksi kehittäjä Anthony Batemankin totesi niiden olevan ”shitty names” 🫠 Bateman kutsuu pretend modea ”bubbleksi” koska tässä moodissa ihminen saattaa elää kuin omassa kuplassaan, yksin ‼️

Pretend mode ei kuitenkaan siis todellakaan ole tietoista teeskentelyä vaan se on eräänlainen automaattinen tapa olla (ja selviytyä). Usein pretend modessa on kyse siitä, että ihminen katkaisee yhteyden omiin aitoihin kokemuksiin, tunteisiin ja tarpeisiin. Tällöin voi tuntua ettei tunne itseään, on hukannut itsensä tai valehtelee itselleen.

Arkinen esimerkki on se, että sinusta saattaa tuntua ettei asiat omassa elämässä ole ihan niin kuin pitäisi mutta hoet itsellesi kaiken olevan hyvin tai sinulla on jopa eräänlainen ”hällä väliä” olotila jossa mikään ei oikein tunnu miltään. Toisaalta taas saatat ”pakottaa” itsesi positiiviseksi ja reippaaksi tukahduttaen samalla muita aitoja kokemuksiasi (tämä on tosi tavallista).

Usein tämä näkyy myös vuorovaikutuksessa siten, että aidot kokemuksesi eivät välity muille ja olo voi olla eristynyt, ulkopuolinen, ei-ymmärretty. Pretend mode on tuttu pärjääjätyypeille jotka piilottavat oman haavoittuvuutensa sen taa ja samalla jäävät kokemustasolla yksin. 

Vakavampi esimerkki on dissosiaatio, joka on olotilana sellainen että tunteet on eristetty omasta tietoisuudesta täysin. 

Onko sulla kokemuksia tästä kuplasta? Jää seuraamaan jos mentalisaatio eli mielen supervoima kiinnostaa.

Miten sitten palautua mentalisoivaan tilaan eli saada se järki takaisin tunteiden rinnalle?

Tarkoitus ei ole tukahduttaa tunteita vaan saada järki ja tunteet taas parempaan tasapainoon. Parhaiten tämä lähtee liikenteseen tunnistamalla, milloin mieli on epämentalisoivassa tilassa/psyykkisen ekvivalenssin vallassa. Jo tämä huomaaminen tuo kokemukseemme väljyyttä. Kyseenalaista omaa mieltäsi lempeästi, pysähdy sen äärelle. Voit kokeilla laukkaavan mielen rauhoittamiseen myös fyysiseen olotilaan vaikuttamista: istu alas, hengitä hetki, tunne alusta allasi, laske hartiat. Tästä se lähtee liikenteeseen. Pitkässä juoksussa sisäinen turva vähentää psyykkistä ekvivalenssia tai ainakin kykyä palata takaisin mentalisoivaan tilaan.

Häpeän tunne taas yrittää saada meidät vetäytymään edelleen lisää, joten kierre on valmis.

Auttajan ei tarvitse olla malli jostakin, joksi asiakkaan tulisi tulla tai muuttua.

Sen sijaan meidän tehtävä on edes auttaa sellaisen tilan syntymistä, jossa asiakas voi löytää ITSE ITSENSÄ: 

”Tavallinen uutta kehitysobjektia koskeva väärinymmärrys on se, että on kyse psykoterapeutin/auttajan itsensä tarjoamisesta, ikään kuin mallina, jonka mukaan potilas/asiakas alkaisi sitten muovautua. Suomeksi sanottuna auttajan ei tarvitse olla itse mikään malliesimerkki tai kansankynttilä. Pelkkä ihminen riittää. Auttamistyössä on tärkeä pyrkiä luomaan sellaiset olosuhteet että asiakas voi löytää itse itsensä ja voimavaransa.

Graindin, innostuksen jne ja suorittamisen raja on myös hyvin häilyvä. Huomaatko sinä innostuksesi taakse vilkaistuasi myös muuta kuin tekemisen iloa, ehkä jonkinlaista painetta tai vaikeutta höllätä? Tää on tavallista etenkin niin sanotuilla pärjääjä-tyypeillä.

Why Do We Need Collagen?
Collagen is basically the structure that holds the entire body together. As you know, it is found in the skin, but also in the bones, muscles, tendons, and connective tissues such as joint cartilage. 
Collagen is very important for the regrowth and replacement of skin cells, because it forms the network within the dermis to which these new cells can attach. When this network starts to sag due to declining collagen production, lines and wrinkles are the obvious and direct result.
 At the age of 20, our skin begins producing 1% less collagen every year. The cumulative depletion of this essential protein as we age can be seen and felt from the inside out.

Most people with bipolar disorder spend years being treated for depression first. Here's what that costs.

At Regions, we see this every week.

Someone comes in after years of trying antidepressants that never quite worked. They've been told they have depression. They've done the work — therapy, medication, lifestyle changes. But the cycles keep coming. The highs that feel like productivity. The crashes that take out weeks at a time. The relationships they can't explain to themselves, let alone their family.

What they haven't been told: according to the Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance, only 1 in 4 people with bipolar disorder gets an accurate diagnosis within the first 3 years. Most spend nearly a decade being treated for the wrong condition.

That's not a personal failure. That's a diagnostic gap — and it has a staggering career cost. Research published in the American Journal of Managed Care found that bipolar disorder accounts for 65.5 lost workdays per year — more than double the 27.2 days lost to unipolar depression. The wrong treatment can't fix it.

When the right diagnosis finally arrives, DBSA research shows 89% of people see meaningful improvement in quality of life. The difference isn't willpower. It's the right evaluation.

That's what we offer at Regions Behavioral Health in Baton Rouge. Inpatient psychiatric care designed around getting it right — with a clinical team equipped to evaluate mood disorders accurately and compassionately. 75% of our patients choose to come. Because they've finally found somewhere that takes the full picture seriously.

If the treatment you've tried hasn't worked, it may not be you. It may be the diagnosis.

Most high-functioning adults who notice they're not as sharp as they used to be assume it's burnout. Or getting older. Or just having too much on their plate.

That's not a metaphor. That's a measurable biological change happening to people who think they're just stressed.
The good news is equally concrete: research published in Frontiers in Psychiatry found that treatment reverses the damage — about 1 in 3 people with depression-related cognitive impairment see full cognitive recovery after structured treatment.
At Regions, 75% of our inpatient admissions are voluntary — compared to roughly 10% industry-wide. Our patients walk in because they decided to. That decision — that one moment of choosing differently — is what separates "functioning at 70%" from getting back to who you actually are.

"I'm keeping it together for my family." But the research says they're already absorbing it.

Most people who are delaying mental health treatment have a reason that feels selfless.

"I can't step away from work right now." "My family needs me present." "I'll handle it after things settle down."

But here's what the research actually shows: untreated mental illness doesn't stay inside you. It radiates outward.

Spouses of adults with untreated mental illness develop anxiety and depression at 2–3 times the rate of the general population. Not because they're weak — because sustained exposure to a partner's unmanaged symptoms takes a documented clinical toll.

And it's not just your family. People with severe untreated mental illness die 10–20 years earlier than average, mostly from physical conditions — heart disease, diabetes, respiratory illness — that go unmanaged because the mental illness was never treated.

The cost of waiting isn't abstract. It's measured in years and in the people around you.

The good news: 80% of people who receive treatment for depression improve significantly. The barrier isn't the treatment — it's getting there. And for most people, cost is the last wall: more than half of adults who need psychiatric care but don't get it say they can't afford it.

At Regions, we have counselors on staff. We accept most major insurance. We work with people to figure this out before they ever walk through the door.

“The largest network on Earth is made by fungi.

Scientists have now mapped Earth's underground fungal network and discovered it contains an estimated 68 quadrillion miles (110 quadrillion km) of microscopic threads known as hyphae.

If all of its microscopic threads were stretched into a single line, they would extend roughly 12,000 light-years through space.

That's enough to span a significant portion of the Milky Way galaxy.

The study focused on arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, organisms that form vast underground partnerships with plants.

These fungi form partnerships with about 70 percent of plant species on Earth. They help plants absorb water and nutrients while receiving carbon produced through photosynthesis in return.

Scientists often describe them as part of Earth's underground circulatory system.
Every year, these fungal networks move an estimated 4 billion tons of carbon dioxide into soils, equivalent to about 11 percent of annual human-related carbon dioxide emissions.

The researchers estimate the global network contains roughly 300 megatons of carbon, about four to six times the biomass of all humans on Earth.

The study also found that grasslands contain around 40 percent of the world's fungal infrastructure, with especially dense networks predicted in places such as the Florida Everglades, South Sudan's flooded grasslands, and the Tibetan Plateau.

One surprising statistic highlights just how concentrated these networks can be: a single teaspoon of healthy soil may contain up to 32 feet (10 meters) of fungal threads.

To create the first global map of this hidden infrastructure, scientists analyzed more than 16,000 soil samples and used machine learning to estimate fungal densities across nearly every square mile of Earth's land surface.”

“Cannabis is no longer classified in the same category as heroin.

After more than half a century, the federal government has reclassified state-licensed medical marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, removing it from the same category as heroin and LSD.

It's one of the biggest changes to U.S. cannabis policy in decades.

Since 1970, marijuana has been classified as a Schedule I substance, a category reserved for drugs considered to have a high potential for abuse and no accepted medical use.

That classification increasingly clashed with reality.

Today, 40 states operate medical marijuana programs, and millions of Americans legally use cannabis products under state law. Researchers, doctors, and lawmakers have long argued that treating marijuana the same way as heroin no longer reflected the available evidence.

The new classification doesn't make marijuana federally legal. Recreational cannabis remains illegal under federal law, and interstate cannabis sales are still prohibited.

But the change has major practical consequences.

State-licensed medical marijuana businesses will face fewer restrictions and gain access to significant federal tax relief. Researchers will also encounter fewer barriers when studying cannabis, potentially leading to better evidence about both its benefits and risks.

Scientists are still working to answer many important questions about marijuana. Studies have suggested cannabis may help with chronic pain, chemotherapy-induced nausea, and appetite loss associated with certain illnesses. Other research has raised concerns about heavy use, addiction risk, impaired driving, and potential effects on developing brains.

Supporters call the move a long-overdue correction. Critics argue it could send the wrong message about the risks associated with marijuana use.”

✨ Turning a haircut into a mini art studio 🎨✂️

As a mama with a little bit of a perfectionist streak in me, I started the haircut high hopes of having it done perfectly.

But my little explorer had other ideas. He wiggled, shouted “No!”, and turned the dining table into his own art canvas.

Things shifted when we handed him his favorite markers. Suddenly, the haircut became a play time with his markers.

He drew lines and circles, laughed, and had fun. It turned a stressful moment into shared joy.

What I learned:
💫 Mess is magic — A little chaos can unlock the biggest smiles.
💫 Give them agency — When kids co-create, they engage with more joy and less resistance.
💫 Celebrate the process — Messy is the default mode. Joy is the choice in the middle of it.
💫 Reward after — It’s not about the flawless haircut. It’s about showing up even through perfectionism & anxiety.

So next time you’re in a wiggle-war, grab the markers, splash some water, and let the bubbles fly.

The mess fades, but the laughter stays. 💛

From day one God gave me an assignment and with tears in my eyes (yes I’m a crybaby😭) I was chin up and chest out. Being diagnosed with level 1 Autisum at the age of two with so much uncertainty I knew giving up was NEVER an option. Kicked out of 4 schools cause they couldn’t “help him” to being guided right where his journey would start my baby boy has excelled soooo much. Today it’s not only about accomplishing  how to sit in circle time with peers. 
From learning how to talk (junk😭 little slick mouth” motor skills , aba Theraphy , speech Theraphy and more Zayden has hit every task that was set out for him. He’s now on his way to public school entering Kindergarten and I’m super proud of him.
He’s so smart , demanding and with a personality that’s so funny I can’t be more grateful then to be able to be his mommy or “Pooh Pooh head” 🙄. It was a time when he never said mommy or even communicated effectively ; now I wanna change my name cause he won’t stop saying it and he talk soooo much I have to tell him let’s play the “quiet game” 😭😭😭I know God will continue to guide his steps and help me lead him along his way. Ase’ 💫 Autisum STOPS nothing! Always loving him out loud 🤩This is not the beginning and it’s definitely not the ending this is just one more chapter in his life that he can look back on and be proud of himself 🥹 forever grateful for our village. 🫂

 love mommy 💕

Let’s talk about the Jacoya Morgan story being shared online.

First, prayers to her family. 🕊️

This is not gossip. This is grief. This is workforce care. This is a systems conversation.

According to reports circulating online, #JacoyaMorgan worked a 12-hour shift at Birmingham Children’s Hospital and told leadership she felt sick. She was allegedly denied the ability to go home. After that, she reportedly collapsed and suffered a medical emergency. There are also allegations that CPR was not immediately provided.

If true, this should disturb every healthcare worker, every hospital leader, and every person who has ever been told to “push through” when their body was clearly warning them.

As a nurse, I keep coming back to one word:

Assessment.

When a healthcare worker says, “I don’t feel well,” the response should not be pressure, guilt, staffing panic, or punishment.

The response should be assessment, documentation, care, and safety.

One thing I teach Black career women and healthcare workers is this:

Stop asking permission to protect your body.

You are not begging.
You are not being difficult.
You are not abandoning anyone.

You are putting leadership on notice that you are unable to safely continue.

The language matters:

“I am sick and unable to safely continue working. I am notifying you that I need medical assessment and/or need to leave. Please document that I informed leadership.”

That is a mindset shift.

Because too many workers have been trained to override their bodies for jobs that may not protect them.

This is why Workforce Care™ exists.

We help Black career women and RNs recognize work fatigue before it becomes collapse, crisis, resignation, mislabeling, or long-term disability.

If your body has been warning you for more than six weeks, your next appointment matters.

A woman told her doctor:
“My children are upsetting me.”
She left with Paxil.
Four months later, the children were still doing the same thing.
But now her hair was falling out, she felt emotionally numb, and she was biting the side of her tongue.
As an RN, my first thought is this:
Was this woman even taking medication for the right reason?
Because from what she described, this sounds like a family-function problem that needed assessment, not an automatic psychiatric response.
My intervention would have started with:
• Parenting skills
• Standard setting
• A family meeting
• Boundaries
• Household structure
• Support
• A plan
Medication cannot parent the children.
Medication cannot set the standards.
Medication cannot hold the family meeting.
Medication cannot fix the environment that is still upsetting her every single day.
This is not an anti-medication conversation.
This is an informed-care conversation.
Before we medicate a woman’s response to her environment, we need to assess the environment she is trying to survive in.
Because sometimes the problem is not her brain.
Sometimes the problem is what keeps happening around her.
