It’s Multiple Awareness Week and this ain’t my first rodeo 😅🤠

As a mama of two sets of twins and a slightly crunchy twin mama trying to challenge the way we approach twin motherhood…

These are the hills I’d die on:

✌🏽Not all twins come early. I went over 41 weeks with both sets. All four arrived beautifully healthy and we didn’t need special care or NICU time. I don’t believe we should be cutting twins out early just because “twins come early” or “my doctor said.” Always ask why.

✌🏽And on that… you can birth twins vaginally and in water. Being told you’re “not allowed” to do something when it isn’t medically necessary doesn’t sit right with me. It’s your body and your babies. Assuming all is well, you can absolutely birth without an epidural, in water, vaginally.

✌🏽Twin babies are still babies, not robots. Syncing them into strict routines is wild to me. Two completely different little people with their own personalities, needs, sleep patterns, and feeding rhythms. Embrace rhythm over rigid routine. Learn your babies instead of trying to force them to be the same. 

✌🏽You don’t need two of everything. You don’t need double the stuff just because it’s twins. More things don’t always make it easier. Keep it simple and marketplace is your best friend.

✌🏽You can absolutely bed share and enjoy sleep in your first year of twins. I don’t get up once over night with my twins. Because we are all together feeding, co regulating, sleeping and rousing the way we are designed to. 

✌🏽You can breastfeed twins. You don’t have to formula feed “just to survive.” It’s not always easy, but it is absolutely possible. Support makes all the difference.

✌🏽You can love being a twin mum, adore your babies, and still long for easier days.Amongst the beauty there is chaos. Amongst the tears and overwhelm, there is the most incredible gift.Twins are the biggest blessing.

I won the lottery twice.

Top 5 tips for graduating nappies 🐨🚽

The OG twins are finally graduating out of nappies and honestly… toilet training twins felt incredibly daunting.

Every child is so different. My daughter practically toilet trained herself at 2, while the boys showed absolutely no signs of readiness at that age. So I left it and decided to tackle it over summer instead.

And truly, if you can time it for summer, do it! Less layers, more outside time, and easy nappy-free moments make it so much easier.

We always focus on daytime first, then nighttime usually follows a little later.

Here are my biggest toilet training tips:

1. Wait until they’re ready
Don’t force it. You don’t want stress, fear, or pressure around toileting. It becomes so much easier when they’re interested and involved. Every little bum is different, there’s no rush. My twins were months apart in readiness!

2. Put undies in the nappy drawer
Such a simple shift, but it helps create a new rhythm. Instead of automatically reaching for a nappy, offer “big kid” undies instead. It doesn’t take many accidents before they start becoming more aware of their body and cues.

3. Get a kids toilet seat
Toilets can feel huge and intimidating for little people. We skipped the potty and went straight to a toilet seat insert to avoid double training. The built-in magnetic kids seats from Bunnings are so good and made a huge difference to confidence. 

4. Waterproof sheets are essential
Night training can take a little longer and accidents are completely normal. Waterproof sheets make the whole process so much less stressful. I love @organicpeach_ and @spewyau 

5. A flexible nappy subscription helps so much
Toilet training is unpredictable. Some weeks you fly through nappies, other weeks barely any. Having a flexible subscription you can pause or stop anytime makes the whole transition feel much more seamless and less wasteful.

Feeding babies can be SO hard. It feels strange saying that at the 11 week mark with my second set of twins and another beautiful daughter who were all exclusively breastfed until well over two.

But just like each of our babies are different, we can be different each time too. Our bodies change. Sometimes that shows up in beautiful ways, and other times it can be incredibly challenging. This can play out in pregnancy, birth, and motherhood. 

I’m working through it with amazing support and love from the village. Another way the village shows up long after the six weeks are done. I don’t believe in ‘postpartum is forever’. Yes, you are forever changed when you become a mother, but you are not stuck in postpartum forever. That idea can feel overwhelming and unhelpful for mothers. Matrescence is the transition, the lifelong change that follows.

But six weeks isn’t enough.

Let’s talk about something slightly boring… but extremely important.

✨ Consent forms ✨

(And there is a code for you below)

I know. Not the coolest topic in tattooing 🙄
But tattooing involves skin, health information, legal responsibility… and as you know, and are often not happy about, content creation too. 😅

A proper consent form should clearly mention:
✔️ the tattoo procedure
✔️ medical information
✔️ aftercare responsibility
✔️ and ofc photos, videos, social media, promotional or educational use

‼️Because if you’re recording, photographing, or posting clients, that needs to be written and signed. No gray area zone here‼️

Beyond the legal aspect, consent forms do something bigger.
They make your space feel professional!
Clients feel safer when everything is clear. You, also, definitely feel safer when everything is documented.

Now, you guys know I don’t randomly talk about apps. I’m very picky about tools.

It’s a digital consent form system made for tattoo artists.
👉 You can send forms before the appointment, collect signatures online, store everything in one place, and they support multiple languages too (English, German, Turkish, Dutch, Spanish and French).

Let me know if you have further questions about your consent forms, and definitely check out @wavrr.app

Last year I set a goal to ride in miles my age on or around my bday (next week I will officially be 60!).

Next year I will do it again, and each year after until I can’t. 

My body is in deep pain right now but my heart soul and ego are turned up! 

Some ole man wisdom, don’t stop pushing!

🚒 Why 4-Person Engine Companies Matter

When an engine company is fully staffed with four firefighters, we can operate the way modern fireground tactics are designed — faster, safer, and more effective for the community we protect.

🔥 On Arrival:
	•One firefighter can immediately pump the truck and secure a water supply, ensuring continuous, reliable water.
	•The officer can complete a 360° size-up, identify hazards, and make a sound game plan.
	•The other two firefighters deploy the attack line without delay.

🏠 Inside the Structure:
With four on the engine, the crew can push inside as a coordinated team.
	•Three firefighters advance the hose together deep into a dark, smoke-filled structure.
	•The officer maintains supervision, accountability, and direction, using the thermal imaging camera (TIC) to guide the team toward fire and potential victims.

👨‍👩‍👧 For the Community:
Four-person staffing means:
	•Faster fire attack, slowing fire growth and reducing property loss
	•Quicker searches for trapped occupants
	•More controlled, safer operations, reducing the chance of fire spread to neighboring homes
	•Better outcomes for citizens who depend on us in their worst moments

✔️ Bottom Line:
Four-person engines don’t just make operations safer for firefighters — they make our entire community safer. This is the standard our citizens deserve.

Thank you to every department and firefighter who responded for mutual aid and backfill during the Greystone fire. Your support ensured our city stayed protected while our crews worked a difficult and unfortunate incident.

We want the Wilmington community and the owners of The Greystone to know that we truly feel for everyone impacted. The circumstances of this fire were not what any of us ever want to see in our city.

This incident also highlights the reality of our current staffing model. With a minimum of 3 firefighters on an apparatus, we often end up with only 2 advancing hose and 2–3 searching. Our crews give everything they have, but this setup slows down critical tasks that directly affect rescue and fire control.

Achieving the NFPA-recommended minimum of 4 firefighters per apparatus is essential. Proper staffing makes hose advancement more efficient, speeds up searches, and improves overall safety for both the community and our firefighters.

Local 129 will continue making this a top priority, working with elected officials and city administration to secure the staffing our city needs.

Thank you again to all who answered the call. 🚒🔥💛

MY SON ☀️

I don’t know where Liddle came from but I’m so glad he took shelter in my bushes. 
He was there when we moved in… this little cat with a stumpy tail and little legs. He was terrified of humans and would hiss if we went near him. 
I started to feed him and he began coming out of the bush and hanging out our door. For around a year and a half I made sure there was food and water for him and a bed outside. 
When we decided to move out, I knew I couldn’t just abandon him. He relied on me and trusted me. 
I brought him inside to get him ready to find his forever home. We found out he had FIV and even with the help of a rescue no one wanted him. He had bad skin, a bad attitude and required too much work and patience. 
That’s when I knew that he was mine. I loved him so much but with a baby and 2 cats already I thought I couldn’t possibly keep him! The universe showed me otherwise. 
Liddle was my biggest project, everyday I’d spend big chunks of time just gaining his trust and love. He was there everyday when my mum was sick in hospital and after she passed. Dedicating time to him helped ease my pain. He was always there for me. I will never forget that. So I will always be there for him ❤️❤️❤️🐱🐈

Mary Jane McLeod Bethune was one of the most important leaders in African American education, civil and women’s rights and government. 

The college she founded set educational standards for today’s black colleges, and her role as an advisor to President Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave African Americans an advocate in government. 

A champion of racial and gender equality, Bethune founded many organizations and led voter registration drives after women gained the vote in 1920.

In 1935, she became the founding president of the National Council of Negro Women.

My wife and I woke up at 5AM after a long flight from Atlanta and hours of driving from Edmonton. After witnessing the beauty of the Canadian Rockies as we entered Jasper National Park the night before, we decided that we didn't have time to waste and spent the next 9 days extracting as many experiences as we could out of the time we had there.

T minus 10 days until we hop on another plane and head back to Canada to revisit the same mountains we saw last September. 

My wife and I decided that for spring break this year, we'd return to the very same place we spent our honeymoon. Let me explain:

When we were there at the end of September, we spent 10 days driving from Edmonton to Jasper, through the icefields parkway to Banff and visiting every national park in between. We took advantage of every day, every moment, and extracted every ounce of energy we had. By the time we flew out of Calgary, we had clocked about 60 miles of hiking through some of the most astounding scenery I have ever witnessed. We were there for the end of the season, visiting many places just days before they started closing for the winter. This was the peak of wildlife activity for many species that we wanted to see, and it offered the most astounding pallet of colors.

This time, we decided to do it a little differently. We want to see as many of these places as nature will allow, but in their frozen glory. The rivers and waterfalls that were so full of life will be still. The mountain peaks will be soft and white. The blue and green lakes will be frozen and white. We'll hike some of the same trails, maybe even go dog sledding and snow tubing. 🤷‍♂️

We're looking forward to seeing what these mountains have to offer when winter is just starting to close, virtually the opposite of what we saw just months ago.

See you soon @parks.canada 🫡

Memento Mori.

This is a Latin phrase that translates to "remember, you must die." It is a symbolic reminder from Roman times that as all things once began, all things will end and death is an inevitable and inescapable part of life. The purpose of this phrase was not as a grim reminder of life's passing, but as a stoic reminder that like all beings, you are mortal and the acceptance of this reality is meant to bring clarity to life. The stoics would say that death gives life the ultimate meaning. 

It's a tool to create priority, meaning, and happiness. It's a tool that generations have used to create real perspective and urgency. To treat our time as a gift. To be grateful for every single moment and not waste it on the trivial and vain. Death doesn't make life pointless but rather purposeful.

When you wake up tomorrow, take a few moments to meditate on this, and carry it with you every day. Use it as a building block for truly living your life to the fullest rather than just "living" every passing day. 

"Let us prepare our minds as if we've come to the very end of life. Let us postpone nothing. Let us balance life's books each day. The one who puts the finishing touches on their life each day is never short of time."

-Seneca

Did a simple and silly one to commemorate this holiday season. Acrylic and paint pens.

Did this one a few weeks ago. I wanted to paint it using coffee but it ended up looking like shit so I went over it with oil pastels. I wasn't really pleased with how it turned out, but looking at it now I kind of like it.

I'm not exactly sure what this is supposed to represent. I do remember laying it out thinking "stop fighting and just let it happen." I sat in front of the canvas (it's not canvas 😂)for a few hours and nothing was happening. I thought back to when I was a kid and would write down a squiggly line and build off of it. The thought of what would the mind look like if you could see it and how would our thoughts appear crossed my mind. What would our social constructs look like? What would the mental trapping of our culture look like? Ultimately I just wanted to have fun and this is the result.

I originally intended to paint the gate of a wrought iron fence. I wanted it to symbolize something to the effect of "entering a new phase of life" or "leveling up". I had seen a completely different image in my mind and as always the painting decided to do something else entirely. During the process of painting I had the thought of "what you hate about me is what you hate about yourself" and similarly "what you like about me is what you like about yourself" running through my head - quite the "gem" of introspection. So, I think I'll call this one "I am just a mirror".

Feeding your baby to sleep doesn’t create a bad habit. It creates a fed, sleeping baby.

The ‘bad habit’ narrative comes from sleep training culture, where independent sleep is usually the goal and anything involving you is framed as a problem you need to fix.

But sleep associations are just the conditions present when your baby falls asleep. Feeding. Rocking. Contact. Darkness. White noise. They’re all associations (we all have them!) - and they’re neutral until they stop working for your family.

That’s the only test that matters. Not whether somebody else says it’s wrong. Whether it’s sustainable for YOU.

Babies who feed to sleep don’t stay that way forever. They will usually naturally transition as they develop, as overnight feeding needs drop, as they mature. You’re not locking them into a pattern for life. 

If feeding to sleep is working and you’re both getting rest, keep going. If it’s stopped working or you’re exhausted, or you just can’t do it anymore, we can change it gently without cutting off comfort or connection.

You can feed your baby to sleep AND work toward easier nights. Those two things can co-exist while you figure out what actually works for your baby.

Except nobody tells you what drowsy actually looks like.

Is it the heavy eyelids? The slowing movements? The yawn? The moment right before they pass out in your arms?

Because if you miss the window by 30 seconds and you’ve got a more sensitive baby, you’ve potentially hit overtired territory and all hell breaks loose (yep, been there!)

That’s not a failure on your part. That’s biology.

If you’ve ever been confused about tired cues, this will change your life ⤵️

Most parents are told to watch for “drowsy signs.”

But nobody explains what that actually looks like in practice.

Here’s what it looks like:

Your baby rubs their eyes. 
Then turns their head away from a toy.
Then starts yawning. Maybe fussing a little.

That’s the cluster.

Tired cues don’t come one at a time.
They come in a group.

Things like:
↓ Eye rubs or red eyebrows
↓ Looking away/disengaging
↓ Fussing
↓ Yawning
↓ Staring into space

The thing is, one cue on its own could be anything. 

Like, “my eye is itchy”, or “I’m bored of this”.

Multiple cues together?
That’s your window.

And here’s the test: if you offer a new activity and the cues disappear, they weren’t truly tired yet. They might have just wanted to do something new.

If the cues stay, that’s telling you it’s time for sleep.

The wake window chart can’t tell you when that cluster will appear.

Only your baby can!

If bedtime keeps dragging, it’s not always overtiredness.
Sometimes your baby just isn’t ready.
Sometimes they’re wound up from the day.
Sometimes the timing just slipped.

Start with one thing.
Did you see real tired signs?

Not one yawn.
A cluster of tired signs.
Yawning, rubbing eyes, looking away, maybe red eyebrows.
If that didn’t show up, their body may not have been ready for sleep.

Undertired can look peaceful.
Rolling. Babbling. Kicking around happy.

It can also look messy.
Crying because they weren’t done.
Sometimes they’re just bored. Those signs look a lot like tired signs.

People call that overtired. It’s usually not.

Dysregulated feels different.
You can see the upset.
They’re hard to settle.
Everything escalates.
That often shows up after long wake windows, hectic days, or big feelings that never got cleared.

Here’s the part that makes bedtime finally make sense.

Calm with no tired signs: add ten to fifteen minutes extra before bedtime tomorrow.

Upset with no tired signs: slow the lead up. More connection. They may still need extra wake time.

Clear tired signs plus dysregulation: shorten the last stretch or bring bedtime forward next time.

Watch the pattern.
That’s what tells the truth.

When you read cues and timing together, bedtime stops feeling like a mystery.
You know what move to make.

• understanding what’s normal for your baby’s age and stage
• supporting regulation before bedtime

Time for the new tattoo 🐞 What do you have in mind? Tell me!

We went from Pinterest to AI, and let’s please drop both. 

I used to receive plenty of tattoo requests with people looking for references going through the artwork by other tattooers. Now more and more people start using AI to pre-design their idea to show me what they mean. 

And I get it. For people who don’t work with visuals, it seems impossible to explain what you have in mind, and you feel like you need help to sort out your messy thoughts and fluff it all up before you share it with me, your tattoo artist.

But you are not helping. First of all, your raw ideas and inner mess is key for me: it can lead to an unexpected decisions and twists, I might notice something the chat gpt would miss, and I will get ahold of it, and we will build something even more interesting together. 

You think you can’t explain it but you can, and I, a human, will understand you better than any machine ever will. 

You might be worried that you are wasting my time, and through fixing the design with ai you are making shortcuts, but working with you on the design is a huge and a very important part of my job. I love it. I love creating for you, with you. I love making alterations and always leave room for some changes. 

The most dangerous part though is: you ask AI to draw a pre sketch just to explain your idea. But then. Without understanding it. You get attached to it. And all the changes you later ask me to make in my design are your subconscious attempts to get my design closer to what AI built for you. Not because you like it more. Because it feels familiar now. 

Please, please don’t do it. Leave the artistic part to your artist. If you like my art, trust me. Use my older artwork as a reference. Send me pictures of the alive creatures or objects you mean (that old grandma’s chair, your silly goofy dog). Let me do my job. Let’s put some time and communication into it. I will not disappoint.
I am in love, let’s meet there ❤️
I am patiently waiting for your message 😏

I identify as a woman, despite struggling with this concept all my life. I didn’t like my shapes and curves, my breasts, since quite early age I was mocked for having “udders,” then for having hair on my legs. I had extremely painful cramps, but I was shamed by my (female) school gym teacher for being weak, so I had to suck it up. I was scared that someone would hear my pad make a noise, god forbid see me leak through. I was so ashamed of how I was. So I was trying to fit in. I did all of it: make up, nails, I shaved everything I could, I was trying so hard to find a way to look like a real woman. 

Only years and years later I found out that actually being a real woman doesn’t require you to be anything other than what you want to be. 

You can be classy and chic, wearing heals and red lipstick even when going to a grocery shop. You might as well shave your head before an important event and wear snickers and no bra under an oversized hoodie. You can be both. 

You can run like a girl: fast and strong. You can run like a girl: slow and steady. You can also just not run - equally like a girl. 

You can be tiny, you can be big, you can be soft, you can be stronger than any gym bro you know. 

You can work or not, have kids or not, get married to whom you want, or not. 

I am lucky to have amazing strong smart gorgeous women around me whom I call friends. Running world known media, designing clothes that is being worn all over the globe, operating tattoo shops that host thousands of people who feel safe there, raising kids, working in healthcare and IT. There are women who support me, there are women who inspire me, there are women who are my role models. 

Here’s to all of you. All of us. If you, as well as myself, identify as a woman: I see you. I am here for you. Here’s to the sisterhood. To the girl power. To the world that we are building. Where all people are enough as they are, where all people are safe, all have equal respect and equal rights.

Hunger shouldn’t be penalized. 
 In 2017, All for Lunch founder Alessandra Ferrara-Miller heard a story on the news detailing an incident of the school lunch shaming of a young boy at an elementary school. With a 5-year-old daughter in kindergarten at the time, the reality of a child that young being denied lunch at school for financial reasons so far out of their control broke her heart and she knew something had to be done to help. 

Through her research, she found that lunch debt was a nationwide problem affecting kids in kindergarten through high school which came along with various forms of lunch shaming. From kids being sent home with stamps on their arms saying “I need lunch money,” to children doing custodial work in the cafeteria to pay for the cost of the meal, to having their lunch taken away in front of their classmates, and on and on children as young as 5 were experiencing these challenges daily as a result of financial circumstances completely out of their control.
